CODE OF CONDUCT – COMPLIANCE – EXPORT CONTROL", "html": "<p><strong>21.1<\/strong><strong>1<\/strong><strong>.1. <\/strong><strong>Stellantis<\/strong><strong>’ Code of Conduct<\/strong><strong> <\/strong><\/p><p>Both Parties acknowledge that they have adopted own codes of conduct, available on the respective internet websites, and comprehensive compliance programs. <\/p><p>Compliance programs include guidelines, periodic trainings, awareness and advice all aimed at ensuring compliance with their own ethical principles and with all applicable laws and regulations, including, but not limited: anti-money laundering, export and trade regulations, competition, insider trading, anti-corruption, data privacy and protection laws. For information, Stellantis Code of Conduct is available at the following web address:  <\/p><p>https://www.stellantis.com/en/group/governance/code-of-conduct. <\/p><p>The Parties agree to comply with such provisions and principles and are aware that the infringement of the above-mentioned provisions and principles shall represent a material breach of the present Agreement. <\/p><p><strong>21.1<\/strong><strong>1<\/strong><strong>.2 Compliance on Anti-Corruption, Sanctions, Export Control Laws and CSR Obligations<\/strong><strong> <\/strong><\/p><p>(i) Supplier, its directors, officers and employees shall engage neither in any act that would represent a Corrupt Act not at any time, engage in any activity, practice or conduct that would constitute an offence under the Anti-Corruption Laws.  <\/p><p>(ii) Supplier has and shall maintain an internal prevention system in place to ensure compliance with Anti-Corruption Laws and the prevention of Corrupt Acts. <\/p><p>(iii) Supplier agrees to comply with all Export Control Laws. Supplier will not violate, and will not cause Customer to violate, any Export Control Laws (e.g. by transshipping goods through, or supplying Services from sanctioned countries). In order to comply with these Export Control Laws, Customer requires Supplier to provide the appropriate Export Control Classification Number (ECCN), or other country’s export classification for any Services included in this Agreement. Furthermore, Supplier undertakes to inform Customer of the exact US content in [%] of value, in accordance with U.S. Export Administration Regulation (EAR) of its deliverables before delivery, if applicable. Should the U.S. content of the Services change after the delivery date and during the Term of this Agreement, Supplier is obliged to inform Customer immediately of U.S. content change. Licenses or other authorizations required for the export of Services will be the responsibility of Supplier unless otherwise agreed by Customer and Supplier, in which event Supplier shall provide all necessary information as may be requested by Customer in order to obtain such licenses or authorizations. This includes, but is not limited to, the prohibition on the transfer of commodities, materials, software and technology (i.e., all Items) subject to this Agreement to, transit through, or procurement from, European Union /United States sanctioned countries and regions unless such transactions are permissible under applicable European Union /United States laws and regulations. <\/p><p>(iv) Supplier shall make and keep books, records and account which, in reasonable detail, accurately and fairly reflect the transactions and dispositions of its funds and assets, and shall maintain a system of internal accounting controls intended to ensure compliance with Anti-Corruption Laws and sufficient to provide reasonable assurance that (i) transactions are executed and access to assets is permitted only in accordance with Supplier’s applicable policies and procedures and management’s general or specifications authorization; and (ii) transactions are recorded as necessary to permit preparation of periodic financial statements and to maintain accountability for assets.  <\/p><p>(v)Supplier shall comply, and to require its subcontractors or any person under its control to comply with the CSR Rules.  <\/p><p>(vi)Supplier undertakes that neither it or nor any of its subcontractors, vendors, agents, or other associated third parties shall utilize child, slave, prisoner or any other form of forced or involuntary labor, or engage in abusive employment or corrupt business practices in the supply of Services.  <\/p><p>Supplier and its directors, officers, employees shall: <\/p><p>Comply in all respects with all Sanctions and;  <\/p><p>Not carry on any trade, business or other activities with or for the benefit of any Sanctioned Person or which, in any other manner, could result in Supplier or its directors or Customer being in breach of any Sanctions or being designated, being subject to any penalties or restrictive measure being imposed pursuant to Sanctions or being designated as a Sanctioned Person.  <\/p><p>(vii)    Supplier shall promptly notify Customer if it becomes aware of any non-compliance with this clause and any non-compliance with Sanctions and Customer reserves the right to require Supplier to immediately take appropriate remedial actions. <\/p>", "text": "21.11.1. Stellantis’ Code of Conduct \nBoth Parties acknowledge that they have adopted own codes of conduct, available on the respective internet websites, and comprehensive compliance programs. \nCompliance programs include guidelines, periodic trainings, awareness and advice all aimed at ensuring compliance with their own ethical principles and with all applicable laws and regulations, including, but not limited: anti-money laundering, export and trade regulations, competition, insider trading, anti-corruption, data privacy and protection laws. For information, Stellantis Code of Conduct is available at the following web address:  \nhttps://www.stellantis.com/en/group/governance/code-of-conduct. \nThe Parties agree to comply with such provisions and principles and are aware that the infringement of the above-mentioned provisions and principles shall represent a material breach of the present Agreement. \n21.11.2 Compliance on Anti-Corruption, Sanctions, Export Control Laws and CSR Obligations \n(i) Supplier, its directors, officers and employees shall engage neither in any act that would represent a Corrupt Act not at any time, engage in any activity, practice or conduct that would constitute an offence under the Anti-Corruption Laws.  \n(ii) Supplier has and shall maintain an internal prevention system in place to ensure compliance with Anti-Corruption Laws and the prevention of Corrupt Acts. \n(iii) Supplier agrees to comply with all Export Control Laws. Supplier will not violate, and will not cause Customer to violate, any Export Control Laws (e.g. by transshipping goods through, or supplying Services from sanctioned countries). In order to comply with these Export Control Laws, Customer requires Supplier to provide the appropriate Export Control Classification Number (ECCN), or other country’s export classification for any Services included in this Agreement. Furthermore, Supplier undertakes to inform Customer of the exact US content in [%] of value, in accordance with U.S. Export Administration Regulation (EAR) of its deliverables before delivery, if applicable. Should the U.S. content of the Services change after the delivery date and during the Term of this Agreement, Supplier is obliged to inform Customer immediately of U.S. content change. Licenses or other authorizations required for the export of Services will be the responsibility of Supplier unless otherwise agreed by Customer and Supplier, in which event Supplier shall provide all necessary information as may be requested by Customer in order to obtain such licenses or authorizations. This includes, but is not limited to, the prohibition on the transfer of commodities, materials, software and technology (i.e., all Items) subject to this Agreement to, transit through, or procurement from, European Union /United States sanctioned countries and regions unless such transactions are permissible under applicable European Union /United States laws and regulations. \n(iv) Supplier shall make and keep books, records and account which, in reasonable detail, accurately and fairly reflect the transactions and dispositions of its funds and assets, and shall maintain a system of internal accounting controls intended to ensure compliance with Anti-Corruption Laws and sufficient to provide reasonable assurance that (i) transactions are executed and access to assets is permitted only in accordance with Supplier’s applicable policies and procedures and management’s general or specifications authorization; and (ii) transactions are recorded as necessary to permit preparation of periodic financial statements and to maintain accountability for assets.  \n(v)Supplier shall comply, and to require its subcontractors or any person under its control to comply with the CSR Rules.  \n(vi)Supplier undertakes that neither it or nor any of its subcontractors, vendors, agents, or other associated third parties shall utilize child, slave, prisoner or any other form of forced or involuntary labor, or engage in abusive employment or corrupt business practices in the supply of Services.  \nSupplier and its directors, officers, employees shall: \nComply in all respects with all Sanctions and;  \nNot carry on any trade, business or other activities with or for the benefit of any Sanctioned Person or which, in any other manner, could result in Supplier or its directors or Customer being in breach of any Sanctions or being designated, being subject to any penalties or restrictive measure being imposed pursuant to Sanctions or being designated as a Sanctioned Person.  \n(vii)    Supplier shall promptly notify Customer if it becomes aware of any non-compliance with this clause and any non-compliance with Sanctions and Customer reserves the right to require Supplier to immediately take appropriate remedial actions. "}, {"id": "d0-s55", "doc": 0, "title": "22.1 Applicable law", "html": "<p>This Agreement shall be governed by and interpreted in accordance with the laws of France, without regard to conflict of law provisions.  <\/p>", "text": "This Agreement shall be governed by and interpreted in accordance with the laws of France, without regard to conflict of law provisions.  "}, {"id": "d0-s56", "doc": 0, "title": "22.2Disputes", "html": "<p>Any disputes arising under this Agreement shall first be submitted to the respective authorized management representatives of the Parties for discussion in good faith and amicable resolution. time.<\/p><p>Annual rebates – if agreed – should be inserted here<\/p><p>Penalties:<\/p><p>In case of non-compliance by the Supplier with a commitment made under the Agreement subject to penalties, Supplier shall be liable to pay penalties as defined in the Agreement and/or in an Appendix, without such payment exempting Supplier or exonerating it from performing its obligations under the present Agreement.  Such penalties are subject to the following conditions:  - Penalties shall be applied, where applicable concurrently, during the period during which the cause for their application exists and without the need to carry out any formality or issue a formal notice.  - Penalties shall be calculated in accordance with the terms set out in the Appendix I Technical Appendix and/or Appendix 2 Financial Appendix.  - Except otherwise agreed elsewhere in the Agreement, penalties shall be capped at thirty percent (30%) of the agreed overall fixed price.  - Customer shall inform the Supplier, in writing at the end of each month, of the amount of the penalties which Supplier has to pay to Customer for the month concerned. However, it is understood between the Parties that failure by Customer to assert its rights to apply penalties shall under no circumstances be construed as a waiver of such rights. Customer reserves the right to demand in writing (email, letter etc.) the payment of penalties owed by the Supplier within twenty-four (24) months of the event providing causes for the application of a penalty. - Penalties shall be paid by the Supplier to Customer in accordance with the terms set out in the Agreement<\/p><p>A-Here are the expected elements regarding the penalties to be taken into account for the BUILD (project) and the RUN (current life):<\/p><p>1-Penalties for the BUILD: <\/p><p><strong>One milestone with penalty<\/strong> : respect of the GO LIVE milestone<\/p><p>The penalty is based on the number of days of delay due to the supplier. The penalty amount will be one percent (1%) of the amount of the project by calendar days of delay.<\/p><p><strong>Two quality defects will be <\/strong><strong>penalyzed<\/strong> : <\/p><p>               1 – Defect during Acceptance test phase<\/p><p>               2 – Defect between Go Live and Go Live + 1 month<\/p><p>These 2 defects KPI will be calculated as follow :<\/p><div class=\"tablewrap\"><table><tr><td><strong>Phase<\/strong><\/td><td><strong>Unit<\/strong><\/td><td><strong>Thresholds<\/strong><\/td><td><strong>Penalty calculation<\/strong><\/td><td><strong>Penalty amount<\/strong><\/td><\/tr><tr><td>Acceptance test<\/td><td>Number of blocking defects<\/td><td>4 blocking defects for 200 mandays of development and unit test activity<\/td><td>0,1 demerit point for each blocking defect above the threshold<\/td><td>1 demerit point = 4 000 euros<\/td><\/tr><tr><td>Go-Live + 1 month<\/td><td>Number of blocking defects<\/td><td>1 blocking defect for 200 mandays of development and unit test activity<\/td><td>0,1 demerit points for each blocking defect above the threshold<\/td><td>1 demerit point = 4 000 euros<\/td><\/tr><\/table><\/div><p>The total amount of penalties could not exceed 10% of the amount of the order.<\/p><p>2-Penalties for the RUN :<\/p><p><img loading=\"lazy\" alt=\"Source document figure\" src=\"data:image/png;base64,\"><\/p><div class=\"tablewrap\"><table><tr><td colspan=\"2\"><strong>Cost for 1 point of demerit :<\/strong> 500 Euros<\/td><td><\/td><td><\/td><td><\/td><td><\/td><td><\/td><td><\/td><td><\/td><\/tr><tr><td><\/td><td><\/td><td><\/td><td><\/td><td><\/td><td><\/td><td><\/td><td><\/td><td><\/td><\/tr><tr><td colspan=\"9\"><strong>Example of calculation :<\/strong> if 5 &quot;emergency&quot; incidents were declared during the quarter and 3 of them respected the threshold, the % of incidents corrected on time is 60%, so 20 % are below the thresold. The penalty cost will be : 20 (%) X 3 (pts) X 500 (€) = 30000 €<\/td><\/tr><tr><td><\/td><td><\/td><td><\/td><td><\/td><td><\/td><td><\/td><td><\/td><td><\/td><td><\/td><\/tr><tr><td colspan=\"8\"><strong>Capping of the penalties :<\/strong> the penalties that have to be payed each quarter can&#x27;t exceed 10% of the monthly cost of the Run contract<\/td><td><\/td><\/tr><tr><td><\/td><td><\/td><td><\/td><td><\/td><td><\/td><td><\/td><td><\/td><td><\/td><td><\/td><\/tr><tr><td colspan=\"9\"><strong>(*)<\/strong> For relevant reasons if for one KPI whose threshold (S) is expressed in percentage, the incident number is below to  1/(1-S), the measurement period is extended until the minimum number of incident is reached and the penalty will not be calculated  (and applied) until the minimum number of incident is reached. The calculation will be done on several quarters in order to reach the minimum incident number.  The final calculation will be always done on quarter end. <strong>For example :<\/strong> For the threshold S = 80, the minimum number of incident, below which the period of calculation is extended is 1:(1-0,8) = 5 incidents.<\/td><\/tr><\/table><\/div><p>B- The following elements must also be included in the supplier&#x27;s answer :<\/p><p>1-For the BUILD part : <\/p><p>- Elements used to calculate the amount of the project: details of the quotation mentioning <strong>by profile<\/strong>: the number of HJs, the rate (in €) and the location of the resources<\/p><p> -Element allowing to calculate the &quot;change requests&quot; that may appear during the project: <\/p><p>-detail the different types of work (units of work) that can be the subject of a change request <\/p><p>- for each type of work, mention the drivers used to estimate the load in HJ and the rate in € that will be applied<\/p><p>2-For the RUN part <strong>:<\/strong><\/p><p> - Element allowing to calculate the evolution requests that may appear on the application during the RUN phase: <\/p><p> -detail the different types of work (units of work) that can be subject to development <\/p><p> -for each type of work, mention the drivers used to estimate the load in HJ and the rate in € to be applied<\/p><p><strong><\/strong><\/p>", "text": "Financial appendix shall be agreed from time to time.\nAnnual rebates – if agreed – should be inserted here\nPenalties:\nIn case of non-compliance by the Supplier with a commitment made under the Agreement subject to penalties, Supplier shall be liable to pay penalties as defined in the Agreement and/or in an Appendix, without such payment exempting Supplier or exonerating it from performing its obligations under the present Agreement.  Such penalties are subject to the following conditions:  - Penalties shall be applied, where applicable concurrently, during the period during which the cause for their application exists and without the need to carry out any formality or issue a formal notice.  - Penalties shall be calculated in accordance with the terms set out in the Appendix I Technical Appendix and/or Appendix 2 Financial Appendix.  - Except otherwise agreed elsewhere in the Agreement, penalties shall be capped at thirty percent (30%) of the agreed overall fixed price.  - Customer shall inform the Supplier, in writing at the end of each month, of the amount of the penalties which Supplier has to pay to Customer for the month concerned. However, it is understood between the Parties that failure by Customer to assert its rights to apply penalties shall under no circumstances be construed as a waiver of such rights. Customer reserves the right to demand in writing (email, letter etc.) the payment of penalties owed by the Supplier within twenty-four (24) months of the event providing causes for the application of a penalty. - Penalties shall be paid by the Supplier to Customer in accordance with the terms set out in the Agreement\nA-Here are the expected elements regarding the penalties to be taken into account for the BUILD (project) and the RUN (current life):\n1-Penalties for the BUILD: \nOne milestone with penalty : respect of the GO LIVE milestone\nThe penalty is based on the number of days of delay due to the supplier. The penalty amount will be one percent (1%) of the amount of the project by calendar days of delay.\nTwo quality defects will be penalyzed : \n               1 – Defect during Acceptance test phase\n               2 – Defect between Go Live and Go Live + 1 month\nThese 2 defects KPI will be calculated as follow :\nPhase\nUnit\nThresholds\nPenalty calculation\nPenalty amount\nAcceptance test\nNumber of blocking defects\n4 blocking defects for 200 mandays of development and unit test activity\n0,1 demerit point for each blocking defect above the threshold\n1 demerit point = 4 000 euros\nGo-Live + 1 month\nNumber of blocking defects\n1 blocking defect for 200 mandays of development and unit test activity\n0,1 demerit points for each blocking defect above the threshold\n1 demerit point = 4 000 euros\nThe total amount of penalties could not exceed 10% of the amount of the order.\n2-Penalties for the RUN :\n\nCost for 1 point of demerit : 500 Euros\n\n\n\n\n\n\n\n\n\n\n\n\n\n\n\n\nExample of calculation : if 5 \"emergency\" incidents were declared during the quarter and 3 of them respected the threshold, the % of incidents corrected on time is 60%, so 20 % are below the thresold. The penalty cost will be : 20 (%) X 3 (pts) X 500 (€) = 30000 €\n\n\n\n\n\n\n\n\n\nCapping of the penalties : the penalties that have to be payed each quarter can't exceed 10% of the monthly cost of the Run contract\n\n\n\n\n\n\n\n\n\n\n(*) For relevant reasons if for one KPI whose threshold (S) is expressed in percentage, the incident number is below to  1/(1-S), the measurement period is extended until the minimum number of incident is reached and the penalty will not be calculated  (and applied) until the minimum number of incident is reached. The calculation will be done on several quarters in order to reach the minimum incident number.  The final calculation will be always done on quarter end. For example : For the threshold S = 80, the minimum number of incident, below which the period of calculation is extended is 1:(1-0,8) = 5 incidents.\nB- The following elements must also be included in the supplier's answer :\n1-For the BUILD part : \n- Elements used to calculate the amount of the project: details of the quotation mentioning by profile: the number of HJs, the rate (in €) and the location of the resources\n -Element allowing to calculate the \"change requests\" that may appear during the project: \n-detail the different types of work (units of work) that can be the subject of a change request \n- for each type of work, mention the drivers used to estimate the load in HJ and the rate in € that will be applied\n2-For the RUN part :\n - Element allowing to calculate the evolution requests that may appear on the application during the RUN phase: \n -detail the different types of work (units of work) that can be subject to development \n -for each type of work, mention the drivers used to estimate the load in HJ and the rate in € to be applied\n"}, {"id": "d0-s60", "doc": 0, "title": "APPENDIX III: CUSTOMER CYBERSECURITY RULES", "html": "<p>Supplier undertakes to comply with the following documents Rules<\/p><p><img loading=\"lazy\" alt=\"Source document figure\" src=\"data:image/jpeg;base64,\"><\/p><p>Stellantis Global Supplier Information Security Requirements<\/p><p>Contents<\/p><p><strong>1.<\/strong><strong>Introduction<\/strong><strong>2<\/strong><\/p><p><strong>2.<\/strong><strong>Purpose<\/strong><strong>2<\/strong><\/p><p><strong>3.<\/strong><strong>Applicability<\/strong><strong>2<\/strong><\/p><p><strong>4.<\/strong><strong>Compliance<\/strong><strong>2<\/strong><\/p><p><strong>6.<\/strong><strong>Definitions<\/strong><strong>5<\/strong><\/p><p>Document History<\/p><div class=\"tablewrap\"><table><tr><td>Version<\/td><td>Month &amp; Year<\/td><td>Comments<\/td><td>Owner<\/td><\/tr><tr><td>1.0<\/td><td>9 June 2022<\/td><td>Initial Document creation<\/td><td>Stellantis - Security Governance &amp; Coordination Team<\/td><\/tr><\/table><\/div><p><strong>Introduction<\/strong><\/p><p>The security requirements outlined herein are applicable to Third Parties that process, access, interact with, or store Stellantis data. This data may include intellectual property, customer or employee personal information, or other uncategorized Stellantis-owned data. In addition, this document applies to any Third Party that has access to Stellantis Information Systems through the Partner VPN or other approved method.<\/p><p>Stellantis reserves the right to update this document from time to time.<\/p><p><strong>Purpose<\/strong><\/p><p>The purpose of this document is to define the high-level security requirements Third Parties must follow to protect Stellantis information and IT (Information Technology) assets.<\/p><p><strong>Applicability<\/strong><\/p><p>These requirements apply to all Third Parties who:<\/p><p>Collect, transmit, manage, access, or store Stellantis Information (including intellectual property, customer/employee personal information, or other uncategorized Stellantis-owned data)<\/p><p>Provide Stellantis Vital or Critical Business Services<\/p><p>Connect to Stellantis Information Systems using the Partner VPN or other approved method.<\/p><p><strong>Compliance<\/strong><\/p><p>Third Party contracts in place prior to publishing of this document must minimally comply with the version of the Stellantis information security provisions or Third-Party Information Security Requirements specified in their contract and are subject to an annual request for attestation of compliance. Additionally, existing Third-Party agreements are subject to evaluation of inherent risk, based on the nature of the goods and/or services provided to Stellantis. Modifications to these Stellantis Third Party Information Security Requirements must be reviewed on a case-by-case basis.<\/p><p><strong>Requirements<\/strong><\/p><p>The following identifies the minimum level of Information Security Requirements: <\/p><div class=\"tablewrap\"><table><tr><td><strong>#<\/strong><\/td><td><strong>Security Control<\/strong><\/td><td><strong> <\/strong><\/td><td><strong>Requirements<\/strong><\/td><\/tr><tr><td>1<\/td><td>Information Security Policy<\/td><td>1.1<\/td><td>Maintain an information security policy that, at a minimum, includes its overall objectives and scope and the importance of security to Third Party.<\/td><\/tr><tr><td>2<\/td><td>Password Controls And Access Management<\/td><td>2.1<\/td><td>Assign unique access/authentication credentials to each Third-Party Personnel with authorized access to Stellantis data.<\/td><\/tr><tr><td><\/td><td><\/td><td>2.2<\/td><td>At a minimum comply with the password standards and requirements established by ISO 27002 or equivalent industry standard.<\/td><\/tr><tr><td><\/td><td><\/td><td>2.3<\/td><td>Ensure segregation of duties through the use of role-based access controls.<\/td><\/tr><tr><td><\/td><td><\/td><td>2.4<\/td><td>Promptly disable access privileges to Stellantis data for any Third-Party Personnel who are terminated or otherwise no longer need such access.<\/td><\/tr><tr><td>3<\/td><td>Encryption<\/td><td>3.1<\/td><td>Encrypt all Stellantis Data in transit and at rest using industry-standard encryption that meets NIST FIPS minimum requirements.<\/td><\/tr><tr><td>4<\/td><td>Anti-Malware Protection<\/td><td>4.1<\/td><td>Protect all IT systems from malware through the use of antivirus or other anti-malware practices<\/td><\/tr><tr><td>5<\/td><td>Network Security<\/td><td>5.1<\/td><td>Isolate trusted networks containing sensitive data from non-trusted networks.<\/td><\/tr><tr><td><\/td><td><\/td><td>5.2<\/td><td>Encrypt wireless network traffic and implement default-deny, least-privilege policies on network firewalls.<\/td><\/tr><tr><td>6<\/td><td>Vulnerability Assessments<\/td><td>6.1<\/td><td>Implement a vulnerability assessment process that includes steps to prioritize high risk vulnerabilities and This data may include intellectual property, customer or employee personal information, or other uncategorized Stellantis-owned data. In addition, this document applies to any Third Party that has access to Stellantis Information Systems through the Partner VPN or other approved method.\nStellantis reserves the right to update this document from time to time.\nPurpose\nThe purpose of this document is to define the high-level security requirements Third Parties must follow to protect Stellantis information and IT (Information Technology) assets.\nApplicability\nThese requirements apply to all Third Parties who:\nCollect, transmit, manage, access, or store Stellantis Information (including intellectual property, customer/employee personal information, or other uncategorized Stellantis-owned data)\nProvide Stellantis Vital or Critical Business Services\nConnect to Stellantis Information Systems using the Partner VPN or other approved method.\nCompliance\nThird Party contracts in place prior to publishing of this document must minimally comply with the version of the Stellantis information security provisions or Third-Party Information Security Requirements specified in their contract and are subject to an annual request for attestation of compliance. Additionally, existing Third-Party agreements are subject to evaluation of inherent risk, based on the nature of the goods and/or services provided to Stellantis. Modifications to these Stellantis Third Party Information Security Requirements must be reviewed on a case-by-case basis.\nRequirements\nThe following identifies the minimum level of Information Security Requirements: \n#\nSecurity Control\n \nRequirements\n1\nInformation Security Policy\n1.1\nMaintain an information security policy that, at a minimum, includes its overall objectives and scope and the importance of security to Third Party.\n2\nPassword Controls And Access Management\n2.1\nAssign unique access/authentication credentials to each Third-Party Personnel with authorized access to Stellantis data.\n\n\n2.2\nAt a minimum comply with the password standards and requirements established by ISO 27002 or equivalent industry standard.\n\n\n2.3\nEnsure segregation of duties through the use of role-based access controls.\n\n\n2.4\nPromptly disable access privileges to Stellantis data for any Third-Party Personnel who are terminated or otherwise no longer need such access.\n3\nEncryption\n3.1\nEncrypt all Stellantis Data in transit and at rest using industry-standard encryption that meets NIST FIPS minimum requirements.\n4\nAnti-Malware Protection\n4.1\nProtect all IT systems from malware through the use of antivirus or other anti-malware practices\n5\nNetwork Security\n5.1\nIsolate trusted networks containing sensitive data from non-trusted networks.\n\n\n5.2\nEncrypt wireless network traffic and implement default-deny, least-privilege policies on network firewalls.\n6\nVulnerability Assessments\n6.1\nImplement a vulnerability assessment process that includes steps to prioritize high risk vulnerabilities and remediate identified security issues on infrastructure, middleware, and applications in a timely manner.\n\n\n6.2\nPerform regular vulnerability scans and assessments to identify all potential vulnerabilities. Stellantis may ask for a vulnerability report for any systems that handle Stellantis data.\n7\nIncident Response\n7.1\nHave in place a security incident response plan for identifying, reporting, and appropriately responding to known or suspected security incidents impacting Stellantis data.\n\n\n7.2\nNotify Stellantis of any security incidents impacting Stellantis Data or systems within 72 hours of detection and provide an action plan that includes coordination of investigation, impact to Stellantis data, and remediation activities.\n8\nSystem And Data Availability\n8.1\nMaintain an availability plan that can meet the business requirements outlined in the contractual agreements. This may include backups and restorations, disaster recovery, and business continuity for all locations and applications used to provide services to Stellantis.\n\n\n8.2\nMaintain a business continuity plan for restoring normal business functions within the restoration requirements defined in the agreement.\n9\nPhysical Security\n9.1\nImplement safeguards and controls that restrict unauthorized physical access to areas containing equipment used to access, store, or transmit Stellantis Data. This includes, but is not limited to access controls (keys, key cards, badge access, etc.), surveillance (Closed Circuity TV, networked security cameras, etc.), and alarms.\n10\nData Retention And Destruction\n10.1\nAt any time, and upon termination or expiration of business agreements, except to the extent required by law, immediately return or, if directed by Stellantis, securely destroy any and all Stellantis Data.\n11\nSubcontractors\n11.1\nEnsure Third Party workforce members working with Stellantis information are aware of and conform to these Third-Party Information Security Requirements as well as legal and regulatory requirements pertaining to Stellantis Information.\n12\nSecurity Awareness\n12.1\nHave a defined program to provide periodic information security awareness training to Third Party’s workforce who will have access to Stellantis Data. Education and awareness training shall include the secure handling of Stellantis Data.\n\n\n12.2\nEnsure all Workforce members are sufficiently educated to perform their jobs effectively and ensure the security of Stellantis Data.\n13\nRemote Access Control\n13.1\nAlways use a Stellantis-approved method when connecting remotely.\n\n\n13.2\nProvide Stellantis the right to monitor all network connections between Stellantis and Third Party.\n14\nAudit\n14.1\nProvide Stellantis, or a mutually agreed upon independent firm, permission to perform a security assessment to ensure compliance with the Third-Party Information Security Requirements and other contractual agreements.\n15\nSoftware Lifecycle\n15.1\nInformation security checkpoints shall be incorporated into the software development lifecycle when necessary;\nRisk assessment process\nDocumented security requirements\nSource code review\nSecurity testing\nPatch management\nChange management\nProblem Management\n16\nCommunications\n16.1\nStellantis Data must not be disclosed or communicated in any manner without approval in writing from Stellantis.\n17\nConfiguration Management\n17.1\nMaintain a documented set of baseline security configuration standards for devices with the concept of Least Functionality.\n\n\n17.2\nMonitor unauthorized changes or deviations from the Security Baselines in deployed devices.\n18\nRemovable Media\n18.1\nProtect Stellantis data from unauthorized disclosure such as through the use of Data Loss Prevention Tools.\n19\nSecurity Assessment\n19.1\nComplete a Supplier Security Assessment within an agreed upon timeframe (typically 14 days after receipt of the assessment) if requested by Stellantis.\nDefinitions\nAvailability Plan\nPlan to ensure availability requirements can be met as determined by the Agreement.\nAgreement\nThe governing contracts, purchase orders, or other documented or non-verbal agreements between the Third Party and Stellantis that set forth the scope of products and/or services being provided.\nContinuity Plan\nPlan to quickly recover or ensure availability during unforeseen circumstances (i.e., natural disasters, power outages, pandemics, etc.).\nData Loss Prevention Tools\nInformation security tools that are used to prevent data loss by prohibiting the use of removable media, uploading data to unauthorized file sharing sites, or other industry standard data loss prevention strategies.\nThird Party\nPerson, company, business, organization, vendors, contractor, sub-contractor, service provider, or other group that provides goods or services to Stellantis.\nSecurity Baselines\nNormal activity that is observed in everyday use of an Information System. Deviations from these baselines could be caused by a security incident.\nSupplier Security Assessment\nA self-attestation questionnaire that provides Stellantis with a overview of a supplier’s internal information security practices. This questionnaire may be assigned to a supplier via a secured SaaS based platform. \nInformation System\nAny electronic systems that handle information. This can include network infrastructure, servers, or other systems that support the terms outlined in the Agreement.\nLeast Functionality\nConcept that ensures an Information System is configured only to provide the essential functionality and prohibits or significantly limits non-essential functions.\nPartner VPN\nA secured VPN that Stellantis provides to its suppliers when necessary. Access to the Partner VPN is provided on an as-needed basis.\nWorkforce\nEmployees, contractors, or other third parties that are supporting the Agreement.\n\nAppendix IV : FOSS TERMS OF USE  (Free and to include in any Deliverable (i) any FOSS for which Customer has not granted its prior written agreement for the underlying Open Source Licence terms and/or (ii) any software subject to an Incompatible Licence.\n2.4Supplier undertakes to communicate prior to the delivery of any Deliverable to Customer: \nthe comprehensive and detailed list of FOSS included in any Deliverable or any feedback27\n6.3SLAs29"}, {"id": "d1-s2", "doc": 1, "title": "General Description", "html": "<p>The uncertain and changing situation the Stellantis Group is living, as a global car manufacturer, is an opportunity to promote and adopt new tools based on data, digital solutions &amp; Lean/Agile methodologies at a Stellantis level. With constantly evolving and competitive markets and optimizing resources, it is also necessary to review how we animate our networks to be more efficient. <\/p><p>That is why, we are pursuing its transformation and launch a project which purpose is to change the way we collectively work. At the same time, Stellantis wants to strengthen the relationship between the brands and their network via a community platform called Business Community.<\/p><p>The main target of the new Digital backbone is to allow synergies, simplification and efficiency through a unique platform for dealers and field force with personalized contents to know very quickly what you need to know and what you have to do. Thus, this platform aims to replace existing tools and functionalities, which are today duplicate for several brands and countries. <\/p><p>This new version of DealerX platform will be at the same time a business social network, which will allow top-down and bottom-up communications and a digital workplace, which will improve the efficiency of the Stellantis Network Operations.  <\/p><p>To improve the productivity and the user experience, the provider will have to work on 3 pillars: <\/p><p><strong>ONLY ONE TOOL<\/strong><\/p><p>For all profiles &amp; all activities (one user may also mix several profile &amp; activities) to access all the process<\/p><p>With Contents, Social interactions, Documentation, Ticketing and Application bookmark (incl. Single Sign on) <\/p><p>Visualization &amp; Personalization according to the profile (Adapt content to user &amp; to management level).<\/p><p>Authorization to contents and documents managed centrally.  <\/p><p>Enabling “Dealer&amp;Repairer SDK” concept to allow Continuous Integration and Delivery of Applications / Features proposed to End users. Allowing them to have “AppStore like” experience customizing as deep as required by local context. <\/p><p>Replace fragmented communication portals with one common DealerX experience.<\/p><p><strong>TO SIMPLIFY DAILY LIFE<\/strong><\/p><p>Assist Stellantis network in their daily tasks. <\/p><p>Display customized information and functionalities. <\/p><p>Deliver the messages at the right person, at the right time.<\/p><p>Make all processes accessible from one single portal.<\/p><p>Make processes faster and more robust. <\/p><p>Provide a flexible platform for dealer-facing features across business units<\/p><p><strong>USE FULL POWER OF DIGITAL<\/strong><\/p><p>Get quick answers to problems.<\/p><p>Allow the rapid creation of contents link to users ‘issues. <\/p><p>Improve the collaboration through social communication tools.<\/p><p>Integrate different technologies to harmonize processes.<\/p><p>Agentic AI implementation<\/p><p>AI Driven DevOps<\/p>", "text": "The uncertain and changing situation the Stellantis Group is living, as a global car manufacturer, is an opportunity to promote and adopt new tools based on data, digital solutions & Lean/Agile methodologies at a Stellantis level. With constantly evolving and competitive markets and optimizing resources, it is also necessary to review how we animate our networks to be more efficient. \nThat is why, we are pursuing its transformation and launch a project which purpose is to change the way we collectively work. At the same time, Stellantis wants to strengthen the relationship between the brands and their network via a community platform called Business Community.\nThe main target of the new Digital backbone is to allow synergies, simplification and efficiency through a unique platform for dealers and field force with personalized contents to know very quickly what you need to know and what you have to do. Thus, this platform aims to replace existing tools and functionalities, which are today duplicate for several brands and countries. \nThis new version of DealerX platform will be at the same time a business social network, which will allow top-down and bottom-up communications and a digital workplace, which will improve the efficiency of the Stellantis Network Operations.  \nTo improve the productivity and the user experience, the provider will have to work on 3 pillars: \nONLY ONE TOOL\nFor all profiles & all activities (one user may also mix several profile & activities) to access all the process\nWith Contents, Social interactions, Documentation, Ticketing and Application bookmark (incl. Single Sign on) \nVisualization & Personalization according to the profile (Adapt content to user & to management level).\nAuthorization to contents and documents managed centrally.  \nEnabling “Dealer&Repairer SDK” concept to allow Continuous Integration and Delivery of Applications / Features proposed to End users. Allowing them to have “AppStore like” experience customizing as deep as required by local context. \nReplace fragmented communication portals with one common DealerX experience.\nTO SIMPLIFY DAILY LIFE\nAssist Stellantis network in their daily tasks. \nDisplay customized information and functionalities. \nDeliver the messages at the right person, at the right time.\nMake all processes accessible from one single portal.\nMake processes faster and more robust. \nProvide a flexible platform for dealer-facing features across business units\nUSE FULL POWER OF DIGITAL\nGet quick answers to problems.\nAllow the rapid creation of contents link to users ‘issues. \nImprove the collaboration through social communication tools.\nIntegrate different technologies to harmonize processes.\nAgentic AI implementation\nAI Driven DevOps"}, {"id": "d1-s3", "doc": 1, "title": "Strategic Approach", "html": "<p>Linked to process improvement and internal reorganization, the Digital Platform will be an enabler of the collective transformation and will boost the business performance. <\/p><p>The new strategy is built on:<\/p><p><strong>A New digital interface<\/strong>: Common entry point for all actors (Central, NSC, Field Staff, Business coaches (BC), Dealers, Importers) which allows direct access to different information and processes (Access to applications, Useful Contents, Social communication, Ticket creation, Documentation, Harmonized user journey...)<\/p><p><strong>A <\/strong><strong>Multi activities and multi brands approach<\/strong> for the Business coach.<\/p><p>The purpose of this tender is to select one or more partners capable of supporting the Stellantis Group in the evolution and enhancement of the current <em>DealerX <\/em>platform, enabling its rollout across multiple countries within the Enlarged Europe region and supporting the Group’s strategic objectives.<\/p><p>Partner(s) is/are expected to demonstrate how their proposed solution meets Stellantis business and technical requirements, aligns with the target vision for the platform, and provides a scalable and sustainable foundation for future growth. In addition, bidders shall demonstrate their capability to deliver and manage the program in close collaboration with Stellantis teams, including their proposed delivery methodology, governance model, organizational structure, and the skills and experience of the proposed resources.<\/p><p>A key requirement of the target solution is the adoption of a reusable SDK-based approach that supports the development of portable features, facilitates reuse across markets and business domains, and enables long-term transferability and maintainability of the platform.<\/p><p>The current <em>DealerX <\/em>platform should be considered the baseline for the proposed solution. Providers are not expected to replace the platform from scratch; instead, they are encouraged to leverage and enhance existing capabilities wherever appropriate. Where the current architecture, processes, or components do not meet target requirements or industry&#x27;s best practices, Partner(s) may propose improvements or alternative approaches. Any recommended architectural evolution, modernization activities, or platform enhancement initiatives should be clearly described within the tender response, including associated effort estimates, resource requirements, dependencies, and budget implications.<\/p><p>The quality of all the documents and work produced by the Provider in the pre-selection phase are fundamental.<\/p><p>The Requirements we have put down are not exclusive of any improvements and additional features that the Provider may propose.<\/p><p>The project and partnership between Stellantis and the tender will be based on agile methodology, with content co-construction, MVPs, iterations, feedbacks and adaptation: workshops on the field with main actors will be paramount. <\/p><p>A Planning milestone proposal is detailed here below which remains an estimation which could be reviewed by Stellantis, as well as any content of this RFQ. <\/p><p><strong>RFQ timeline<\/strong> <\/p><p>From RFQ issue to awarding to end of roll out including deliverables <\/p><div class=\"tablewrap\"><table><tr><td><strong>By <\/strong><strong>8<\/strong><strong> Oct 2026<\/strong> <\/td><td><strong>By <\/strong><strong>15<\/strong><strong> Oct 2026<\/strong> <\/td><td><strong>By <\/strong><strong>20<\/strong><strong> Oct 2026<\/strong> <\/td><td><strong>By <\/strong><strong>27<\/strong><strong> Oct 2026<\/strong> <\/td><td><strong>By <\/strong><strong>4<\/strong><strong> Nov 2026<\/strong> <\/td><td><strong>By 1<\/strong><strong>3<\/strong><strong> Nov 2026<\/strong> <\/td><\/tr><tr><td><strong>01<\/strong> <\/td><td><strong>02<\/strong> <\/td><td><strong>03<\/strong> <\/td><td><strong>04<\/strong> <\/td><td><strong>05<\/strong> <\/td><td><strong>06<\/strong> <\/td><\/tr><tr><td>RFQ issue <\/td><td>RFQ questions deadline <\/td><td>Webinar with bidders <\/td><td>Proof of Value delivery &amp; pitch <\/td><td>RFQ answer deadline <\/td><td>RFQ awarding <\/td><\/tr><\/table><\/div><p><img loading=\"lazy\" alt=\"Source document figure\" src=\"data:image/png;base64,\"><\/p>", "text": "Linked to process improvement and internal reorganization, the Digital Platform will be an enabler of the collective transformation and will boost the business performance. \nThe new strategy is built on:\nA New digital interface: Common entry point for all actors (Central, NSC, Field Staff, Business coaches (BC), Dealers, Importers) which allows direct access to different information and processes (Access to applications, Useful Contents, Social communication, Ticket creation, Documentation, Harmonized user journey...)\nA Multi activities and multi brands approach for the Business coach.\nThe purpose of this tender is to select one or more partners capable of supporting the Stellantis Group in the evolution and enhancement of the current DealerX platform, enabling its rollout across multiple countries within the Enlarged Europe region and supporting the Group’s strategic objectives.\nPartner(s) is/are expected to demonstrate how their proposed solution meets Stellantis business and technical requirements, aligns with the target vision for the platform, and provides a scalable and sustainable foundation for future growth. In addition, bidders shall demonstrate their capability to deliver and manage the program in close collaboration with Stellantis teams, including their proposed delivery methodology, governance model, organizational structure, and the skills and experience of the proposed resources.\nA key requirement of the target solution is the adoption of a reusable SDK-based approach that supports the development of portable features, facilitates reuse across markets and business domains, and enables long-term transferability and maintainability of the platform.\nThe current DealerX platform should be considered the baseline for the proposed solution. Providers are not expected to replace the platform from scratch; instead, they are encouraged to leverage and enhance existing capabilities wherever appropriate. Where the current architecture, processes, or components do not meet target requirements or industry's best practices, Partner(s) may propose improvements or alternative approaches. Any recommended architectural evolution, modernization activities, or platform enhancement initiatives should be clearly described within the tender response, including associated effort estimates, resource requirements, dependencies, and budget implications.\nThe quality of all the documents and work produced by the Provider in the pre-selection phase are fundamental.\nThe Requirements we have put down are not exclusive of any improvements and additional features that the Provider may propose.\nThe project and partnership between Stellantis and the tender will be based on agile methodology, with content co-construction, MVPs, iterations, feedbacks and adaptation: workshops on the field with main actors will be paramount. \nA Planning milestone proposal is detailed here below which remains an estimation which could be reviewed by Stellantis, as well as any content of this RFQ. \nRFQ timeline \nFrom RFQ issue to awarding to end of roll out including deliverables \nBy 8 Oct 2026 \nBy 15 Oct 2026 \nBy 20 Oct 2026 \nBy 27 Oct 2026 \nBy 4 Nov 2026 \nBy 13 Nov 2026 \n01 \n02 \n03 \n04 \n05 \n06 \nRFQ issue \nRFQ questions deadline \nWebinar with bidders \nProof of Value delivery & pitch \nRFQ answer deadline \nRFQ awarding \n"}, {"id": "d1-s4", "doc": 1, "title": "Perimeter of needs", "html": "<p>The implementation of this future tool will be for all Stellantis Brands, all activities and all the markets from Enlarged Europe, including Importers inside EE) . <\/p><p>Digital platform shall manage a complex matrix organization of several users’ communities (internal &amp; external of the group) linked to hierarchical &amp; functional organizations: outlets, groups or outlets, projects, areas, countries (in country language), dealers &amp; users, single brand, dealers &amp; users multi brand, single/multi activities, different maturity levels. <\/p><p>To do so:<\/p><p>Portal will be displaying Content, Applications, Documentation, Social interactions, Ticket cases, based on the user profile (Country, Brand, type of profile, etc..). It must be possible for the user to modify his settings to highlight dominant posts rather than others. Allowing flexibility as well to the local context and diversity.  <\/p><p>From the user’s perspective, it must be possible to find each content very easily through the search engine. It must allow a word search on content, comments, users and file attachments and inside different part of the content (title, body of the content, text, video…)  <\/p><p>Contents recommendations must also be proposed according to the searches performed. <\/p><p>View restrictions must also be possible.  <\/p><p>Access to the tool should be made using the STELLANTIS user IDs. <\/p><p>The Portal must be fully integrated within the Stellantis IT landscape, as well as also with 3rd parties ecosystems.<\/p><p>Meet all legal and regulatory requirements in the countries/regions the user is located <\/p><p>AI Driven DevOps<\/p><p>Administration of <em>DealerX<\/em><em> <\/em>will be managed by central team, with support from the supplier, but delegation to local or functional teams will be possible to increase the appropriation by end-users. Granting Dev flexibility and autonomy to leverage SDK concept and integrate specific “widget”/promotion/etc… for specific national event.<\/p><p><em>DealerX<\/em><em> <\/em>will have to adapt to market evolutions and stay agile.<\/p>", "text": "The implementation of this future tool will be for all Stellantis Brands, all activities and all the markets from Enlarged Europe, including Importers inside EE) . \nDigital platform shall manage a complex matrix organization of several users’ communities (internal & external of the group) linked to hierarchical & functional organizations: outlets, groups or outlets, projects, areas, countries (in country language), dealers & users, single brand, dealers & users multi brand, single/multi activities, different maturity levels. \nTo do so:\nPortal will be displaying Content, Applications, Documentation, Social interactions, Ticket cases, based on the user profile (Country, Brand, type of profile, etc..). It must be possible for the user to modify his settings to highlight dominant posts rather than others. Allowing flexibility as well to the local context and diversity.  \nFrom the user’s perspective, it must be possible to find each content very easily through the search engine. It must allow a word search on content, comments, users and file attachments and inside different part of the content (title, body of the content, text, video…)  \nContents recommendations must also be proposed according to the searches performed. \nView restrictions must also be possible.  \nAccess to the tool should be made using the STELLANTIS user IDs. \nThe Portal must be fully integrated within the Stellantis IT landscape, as well as also with 3rd parties ecosystems.\nMeet all legal and regulatory requirements in the countries/regions the user is located \nAI Driven DevOps\nAdministration of DealerX will be managed by central team, with support from the supplier, but delegation to local or functional teams will be possible to increase the appropriation by end-users. Granting Dev flexibility and autonomy to leverage SDK concept and integrate specific “widget”/promotion/etc… for specific national event.\nDealerX will have to adapt to market evolutions and stay agile."}, {"id": "d1-s5", "doc": 1, "title": "Where are we now?", "html": "<p><strong>Existing Platform and Strategic Direction<\/strong><\/p><p>The vision, principles, and strategic direction described throughout this document represent the foundation upon which the future portal ecosystem shall evolve. These elements define the long-term objectives, key architectural pillars, and overall approach that must remain central throughout the implementation and subsequent evolution of the solution.<\/p><p>However, it is important to emphasize that a platform already exists today and is currently operational. Therefore, the scope of this initiative is <strong>not the development of a completely new platform from scratch<\/strong>, but rather the design, implementation, and industrialization of the new portal experience, including all required functionalities, widgets, services, integrations, and user-facing features.<\/p><p>While the existing platform provides a solid foundation, it should not be considered immutable. Suppliers are expected to review the current landscape and identify opportunities for continuous improvement, optimization, and enhancement wherever these can generate measurable business value.<\/p><p>A key aspect of the initiative is the fact that the backend platform is already shared across multiple business solutions and portals within the ecosystem, including the <strong>Single Repairer Portal (SRP)<\/strong>. This approach enables consistency, scalability, and operational efficiency across multiple services and user journeys.<\/p><p><strong>Platform Reusability as a Core Requirement<\/strong><\/p><p>One of the primary objectives of this RFQ is to maximize platform reusability and accelerate future service adoption.<\/p><p>The target vision is based on the following principles:<\/p><p><strong>High component reusability<\/strong>, targeting approximately <strong>80% reuse<\/strong> of platform capabilities across current and future portals.<\/p><p><strong>Standardized services and shared business capabilities<\/strong> that can support multiple use cases with minimal customization.<\/p><p><strong>Scalable architecture<\/strong> capable of supporting the progressive onboarding of additional services and business domains.<\/p><p><strong>Reduced implementation time and lower total cost of ownership<\/strong> through the reuse of existing assets and components.<\/p><p>Evolution towards a <strong>service marketplace approach<\/strong>, where new services and functionalities can be rapidly integrated and made available to users through a common platform.<\/p><p><strong>Existing Capabilities Already Available<\/strong><\/p><p>Several key capabilities have already been implemented and are available within the current platform, including but not limited to:<\/p><p>User <strong>notifications and alert<\/strong> management.<\/p><p><strong>Mass email campaigns<\/strong> triggered by the publication of new content or communications.<\/p><p>Integration with external systems through <strong>Single Sign-On (SSO)<\/strong> mechanisms.<\/p><p>Configuration and personalization of news and content carousels.<\/p><p>Content management capabilities for <strong>FAQs <\/strong>and knowledge-base sections.<\/p><p>Existing content publishing and administration functionalities.<\/p><p>Core platform services and backend components already leveraged by other portals within the ecosystem.<\/p><p><strong>Supplier Expectations<\/strong><\/p><p>For clarity, Stellantis does not expect the selected Supplier to replace or rebuild existing capabilities where these are already available and fit for purpose.<\/p><p>Instead, the Supplier shall:<\/p><p>Leverage the existing platform as the primary foundation.<\/p><p>Maximize reuse of available functionalities and shared services.<\/p><p>Identify gaps and implement the additional capabilities required by the target vision.<\/p><p>Enhance, optimize, and industrialize the solution where necessary.<\/p><p>Deliver a fully operational, scalable, and future-ready portal that can support business growth and the onboarding of new services over time.<\/p><p>Ultimately, the objective is to capitalize on the investments already made, accelerate delivery through reuse, and transform the existing platform into a robust and extensible ecosystem capable of supporting a growing portfolio of digital services.<\/p><p><img loading=\"lazy\" alt=\"Source document figure\" src=\"data:image/png;base64,\"><\/p>", "text": "Existing Platform and Strategic Direction\nThe vision, principles, and strategic direction described throughout this document represent the foundation upon which the future portal ecosystem shall evolve. These elements define the long-term objectives, key architectural pillars, and overall approach that must remain central throughout the implementation and subsequent evolution of the solution.\nHowever, it is important to emphasize that a platform already exists today and is currently operational. Therefore, the scope of this initiative is not the development of a completely new platform from scratch, but rather the design, implementation, and industrialization of the new portal experience, including all required functionalities, widgets, services, integrations, and user-facing features.\nWhile the existing platform provides a solid foundation, it should not be considered immutable. Suppliers are expected to review the current landscape and identify opportunities for continuous improvement, optimization, and enhancement wherever these can generate measurable business value.\nA key aspect of the initiative is the fact that the backend platform is already shared across multiple business solutions and portals within the ecosystem, including the Single Repairer Portal (SRP). This approach enables consistency, scalability, and operational efficiency across multiple services and user journeys.\nPlatform Reusability as a Core Requirement\nOne of the primary objectives of this RFQ is to maximize platform reusability and accelerate future service adoption.\nThe target vision is based on the following principles:\nHigh component reusability, targeting approximately 80% reuse of platform capabilities across current and future portals.\nStandardized services and shared business capabilities that can support multiple use cases with minimal customization.\nScalable architecture capable of supporting the progressive onboarding of additional services and business domains.\nReduced implementation time and lower total cost of ownership through the reuse of existing assets and components.\nEvolution towards a service marketplace approach, where new services and functionalities can be rapidly integrated and made available to users through a common platform.\nExisting Capabilities Already Available\nSeveral key capabilities have already been implemented and are available within the current platform, including but not limited to:\nUser notifications and alert management.\nMass email campaigns triggered by the publication of new content or communications.\nIntegration with external systems through Single Sign-On (SSO) mechanisms.\nConfiguration and personalization of news and content carousels.\nContent management capabilities for FAQs and knowledge-base sections.\nExisting content publishing and administration functionalities.\nCore platform services and backend components already leveraged by other portals within the ecosystem.\nSupplier Expectations\nFor clarity, Stellantis does not expect the selected Supplier to replace or rebuild existing capabilities where these are already available and fit for purpose.\nInstead, the Supplier shall:\nLeverage the existing platform as the primary foundation.\nMaximize reuse of available functionalities and shared services.\nIdentify gaps and implement the additional capabilities required by the target vision.\nEnhance, optimize, and industrialize the solution where necessary.\nDeliver a fully operational, scalable, and future-ready portal that can support business growth and the onboarding of new services over time.\nUltimately, the objective is to capitalize on the investments already made, accelerate delivery through reuse, and transform the existing platform into a robust and extensible ecosystem capable of supporting a growing portfolio of digital services.\n"}, {"id": "d1-s6", "doc": 1, "title": "Business Glossary", "html": "<p>AFS: After sales<\/p><p>AI: Artificial intelligence<\/p><p>AR: Authorized Repairer – also used the word “dealer”<\/p><p>Assigned stock: Vehicle owned by a dealer<\/p><p>BC: Business Coach<\/p><p><strong>« Blocking Incident» <\/strong>means any absence of function, non-compliance of the Deliverables with the Technical and Functional Specifications and/or with the Documentation, causing indifferently the complete or partial unavailability of an essential function of a Deliverables and/or a problem of consistency and / or integrity of the Data.<\/p><p>CEC : Customer Engagement Center<\/p><p>DMS: Dealer Management System <\/p><p><strong>« DICT  or AICT»<\/strong> : The AICT of an application or an infrastructure service corresponds to the evaluation of the criteria Availability Integrity Confidentiality Traceability for this application or infrastructure service.<\/p><p>EE: Enlarged Europe<\/p><p>KPI : Key Performance Indicator<\/p><p>« <strong>Minor Incident<\/strong>» mean all effect altering the operation pf the Deliverable, all degradation or any non-conformity of the Deliverables, but does not prevent the normal use of the Deliverable.<\/p><p><strong>« Major Incident » <\/strong>means any absence of function, non-compliance of the Deliverables with the Technical and Functional Specifications and/or with the Documentation, any error, bug, hidden defect or malfunction, any discrepancy or inadequacy of performance with the Technical and Functional Specifications and/or with the business best practices.<\/p><p>NSC: National Sales Company<\/p><p>NV: New Vehicle<\/p><p>PR: Spare Parts<\/p><p>UC: Used Car <\/p><p>UI: User Interface (Series of screens, pages &amp; visual)<\/p><p>VIN: Vehicle Identification Number<\/p><p>PSA: Part of Stellantis Group responsible for the following Brands: Peugeot, Citroen, Opel, Vauxhall and DS<\/p><p>FCA: Part of Stellantis Group responsible for the following Brands: Fiat, Fiat Professional, Alfa Romeo, Lancia, Abarth, Jeep, Chrysler, Dodge, Ram<\/p><p>Other Stellantis Brands: MOPAR, Eurorepar Car Service, Free2Move, Leasys, Spoticar, and several others<\/p>", "text": "AFS: After sales\nAI: Artificial intelligence\nAR: Authorized Repairer – also used the word “dealer”\nAssigned stock: Vehicle owned by a dealer\nBC: Business Coach\n« Blocking Incident» means any absence of function, non-compliance of the Deliverables with the Technical and Functional Specifications and/or with the Documentation, causing indifferently the complete or partial unavailability of an essential function of a Deliverables and/or a problem of consistency and / or integrity of the Data.\nCEC : Customer Engagement Center\nDMS: Dealer Management System \n« DICT  or AICT» : The AICT of an application or an infrastructure service corresponds to the evaluation of the criteria Availability Integrity Confidentiality Traceability for this application or infrastructure service.\nEE: Enlarged Europe\nKPI : Key Performance Indicator\n« Minor Incident» mean all effect altering the operation pf the Deliverable, all degradation or any non-conformity of the Deliverables, but does not prevent the normal use of the Deliverable.\n« Major Incident » means any absence of function, non-compliance of the Deliverables with the Technical and Functional Specifications and/or with the Documentation, any error, bug, hidden defect or malfunction, any discrepancy or inadequacy of performance with the Technical and Functional Specifications and/or with the business best practices.\nNSC: National Sales Company\nNV: New Vehicle\nPR: Spare Parts\nUC: Used Car \nUI: User Interface (Series of screens, pages & visual)\nVIN: Vehicle Identification Number\nPSA: Part of Stellantis Group responsible for the following Brands: Peugeot, Citroen, Opel, Vauxhall and DS\nFCA: Part of Stellantis Group responsible for the following Brands: Fiat, Fiat Professional, Alfa Romeo, Lancia, Abarth, Jeep, Chrysler, Dodge, Ram\nOther Stellantis Brands: MOPAR, Eurorepar Car Service, Free2Move, Leasys, Spoticar, and several others"}, {"id": "d1-s7", "doc": 1, "title": "Introduction", "html": "<p>To be clear on the need of Stellantis, working sessions have been performed, in order to provide here:  <\/p><p>Elements and explanations of Business, End User and ICT needs.   <\/p><p>Target tool’s mindset/way of working.  <\/p><p>Assessment criteria which are key for Stellantis; to select the best tool but as well. <\/p>", "text": "To be clear on the need of Stellantis, working sessions have been performed, in order to provide here:  \nElements and explanations of Business, End User and ICT needs.   \nTarget tool’s mindset/way of working.  \nAssessment criteria which are key for Stellantis; to select the best tool but as well. "}, {"id": "d1-s8", "doc": 1, "title": "“High level” features of the Platform", "html": "<p>The tool is an essential point of access to network animation. <\/p><p>Access to the tool should be made using the STELLANTIS user IDs.  A link to the new portal tool will be  included in other Stellantis main activity portals (Service Box, Service Box Muti brand, C1ST, Link Entry, and to 3’rd party vendor applications.<\/p><p>For a better User eXperience, SSO connectivity is the target. A user should not have to retype user and password to access from/within this portal to other Stellantis tools that are SSO enabled.<\/p><p>The tool/interface needs to support responsive design, enabling the users any device experience.<\/p><p>The tool needs to be accessible anytime.<\/p><p>Multilingual: The tool must be available in the language of all the countries. The user will have the tool and therefore the texts translated into his mother tongue by default but can decide to change it if necessary.<\/p><p>Content audience targeting and view. <\/p><p>To quickly adapt to changes in the market and needs, the tool and its development must remain agile.<\/p><p>It will provide a quick access to general and most up-to-date information through a homepage and will then allow to deep dive through specific tabs and accurate contents.<\/p>", "text": "The tool is an essential point of access to network animation. \nAccess to the tool should be made using the STELLANTIS user IDs.  A link to the new portal tool will be  included in other Stellantis main activity portals (Service Box, Service Box Muti brand, C1ST, Link Entry, and to 3’rd party vendor applications.\nFor a better User eXperience, SSO connectivity is the target. A user should not have to retype user and password to access from/within this portal to other Stellantis tools that are SSO enabled.\nThe tool/interface needs to support responsive design, enabling the users any device experience.\nThe tool needs to be accessible anytime.\nMultilingual: The tool must be available in the language of all the countries. The user will have the tool and therefore the texts translated into his mother tongue by default but can decide to change it if necessary.\nContent audience targeting and view. \nTo quickly adapt to changes in the market and needs, the tool and its development must remain agile.\nIt will provide a quick access to general and most up-to-date information through a homepage and will then allow to deep dive through specific tabs and accurate contents."}, {"id": "d1-s9", "doc": 1, "title": "User/Business requirements", "html": "<p>It will be the same Platform for the dealers, corporate staff, and people in charge to animate them but with different features according to the profile.<\/p><p>The solution should offer a smooth and pleasant navigation system. <\/p><p>These following elements describe End User and Business requirements that Stellantis is awaiting from the tool. <\/p>", "text": "It will be the same Platform for the dealers, corporate staff, and people in charge to animate them but with different features according to the profile.\nThe solution should offer a smooth and pleasant navigation system. \nThese following elements describe End User and Business requirements that Stellantis is awaiting from the tool. "}, {"id": "d1-s10", "doc": 1, "title": "Brief", "html": "<p>To ensure the best UX possible, we should expose One Door URL concept which (by authenticating the user) is setting up a Homepage based on the Roles of the user, with relevant and customized content.<\/p><p>Each user may have different needs; thus this homepage can be fully personalized for a better experience of the user: <\/p><p>Position/content of the element can be changed. <\/p><p>Tools/applications can be added in widgets.<\/p><p>Etc.  <\/p><p>Access to different sections of the tool must be possible with one click, regardless of the page displayed. <\/p><p>When necessary, a vertical scrolling system to access the various elements of the displayed page can be set up. In case of vertical scrolling, a button to go back to the top of the page must be present. Also, with corporations owning dealer groups we will require the capability for the dealer user to toggle between ‘allowed’ dealer entities / Dealer id’s.<\/p><p>Whatever the page, it must be possible to return to the home page and this possibility must be visible (dedicated button) <\/p><p>Except for the home page, a system for returning to the previous page must be in place (dedicated button)<\/p><p><img loading=\"lazy\" alt=\"Source document figure\" src=\"data:image/png;base64,\"><\/p>", "text": "To ensure the best UX possible, we should expose One Door URL concept which (by authenticating the user) is setting up a Homepage based on the Roles of the user, with relevant and customized content.\nEach user may have different needs; thus this homepage can be fully personalized for a better experience of the user: \nPosition/content of the element can be changed. \nTools/applications can be added in widgets.\nEtc.  \nAccess to different sections of the tool must be possible with one click, regardless of the page displayed. \nWhen necessary, a vertical scrolling system to access the various elements of the displayed page can be set up. In case of vertical scrolling, a button to go back to the top of the page must be present. Also, with corporations owning dealer groups we will require the capability for the dealer user to toggle between ‘allowed’ dealer entities / Dealer id’s.\nWhatever the page, it must be possible to return to the home page and this possibility must be visible (dedicated button) \nExcept for the home page, a system for returning to the previous page must be in place (dedicated button)\n"}, {"id": "d1-s11", "doc": 1, "title": "PoV Context & RFQ Impacts", "html": "<p>This RFQ includes a Proof of Value (PoV) phase based on the platform technology proposed by the Supplier.<\/p><p>The Supplier shall prepare and deliver a PoV within a one-month timeframe, demonstrating the proposed solution against the business use cases defined by Stellantis.<\/p><p>The primary objective is to enable Stellantis to assess how effectively the proposed platform technology addresses its business and technical requirements, while demonstrating its ability to accelerate digital solution delivery through a flexible, scalable, and maintainable architecture.<\/p><p>As part of the PoV activities, the Supplier shall review the current Stellantis environment and provide recommendations to ensure that the proposed platform can support easy and flexible software integration, while effectively meeting current and future business requirements.<\/p><p>The Supplier shall provide the necessary development framework components and integration approach to demonstrate the ease, flexibility, and effectiveness of adopting the proposed solution within the Stellantis ecosystem. The PoV should clearly highlight the added value of the platform capabilities when applied to real business scenarios.<\/p><p>The PoV shall be delivered as a real, operational portal rather than as a conceptual presentation, wireframe, or static prototype. Suppliers may adopt the architecture they deem most appropriate for the demonstration; <\/p><p>however, the solution must be fully accessible, interactive, and navigable, enabling Stellantis stakeholders to actively explore, test, and evaluate its features and user experience.<\/p><p>The PoV must provide both a technical and visual demonstration of the platform capabilities. It should showcase user journeys, business functionalities, integration opportunities, and overall user experience, while evidencing how the platform supports the identified use cases.<\/p><p>The PoV should be sufficiently detailed to demonstrate the value, flexibility, and capabilities of the proposed platform, while avoiding extensive custom development efforts. The focus should be on illustrating the platform&#x27;s native capabilities and its suitability for Stellantis needs.<\/p><p>The outcomes of the PoV will support Stellantis in selecting the most suitable platform technology. Following the technology selection, which will be formally communicated to the Suppliers, the final RFQ response shall be submitted accordingly.<\/p><p>All PoV activities, deliverables, and related efforts shall be provided free of charge and are intended solely for evaluation purposes. The PoV solution and deliverables are not intended for production use or deployment as the target platform.<\/p><p>.<\/p>", "text": "This RFQ includes a Proof of Value (PoV) phase based on the platform technology proposed by the Supplier.\nThe Supplier shall prepare and deliver a PoV within a one-month timeframe, demonstrating the proposed solution against the business use cases defined by Stellantis.\nThe primary objective is to enable Stellantis to assess how effectively the proposed platform technology addresses its business and technical requirements, while demonstrating its ability to accelerate digital solution delivery through a flexible, scalable, and maintainable architecture.\nAs part of the PoV activities, the Supplier shall review the current Stellantis environment and provide recommendations to ensure that the proposed platform can support easy and flexible software integration, while effectively meeting current and future business requirements.\nThe Supplier shall provide the necessary development framework components and integration approach to demonstrate the ease, flexibility, and effectiveness of adopting the proposed solution within the Stellantis ecosystem. The PoV should clearly highlight the added value of the platform capabilities when applied to real business scenarios.\nThe PoV shall be delivered as a real, operational portal rather than as a conceptual presentation, wireframe, or static prototype. Suppliers may adopt the architecture they deem most appropriate for the demonstration; \nhowever, the solution must be fully accessible, interactive, and navigable, enabling Stellantis stakeholders to actively explore, test, and evaluate its features and user experience.\nThe PoV must provide both a technical and visual demonstration of the platform capabilities. It should showcase user journeys, business functionalities, integration opportunities, and overall user experience, while evidencing how the platform supports the identified use cases.\nThe PoV should be sufficiently detailed to demonstrate the value, flexibility, and capabilities of the proposed platform, while avoiding extensive custom development efforts. The focus should be on illustrating the platform's native capabilities and its suitability for Stellantis needs.\nThe outcomes of the PoV will support Stellantis in selecting the most suitable platform technology. Following the technology selection, which will be formally communicated to the Suppliers, the final RFQ response shall be submitted accordingly.\nAll PoV activities, deliverables, and related efforts shall be provided free of charge and are intended solely for evaluation purposes. The PoV solution and deliverables are not intended for production use or deployment as the target platform.\n."}, {"id": "d1-s12", "doc": 1, "title": "Application Bookmark (incl. Single Sign On)", "html": "<p>This new platform will allow Stellantis to deliver an All-in-One Portal integrating as smooth as possible applications / features/ widgets in there to allow perfectly clear UI/UX.<\/p><p>In order to allow dealers to easily find the different applications that Stellantis provide them to perform their daily activities, the dealer portal will include an application bookmark section where dealer and Stellantis users will find links to these applications. <\/p><p>The applications proposed to the user should be configurable by Stellantis and based on the user profile.<\/p><p>The portal should allow for single sign on access to these applications, to prevent the need for the users to enter multiple times their user and password, in the case that these applications are also including the single sign on capability.<\/p>", "text": "This new platform will allow Stellantis to deliver an All-in-One Portal integrating as smooth as possible applications / features/ widgets in there to allow perfectly clear UI/UX.\nIn order to allow dealers to easily find the different applications that Stellantis provide them to perform their daily activities, the dealer portal will include an application bookmark section where dealer and Stellantis users will find links to these applications. \nThe applications proposed to the user should be configurable by Stellantis and based on the user profile.\nThe portal should allow for single sign on access to these applications, to prevent the need for the users to enter multiple times their user and password,
