"html": "<p>The Material 3 Design Kit streamlines UI design by providing ready-made components, styles, and themes for consistent, modern, and accessible interfaces.<\/p><p>The Material 3 Design Kit is a set of UI design resources created by Google to help designers and developers build user interfaces that follow the Material 3 (Material You) design system.<\/p><p>It includes<\/p><p><strong>Figma-based UI kit<\/strong>: Pre-built components, layouts, and templates<\/p><p><strong>Color system tools<\/strong>: Dynamic color palettes that adapt to user preferences<\/p><p><strong>Typography styles<\/strong>: Updated scalable and accessible font guidelines<\/p><p><strong>Components<\/strong>: Buttons, cards, sliders, dialogs, etc., with modern styling and behavior<\/p><p><strong>Elevation, shape, and motion design<\/strong>: To guide depth and interaction feedback<\/p><p>https://m3.material.io<\/p>", "text": "The Material 3 Design Kit streamlines UI design by providing ready-made components, styles, and themes for consistent, modern, and accessible interfaces.\nThe Material 3 Design Kit is a set of UI design resources created by Google to help designers and developers build user interfaces that follow the Material 3 (Material You) design system.\nIt includes\nFigma-based UI kit: Pre-built components, layouts, and templates\nColor system tools: Dynamic color palettes that adapt to user preferences\nTypography styles: Updated scalable and accessible font guidelines\nComponents: Buttons, cards, sliders, dialogs, etc., with modern styling and behavior\nElevation, shape, and motion design: To guide depth and interaction feedback\nhttps://m3.material.io"}, {"id": "d2-s21", "doc": 2, "title": "Multilingual Support", "html": "<p>To provide a seamless and personalized user experience, our system automatically selects the appropriate language for both anonymous and authenticated users. The selection process ensures that users see content in a language that best fits their location, preferences, or previous selections.<\/p><p>By May 2025, <strong>the platform<\/strong><strong> shal<\/strong><strong>l support 33 languages<\/strong> across 38 Markets defined by Stellantis.<\/p><p>The key point to note is that, <strong>while the platform is enabled<\/strong><strong>/capable<\/strong><strong> to support above languages<\/strong>, below 2 conditions need to be sufficed:<\/p><p><strong>The<\/strong><strong> <\/strong><strong>language needs to be supported by Adobe AEM<\/strong><\/p><p><strong>T<\/strong><strong>he <\/strong><strong>localized content and labels <\/strong><strong>in above languages need to be Authored by Stellantis.<\/strong><\/p><p><strong>1. Anonymous Users (e.g., Login Page Visitors)<\/strong><\/p><p>When an anonymous user visits the site, we detect their <strong>browser language<\/strong>.<\/p><p>If the browser language is supported by our system, content is shown in that language.<\/p><p>If not, we default to <strong>English<\/strong>.<\/p><p>Users always have the option to <strong>manually change the language<\/strong>, which immediately updates the content.<\/p><p><strong>Goal:<\/strong> Offer a user-friendly experience from the first interaction, without requiring login.<\/p><p><strong>2. Authenticated Users (Logged-In Experience)<\/strong><\/p><p>For logged-in users, we tailor the language based on their <strong>user profile and market context<\/strong>.<\/p><p>We prioritize language selection as follows:<\/p><p><strong>User&#x27;s saved preference<\/strong> (from previous visits or GDRP settings),<\/p><p><strong>Language from their account profile<\/strong> (authorization system)<\/p><p><strong>Language chosen during login<\/strong><\/p><p><strong>English Language or the language marked as preferred for the market, <\/strong>in the language master data.<\/p><p>This process ensures users consistently see content in their <strong>preferred and market-relevant language<\/strong>.<\/p><p>The below flow chart outlines the logic for determining the user interface language across anonymous and authenticated experiences. Language resolution is driven by browser settings, user context, and predefined language master.<\/p><p><img loading=\"lazy\" alt=\"Source document figure\" src=\"data:image/png;base64,\"><\/p>", "text": "To provide a seamless and personalized user experience, our system automatically selects the appropriate language for both anonymous and authenticated users. The selection process ensures that users see content in a language that best fits their location, preferences, or previous selections.\nBy May 2025, the platform shall support 33 languages across 38 Markets defined by Stellantis.\nThe key point to note is that, while the platform is enabled/capable to support above languages, below 2 conditions need to be sufficed:\nThe language needs to be supported by Adobe AEM\nThe localized content and labels in above languages need to be Authored by Stellantis.\n1. Anonymous Users (e.g., Login Page Visitors)\nWhen an anonymous user visits the site, we detect their browser language.\nIf the browser language is supported by our system, content is shown in that language.\nIf not, we default to English.\nUsers always have the option to manually change the language, which immediately updates the content.\nGoal: Offer a user-friendly experience from the first interaction, without requiring login.\n2. Authenticated Users (Logged-In Experience)\nFor logged-in users, we tailor the language based on their user profile and market context.\nWe prioritize language selection as follows:\nUser's saved preference (from previous visits or GDRP settings),\nLanguage from their account profile (authorization system)\nLanguage chosen during login\nEnglish Language or the language marked as preferred for the market, in the language master data.\nThis process ensures users consistently see content in their preferred and market-relevant language.\nThe below flow chart outlines the logic for determining the user interface language across anonymous and authenticated experiences. Language resolution is driven by browser settings, user context, and predefined language master.\n"}, {"id": "d2-s22", "doc": 2, "title": "Anonymous Pages (e.g., GDRP Login/User Lookup Page)", "html": "<p><strong>Flow Summary:<\/strong>Retrieve the browser&#x27;s locale (navigator.language).Check if the locale language exists in the <strong>AEM-supported language list<\/strong> (non-region specific). <\/p><p><strong>If yes<\/strong>: Set the language to the browser locale.<\/p><p><strong>If no<\/strong>: Default to <strong>English<\/strong>.<\/p><p>If the user changes the language manually, override the above with the <strong>user-selected language<\/strong>.<\/p><p><strong>Key Points:<\/strong><\/p><p>Language list is sourced from AEM’s non-regional configuration.<\/p><p>This logic applies only to unauthenticated users (pre-login state).<\/p><p>Manual selection always overrides auto-detected values.<\/p>", "text": "Flow Summary:Retrieve the browser's locale (navigator.language).Check if the locale language exists in the AEM-supported language list (non-region specific). \nIf yes: Set the language to the browser locale.\nIf no: Default to English.\nIf the user changes the language manually, override the above with the user-selected language.\nKey Points:\nLanguage list is sourced from AEM’s non-regional configuration.\nThis logic applies only to unauthenticated users (pre-login state).\nManual selection always overrides auto-detected values."}, {"id": "d2-s23", "doc": 2, "title": "Authenticated Pages (Post-login and Secure Areas)", "html": "<p><strong>Flow Summary:<\/strong><\/p><p>Determine the user&#x27;s <strong>market context<\/strong>: <\/p><p>Corporate User → User.Market<\/p><p>Dealer User → Dealer.Market<\/p><p>Fetch the <strong>AEM-supported languages<\/strong> for the identified market.<\/p><p>Language selection is based on the following precedence: <\/p><p><strong>User’s saved preference from GDPR<\/strong> (if it&#x27;s valid for the market)<\/p><p><strong>Language from the Authorization system<\/strong> (must match the market’s language list)<\/p><p><strong>Language selected on the User Lookup page<\/strong> (must match the market list)<\/p><p>If none of the above match the market&#x27;s supported list, fall back logic will apply which either picks up English or the preferred language for the market.<\/p><p><strong>Key Data Sources:<\/strong><\/p><p><strong>GDPR preference store<\/strong> – set during prior sessions<\/p><p><strong>Auth system<\/strong> – typically pulled from user identity/token claims<\/p><p><strong>User Lookup page selection<\/strong> – language explicitly chosen during login<\/p><p><strong>Dependencies:<\/strong><\/p><p>Language definitions/list per market<\/p><p>User context (corporate vs. dealer)<\/p><p>Browser locale (for anonymous sessions only)<\/p><p>Scenario 1: A dealer user with browser locale set to “italian” from Italy market<\/p><p>Assumption, “Italian” is a supported language in AEM for Italy market and as well as for the login screen.<\/p><p>The login screen shall load in “Italian”<\/p><p>The authenticated pages will also show in “Italian” and with “Italian” content.<\/p><p>Scenario 2: A dealer user with browser locale set to “Hindi” from Italy market.<\/p><p>Assumption, “Hindi” is not a supported language in AEM for Italy market and as well as for the login screen.<\/p><p>Since, Hindi is not supported, <\/p><p>The login screen shall load in “English”, the default language<\/p><p>The authenticated pages shall load in <\/p><p>“Italian”, if the preferred language as per the language master for Italy market<\/p><p>“English”, if the preferred language is not set or “English” itself is set as the preferred language for Italy market.<\/p><p>Scenario 3: A corporate user with browser locale set to “Italian” from Italy market and doesn’t endorse.<\/p><p>Assumption, “Italian” is a supported language in AEM for Italy market.<\/p><p>The login screen shall load in Italian<\/p><p>The authenticated pages shall also load in Italian.<\/p><p>Scenario 4: A corporate user with browser locale set to “Italian” from Italy market and tries to endorse a “Belgium” dealer.<\/p><p>Assumptions:<\/p><p>Italian is supported in AEM<\/p><p>Languages supported in Belgium market are German (preferred), French and English<\/p><p>The login screen shall load in Italian.<\/p><p>The authenticated pages, since the user is endorsing “Belgium” dealer,<\/p><p>Pages will load in German.<\/p><p>If user additionally wants to check the English content, then user shall need to go to User-Preferences tab and change the login preference to Belgium dealer, and set the preferred language to English.<\/p>", "text": "Flow Summary:\nDetermine the user's market context: \nCorporate User → User.Market\nDealer User → Dealer.Market\nFetch the AEM-supported languages for the identified market.\nLanguage selection is based on the following precedence: \nUser’s saved preference from GDPR (if it's valid for the market)\nLanguage from the Authorization system (must match the market’s language list)\nLanguage selected on the User Lookup page (must match the market list)\nIf none of the above match the market's supported list, fall back logic will apply which either picks up English or the preferred language for the market.\nKey Data Sources:\nGDPR preference store – set during prior sessions\nAuth system – typically pulled from user identity/token claims\nUser Lookup page selection – language explicitly chosen during login\nDependencies:\nLanguage definitions/list per market\nUser context (corporate vs. dealer)\nBrowser locale (for anonymous sessions only)\nScenario 1: A dealer user with browser locale set to “italian” from Italy market\nAssumption, “Italian” is a supported language in AEM for Italy market and as well as for the login screen.\nThe login screen shall load in “Italian”\nThe authenticated pages will also show in “Italian” and with “Italian” content.\nScenario 2: A dealer user with browser locale set to “Hindi” from Italy market.\nAssumption, “Hindi” is not a supported language in AEM for Italy market and as well as for the login screen.\nSince, Hindi is not supported, \nThe login screen shall load in “English”, the default language\nThe authenticated pages shall load in \n“Italian”, if the preferred language as per the language master for Italy market\n“English”, if the preferred language is not set or “English” itself is set as the preferred language for Italy market.\nScenario 3: A corporate user with browser locale set to “Italian” from Italy market and doesn’t endorse.\nAssumption, “Italian” is a supported language in AEM for Italy market.\nThe login screen shall load in Italian\nThe authenticated pages shall also load in Italian.\nScenario 4: A corporate user with browser locale set to “Italian” from Italy market and tries to endorse a “Belgium” dealer.\nAssumptions:\nItalian is supported in AEM\nLanguages supported in Belgium market are German (preferred), French and English\nThe login screen shall load in Italian.\nThe authenticated pages, since the user is endorsing “Belgium” dealer,\nPages will load in German.\nIf user additionally wants to check the English content, then user shall need to go to User-Preferences tab and change the login preference to Belgium dealer, and set the preferred language to English."}, {"id": "d2-s24", "doc": 2, "title": "Design Authority Gate Review", "html": "<p>Before starting any new Application Development, it is strongly recommended to start the Design Authority Gate Review Process at the very earliest to avoid any delays. Without the initial gate approval, most of the ICT organization like Cloud or On-prem Infrastructure, Network, DevOps, Security (IAM) etc. will not allocate their resources for build process or consultation.<\/p><p>One of the important groups – GDRP Governance Team – will also need to be engaged in Gate Review process if the Application is intended to be integrated with GDRP Portal Capabilities.<\/p><p>Getting familiarized with Architecture Gate Review Process is critical before introducing any new application, tools, technology, integration patterns, COTS product etc. into the Stellantis IT landscape to make sure that the initiative is in alignment with Enterprise Strategy. <\/p><p>Enterprise Architecture - Home<\/p><p>It is the responsibility of the Architecture Advisory Board to approve the Application Delivery Technical Stack.<\/p>", "text": "Before starting any new Application Development, it is strongly recommended to start the Design Authority Gate Review Process at the very earliest to avoid any delays. Without the initial gate approval, most of the ICT organization like Cloud or On-prem Infrastructure, Network, DevOps, Security (IAM) etc. will not allocate their resources for build process or consultation.\nOne of the important groups – GDRP Governance Team – will also need to be engaged in Gate Review process if the Application is intended to be integrated with GDRP Portal Capabilities.\nGetting familiarized with Architecture Gate Review Process is critical before introducing any new application, tools, technology, integration patterns, COTS product etc. into the Stellantis IT landscape to make sure that the initiative is in alignment with Enterprise Strategy. \nEnterprise Architecture - Home\nIt is the responsibility of the Architecture Advisory Board to approve the Application Delivery Technical Stack."}, {"id": "d2-s25", "doc": 2, "title": "Cloud COE", "html": "<p>While GDRP has adopted AWS as the hosting platform for deploying the SDK components, any existing application will integrate with SDK (Portal Capabilities) as described in section 4 earlier. These existing applications could be hosted within Stellantis controlled infrastructure or externally hosted vendor solutions.<\/p><p>If a Business Group want to create a Greenfield application to be integrated with GDRP platform, ICT dev team may choose to adopt Stellantis supported cloud service provider to deploy their application. Please refer to following Cloud COE knowledge base to begin onboarding process for Cloud Infrastructure Build.<\/p><p>Cloud &amp; SW Engineering - Home<\/p><p><strong>Please Note:<\/strong><strong> <\/strong>Regardless of the hosting environment – cloud or on-premises, the application’s web pages <strong>must be reachable from Internet<\/strong>. Please communicate this very clearly to the cloud/network team.<\/p>", "text": "While GDRP has adopted AWS as the hosting platform for deploying the SDK components, any existing application will integrate with SDK (Portal Capabilities) as described in section 4 earlier. These existing applications could be hosted within Stellantis controlled infrastructure or externally hosted vendor solutions.\nIf a Business Group want to create a Greenfield application to be integrated with GDRP platform, ICT dev team may choose to adopt Stellantis supported cloud service provider to deploy their application. Please refer to following Cloud COE knowledge base to begin onboarding process for Cloud Infrastructure Build.\nCloud & SW Engineering - Home\nPlease Note: Regardless of the hosting environment – cloud or on-premises, the application’s web pages must be reachable from Internet. Please communicate this very clearly to the cloud/network team."}, {"id": "d2-s26", "doc": 2, "title": "DevSecOps", "html": "<p>If the application is hosted on Stellantis Controlled Infrastructure (cloud or on-prem), it is advisable to manage the code base &amp; deployment using Stellantis DevOps Repo &amp; Pipeline.<\/p><p>GDRP has adopted Stellantis Enterprise DevSecOps framework for development, build, code quality control &amp; deployment to the target hosting environment. Following section leverages various common components/templates &amp; standards as defined by Enterprise DevOps Governance Team at: https://github.intra.fcagroup.com/pages/Enterprise-Devops/Stellantis-DevOps/index.html<\/p>", "text": "If the application is hosted on Stellantis Controlled Infrastructure (cloud or on-prem), it is advisable to manage the code base & deployment using Stellantis DevOps Repo & Pipeline.\nGDRP has adopted Stellantis Enterprise DevSecOps framework for development, build, code quality control & deployment to the target hosting environment. Following section leverages various common components/templates & standards as defined by Enterprise DevOps Governance Team at: https://github.intra.fcagroup.com/pages/Enterprise-Devops/Stellantis-DevOps/index.html"}, {"id": "d2-s27", "doc": 2, "title": "GitHub Repository Naming Convention", "html": "<p>In order to avoid discrepancy between the content of this section and the standards defined Enterprise DevSecOps team: Integrators are requested to follow the Repo Creation &amp; Naming Convention documented at Enterprise DevSecOps New Repository Creation.<\/p>", "text": "In order to avoid discrepancy between the content of this section and the standards defined Enterprise DevSecOps team: Integrators are requested to follow the Repo Creation & Naming Convention documented at Enterprise DevSecOps New Repository Creation."}, {"id": "d2-s28", "doc": 2, "title": "GitHub Repository Setup", "html": "<p>Step 1 – Create AMS ID by following the instructions at: Create AMS ID<\/p><p>Step 2 – Create New Repo by following the instructions at: New Repo Creation OR New Repo Creation<\/p>", "text": "Step 1 – Create AMS ID by following the instructions at: Create AMS ID\nStep 2 – Create New Repo by following the instructions at: New Repo Creation OR New Repo Creation"}, {"id": "d2-s29", "doc": 2, "title": "Pipeline Setup & Code Promotion Flow", "html": "<p>Once the repo is created and the target deployment environment is created, the development team shall engage Stellantis Enterprise DevOps Team by following the process at DevSecOps Automated Pipeline to define &amp; design (in case of a new target deployment pattern) and configure pipeline to engage various CICD Quality Checks enabled for the deployment pattern (tech stack) so that a secured build can be packaged &amp; deployed to the target environment.<\/p><p>While there are various “target deployment” pattern defined by Stellantis Enterprise DevSecOps team, GDRP is primarily using the JFROG as the Artifactory and deploying the package to Container Runtime Environment on AWS ECS Fargate following the instructions at AWS ECR Deployment Pattern<\/p><p>Following diagram depicts the actor and the activities at high level involved in developing the various components of GDRP platform – primarily UI component, API component &amp; AEM Component as a code.<\/p><p><img loading=\"lazy\" alt=\"Source document figure\" src=\"data:image/png;base64,\"><\/p><p>Figure 33- Enterprise CICD Toolkit Adoption - GDRP Developed Capabilites<\/p><p>Developers from GDRP Component Engineering Team shall make use of Stellantis GitHub Instance integrated development tool to develop and push the code to various branches mapped to different environment.<\/p><p>Once the pipeline has been configured by Stellantis DevSecOps Admin for the given repo &amp; target deployment environment, it is the responsibility of Developer to appropriately configure the pipeline configuration (yaml) file so that the build &amp; deploy process can go through successfully.<\/p><p>Stellantis DevSecOps Admin must have configured all mandatory quality checks “tool chain” for the given Pipeline template. GDRP platform components make use of following tool chain<\/p><p>Java Code Coverage - JUnit<\/p><p>Overall Code Quality Check - SonarQube<\/p><p>Vulnerability/Security Check - Checkmarx <\/p><p>Developer has complete visibility into deployment status by virtue of OOB feature of GitHub &amp; also various quality reports as defined by pipeline &amp; configured by DevSecOps team.<\/p><p>GDRP also has a SaaS instance for AEM Authoring Component which is being used for Content Authoring targeted for GDRP Platform end users. GDRP is leveraging AEMaaCS (AEM as a Cloud Service) model for CMS solution.<\/p><p>AEMaaCS configuration/customization shall be pushed through Stellantis Enterprise CICD DevSecOps pipeline leveraging defined &amp; designed quality gates before pushing the code through SaaS native DevOps pipeline built into AEMaaCS.<\/p><p>Following diagram depicts the actor and the activities at high level showcasing the autonomy in the development of Business Group specific functionalities/application development independent of the GDRP platform. To avoid conflicts &amp; resource contention across the BGs, every Business Group shall have its own independently billed Deployment/Hosting environment. While this will bring in the autonomy of deployment and scale; the microservices &amp; micro frontend architecture will enable service-based component sharing with loose coupling adhering to the SDK concept with “governed” specifications/contracts. <\/p><p><img loading=\"lazy\" alt=\"Source document figure\" src=\"data:image/png;base64,\"><\/p><p>Figure 34- GDRP &amp; Other BG (for e.g. SRP) development co-existence<\/p>", "text": "Once the repo is created and the target deployment environment is created, the development team shall engage Stellantis Enterprise DevOps Team by following the process at DevSecOps Automated Pipeline to define & design (in case of a new target deployment pattern) and configure pipeline to engage various CICD Quality Checks enabled for the deployment pattern (tech stack) so that a secured build can be packaged & deployed to the target environment.\nWhile there are various “target deployment” pattern defined by Stellantis Enterprise DevSecOps team, GDRP is primarily using the JFROG as the Artifactory and deploying the package to Container Runtime Environment on AWS ECS Fargate following the instructions at AWS ECR Deployment Pattern\nFollowing diagram depicts the actor and the activities at high level involved in developing the various components of GDRP platform – primarily UI component, API component & AEM Component as a code.\n\nFigure 33- Enterprise CICD Toolkit Adoption - GDRP Developed Capabilites\nDevelopers from GDRP Component Engineering Team shall make use of Stellantis GitHub Instance integrated development tool to develop and push the code to various branches mapped to different environment.\nOnce the pipeline has been configured by Stellantis DevSecOps Admin for the given repo & target deployment environment, it is the responsibility of Developer to appropriately configure the pipeline configuration (yaml) file so that the build & deploy process can go through successfully.\nStellantis DevSecOps Admin must have configured all mandatory quality checks “tool chain” for the given Pipeline template. GDRP platform components make use of following tool chain\nJava Code Coverage - JUnit\nOverall Code Quality Check - SonarQube\nVulnerability/Security Check - Checkmarx \nDeveloper has complete visibility into deployment status by virtue of OOB feature of GitHub & also various quality reports as defined by pipeline & configured by DevSecOps team.\nGDRP also has a SaaS instance for AEM Authoring Component which is being used for Content Authoring targeted for GDRP Platform end users. GDRP is leveraging AEMaaCS (AEM as a Cloud Service) model for CMS solution.\nAEMaaCS configuration/customization shall be pushed through Stellantis Enterprise CICD DevSecOps pipeline leveraging defined & designed quality gates before pushing the code through SaaS native DevOps pipeline built into AEMaaCS.\nFollowing diagram depicts the actor and the activities at high level showcasing the autonomy in the development of Business Group specific functionalities/application development independent of the GDRP platform. To avoid conflicts & resource contention across the BGs, every Business Group shall have its own independently billed Deployment/Hosting environment. While this will bring in the autonomy of deployment and scale; the microservices & micro frontend architecture will enable service-based component sharing with loose coupling adhering to the SDK concept with “governed” specifications/contracts. \n\nFigure 34- GDRP & Other BG (for e.g. SRP) development co-existence"}, {"id": "d2-s30", "doc": 2, "title": "SDK Adoption Lifecycle", "html": "<p>Until the GDRP Governance Team/Portal gets defined, this document shall be a evolving repository to enrich the SDK adoption methodology as more application integration use cases are brought forward to Gate Review Process.<\/p><p><img loading=\"lazy\" alt=\"Source document figure\" src=\"data:image/png;base64,\"><\/p><p>Figure 35-SDK Adoption: Application Development<\/p><p><img loading=\"lazy\" alt=\"Source document figure\" src=\"data:image/png;base64,\"><\/p><p>Figure 36-SDK Adoption: Application Onboarding<\/p>", "text": "Until the GDRP Governance Team/Portal gets defined, this document shall be a evolving repository to enrich the SDK adoption methodology as more application integration use cases are brought forward to Gate Review Process.\n\nFigure 35-SDK Adoption: Application Development\n\nFigure 36-SDK Adoption: Application Onboarding"}, {"id": "d2-s31", "doc": 2, "title": "Common Component Library", "html": "<p>To accelerate the integration with GDRP Portal Capabilities, there are few Common Components that has been referred in Section 4. This section focusses on each component whether it is a Web component like Header &amp; Footer or API component like Notification service or SaaS Infrastructure component like AEM for Content Management or Akamai for Content Caching.<\/p>", "text": "To accelerate the integration with GDRP Portal Capabilities, there are few Common Components that has been referred in Section 4. This section focusses on each component whether it is a Web component like Header & Footer or API component like Notification service or SaaS Infrastructure component like AEM for Content Management or Akamai for Content Caching."}, {"id": "d2-s32", "doc": 2, "title": "Adobe Experience Manager – Content Management Solution", "html": "<p>GDRP platform leverages SaaS deployment model of Adobe Experience Manager also referred to as AEMaaCS (AEM as a Cloud Service). GDRP has enabled many back-office Content Management capabilities for the Portal Administrator Users. For fulfilling most of these functions, application team will coordinate with their respective Business Author who will have access to GDRP platform’s AEM Authoring Instance for content authoring. For creating new AEM component – GDRP AEM development team will be engaged as explained earlier in section 4.1.1 (API driven widget development lifecycle).<\/p><p>There is a detailed guide shared with Business Authors and Content Administrator which enables them to fulfil many of the functions to deliver the back-office capabilities.<\/p><p>Any new application that needs to be onboarded onto GDRP menu can do so by getting their SSO Split Proxied URL authored in AEM as shown below:<\/p><p><img loading=\"lazy\" alt=\"Source document figure\" src=\"data:image/png;base64,\"><\/p><p>Figure 37-Hierarichal Menu Layout<\/p><p><img loading=\"lazy\" alt=\"Source document figure\" src=\"data:image/png;base64,\"><\/p><p>Figure 38-Level 1 configuration<\/p><p><img loading=\"lazy\" alt=\"Source document figure\" src=\"data:image/png;base64,\"><\/p><p>Figure 39-Level 2 configuration<em> <\/em><\/p><p><img loading=\"lazy\" alt=\"Source document figure\" src=\"data:image/png;base64,\"><\/p><p>Figure 40-Level 3 - App Link display label &amp; URL<\/p>", "text": "GDRP platform leverages SaaS deployment model of Adobe Experience Manager also referred to as AEMaaCS (AEM as a Cloud Service). GDRP has enabled many back-office Content Management capabilities for the Portal Administrator Users. For fulfilling most of these functions, application team will coordinate with their respective Business Author who will have access to GDRP platform’s AEM Authoring Instance for content authoring. For creating new AEM component – GDRP AEM development team will be engaged as explained earlier in section 4.1.1 (API driven widget development lifecycle).\nThere is a detailed guide shared with Business Authors and Content Administrator which enables them to fulfil many of the functions to deliver the back-office capabilities.\nAny new application that needs to be onboarded onto GDRP menu can do so by getting their SSO Split Proxied URL authored in AEM as shown below:\n\nFigure 37-Hierarichal Menu Layout\n\nFigure 38-Level 1 configuration\n\nFigure 39-Level 2 configuration \n\nFigure 40-Level 3 - App Link display label & URL"}, {"id": "d2-s33", "doc": 2, "title": "Header Footer Web Component", "html": "<p>GDRP platform has adopted Micro Frontend style web embeddable UI component sharing strategy. The components are shared at following location:<\/p><p>https://test.thedealerexperience.stellantis.com/sdk/test/elements/main.js<\/p><p>https://test.thedealerexperience.stellantis.com/sdk/test/elements/polyfills.js<\/p><p>https://test.thedealerexperience.stellantis.com/sdk/test/elements/styles.css<\/p><p>A sample test code is also available at https://test.thedealerexperience.stellantis.com/sdk/test/elements/test.html<\/p><p>Considering the relative path suggestion, 3rd party application should load above JS &amp; CSS files as /sdk/test/elements/main.js; /sdk/test/elements/pollyfills.js &amp; /sdk/test/elements/styles.css. When 3rd party pages will load with relative path via split proxy, the GDRP portal domain will prefix to these relative paths and these JS &amp; CSS will load successfully on end user client browser.<\/p><p>Next place following 2 HTML div tags in omnipresence UI component (dependent upon UI tech of 3rd party web application) as demonstrated in sample test.html code.<\/p><p>&lt;div class=&quot;gdrp-application&quot;&gt;<\/p><p>&lt;gdrp-header id=&quot;header&quot;&gt;&lt;/gdrp-header&gt;<\/p><p>  &lt;/div&gt;<\/p><p>&lt;div class=&quot;gdrp-application&quot;&gt;<\/p><p>    &lt;gdrp-footer id=&quot;footer&quot;&gt;&lt;/gdrp-footer&gt;<\/p><p>&lt;/div&gt;<\/p><p>If the SSO between Split Proxied URL &amp; GDRP Platform is successful, all Header Functionality will automatically populated data for the user identity logged-in to GDRP portal, there by achieving the unified experience of 3rd party web application integrated with GDRP UI framework on client side.<\/p><p>Please note that this component is not meant for server side include. This common component leverages a client-side orchestration architecture a.k.a. Micro frontend.<\/p>", "text": "GDRP platform has adopted Micro Frontend style web embeddable UI component sharing strategy. The components are shared at following location:\nhttps://test.thedealerexperience.stellantis.com/sdk/test/elements/main.js\nhttps://test.thedealerexperience.stellantis.com/sdk/test/elements/polyfills.js\nhttps://test.thedealerexperience.stellantis.com/sdk/test/elements/styles.css\nA sample test code is also available at https://test.thedealerexperience.stellantis.com/sdk/test/elements/test.html\nConsidering the relative path suggestion, 3rd party application should load above JS & CSS files as /sdk/test/elements/main.js; /sdk/test/elements/pollyfills.js & /sdk/test/elements/styles.css. When 3rd party pages will load with relative path via split proxy, the GDRP portal domain will prefix to these relative paths and these JS & CSS will load successfully on end user client browser.\nNext place following 2 HTML div tags in omnipresence UI component (dependent upon UI tech of 3rd party web application) as demonstrated in sample test.html code.\n<div class=\"gdrp-application\">\n<gdrp-header id=\"header\"><\/gdrp-header>\n  <\/div>\n<div class=\"gdrp-application\">\n    <gdrp-footer id=\"footer\"><\/gdrp-footer>\n<\/div>\nIf the SSO between Split Proxied URL & GDRP Platform is successful, all Header Functionality will automatically populated data for the user identity logged-in to GDRP portal, there by achieving the unified experience of 3rd party web application integrated with GDRP UI framework on client side.\nPlease note that this component is not meant for server side include. This common component leverages a client-side orchestration architecture a.k.a. Micro frontend."}, {"id": "d2-s34", "doc": 2, "title": "API", "html": "<p>GDRP platform has leveraged Stellantis Enterprise API Gateway solution – IBM API Connect (APIC) for exposing common APIs. Application team must understand the API standards &amp; guidelines for onboarding on APIC by visiting the information published at API, Integration and Data Platforms knowledge repository.<\/p><p>GDRP has enabled following feature from platform as API.<\/p>", "text": "GDRP platform has leveraged Stellantis Enterprise API Gateway solution – IBM API Connect (APIC) for exposing common APIs. Application team must understand the API standards & guidelines for onboarding on APIC by visiting the information published at API, Integration and Data Platforms knowledge repository.\nGDRP has enabled following feature from platform as API."}, {"id": "d2-s35", "doc": 2, "title": "Notification/Alerts", "html": "<p>One of the functions which is omnipresent in GDRP portal UI is the Notification feature in the Header Component as shown below:<\/p><p><img loading=\"lazy\" alt=\"Source document figure\" src=\"data:image/png;base64,\"><\/p><p>Figure 41-Notification feature of Portal<\/p><p>This feature delivers core Portal capability of capturing end users’ attention in case any alerts need to be pushed to end user for their action. Among many use cases, it is triggered when new contents are pushed to the user, a comment posted on article is like etc.<\/p><p>While this feature currently captures back-office actions &amp; activities on published articles, it can be exposed as API so that various Business Application/Processes can also push their alerts in this common portal capabilities.<\/p><p>&lt;Once this API is available on APIC for subscription, application team can consume the swagger documentation to integrate with this Portal capability&gt;<\/p><p><strong>PLEASE NOTE<\/strong>: If there is a need for exposing other Portal capabilities as APIs, more details about them will be added in subsections of 7.3 when they become available on APIC.<\/p>", "text": "One of the functions which is omnipresent in GDRP portal UI is the Notification feature in the Header Component as shown below:\n\nFigure 41-Notification feature of Portal\nThis feature delivers core Portal capability of capturing end users’ attention in case any alerts need to be pushed to end user for their action. Among many use cases, it is triggered when new contents are pushed to the user, a comment posted on article is like etc.\nWhile this feature currently captures back-office actions & activities on published articles, it can be exposed as API so that various Business Application/Processes can also push their alerts in this common portal capabilities.\n<Once this API is available on APIC for subscription, application team can consume the swagger documentation to integrate with this Portal capability>\nPLEASE NOTE: If there is a need for exposing other Portal capabilities as APIs, more details about them will be added in subsections of 7.3 when they become available on APIC."}, {"id": "d2-s36", "doc": 2, "title": "Content Delivery Network", "html": "<p>GDRP has adopted Akamai as the go-to-market solution leveraging Stellantis enterprise CDN instance for secured &amp; low-latency delivery of content hosted in GDRP domain and proxying content from application hosted outside GDRP domain. Following section describes each of such use cases.<\/p>", "text": "GDRP has adopted Akamai as the go-to-market solution leveraging Stellantis enterprise CDN instance for secured & low-latency delivery of content hosted in GDRP domain and proxying content from application hosted outside GDRP domain. Following section describes each of such use cases."}, {"id": "d2-s37", "doc": 2, "title": "Split proxy", "html": "<p>An Akamai reverse proxy can be used for URL masking by directing users to a single, public Akamai domain while internally forwarding their requests to the actual, hidden origin server, effectively concealing the true location of the website, and protecting it from direct access, a key feature of a reverse proxy function. <\/p><p><img loading=\"lazy\" alt=\"Source document figure\" src=\"data:image/png;base64,\"><\/p><p>Figure 42-Split Proxy Request Flow<\/p><p>In section 4.2.3, one of the design considerations that existing application needs to incorporate is to adjust application functionality. For application to differentiate between traffic channel i.e. whether the request to application is coming directly from client or via proxied URL, Akamai has provision to insert HTTP header variables in the HTTP request. If the application (origin) detects the header, it can execute the logic to respond with modified UI adjusting the native functionality so as to deliver a seamless experience blending with GDRP platform omnipresent component.<\/p><p>Typical Benefits of using Reverse Proxy:<\/p><p><strong>User Experience<\/strong><strong>:<\/strong><\/p><p>End users get a sense of uniform user experience by generating a façade that the content from third party domains is getting delivered from “logged-in” first party domain.<\/p><p><strong>Security:<\/strong><\/p><p>By hiding the origin server IP address, it protects against direct attacks and malicious actors attempting to access the server directly. This is more applicable if application want to block direct traffic and only allow proxy traffic. <\/p>", "text": "An Akamai reverse proxy can be used for URL masking by directing users to a single, public Akamai domain while internally forwarding their requests to the actual, hidden origin server, effectively concealing the true location of the website, and protecting it from direct access, a key feature of a reverse proxy function. \n\nFigure 42-Split Proxy Request Flow\nIn section 4.2.3, one of the design considerations that existing application needs to incorporate is to adjust application functionality. For application to differentiate between traffic channel i.e. whether the request to application is coming directly from client or via proxied URL, Akamai has provision to insert HTTP header variables in the HTTP request. If the application (origin) detects the header, it can execute the logic to respond with modified UI adjusting the native functionality so as to deliver a seamless experience blending with GDRP platform omnipresent component.\nTypical Benefits of using Reverse Proxy:\nUser Experience:\nEnd users get a sense of uniform user experience by generating a façade that the content from third party domains is getting delivered from “logged-in” first party domain.\nSecurity:\nBy hiding the origin server IP address, it protects against direct attacks and malicious actors attempting to access the server directly. This is more applicable if application want to block direct traffic and only allow proxy traffic. "}, {"id": "d2-s38", "doc": 2, "title": "Content Caching", "html": "<p>Content caching by a CDN improves website performance by storing copies of static and dynamic assets on distributed edge servers.<\/p><p>key benefits of content caching by a CDN:<\/p><p><strong>Faster Load Times<\/strong> - Delivers content from edge servers closer to the user, reducing latency.<\/p><p><strong>Reduced Server Load<\/strong> - Offloads traffic from the origin server, improving performance and reliability.<\/p><p><strong>Scalability<\/strong> - Handles large traffic spikes without degrading user experience.<\/p><p><strong>High Availability<\/strong> - Cached content remains available even if the origin server goes down temporarily.<\/p><p><strong>Bandwidth Optimization<\/strong> - Reduces data transfer from the origin, lowering hosting and infrastructure costs.<\/p><p><strong>Improved SEO and User Experience<\/strong> - Faster websites rank better in search engines and improve user retention.<\/p><p><strong>Enhanced Security<\/strong> - Helps absorb and mitigate DDoS attacks and malicious traffic.<\/p><p><strong>Consistent Global Performance<\/strong> - Ensures users worldwide experience similar load times.<\/p><p>While GDRP has enabled Caching for content &amp; assets being delivered from GDRP infrastructure, integrating applications may also leverage the same instance of caching solution (Common Infrastructure Component) from GDRP for their content caching as well. This should be adopted with caution if the application has any other caching solution already in their network flow. Having multiple caching layer may result in content cache getting out of sync.<\/p>", "text": "Content caching by a CDN improves website performance by storing copies of static and dynamic assets on distributed edge servers.\nkey benefits of content caching by a CDN:\nFaster Load Times - Delivers content from edge servers closer to the user, reducing latency.\nReduced Server Load - Offloads traffic from the origin server, improving performance and reliability.\nScalability - Handles large traffic spikes without degrading user experience.\nHigh Availability - Cached content remains available even if the origin server goes down temporarily.\nBandwidth Optimization - Reduces data transfer from the origin, lowering hosting and infrastructure costs.\nImproved SEO and User Experience - Faster websites rank better in search engines and improve user retention.\nEnhanced Security - Helps absorb and mitigate DDoS attacks and malicious traffic.\nConsistent Global Performance - Ensures users worldwide experience similar load times.\nWhile GDRP has enabled Caching for content & assets being delivered from GDRP infrastructure, integrating applications may also leverage the same instance of caching solution (Common Infrastructure Component) from GDRP for their content caching as well. This should be adopted with caution if the application has any other caching solution already in their network flow. Having multiple caching layer may result in content cache getting out of sync."}, {"id": "d2-s39", "doc": 2, "title": "Request Management", "html": "<p>Stellantis has ServiceNow based Incident Management &amp; Request Fulfillment tool named as Drive IT.<\/p><p>Stellantis has Reunis portal as the Access Management Solution to various IT tools &amp; functions.<\/p>", "text": "Stellantis has ServiceNow based Incident Management & Request Fulfillment tool named as Drive IT.\nStellantis has Reunis portal as the Access Management Solution to various IT tools & functions."}, {"id": "d2-s40", "doc": 2, "title": "Sonar Access", "html": "<p>Sonar is code quality tool that is integrated with Stellantis GitHub pipeline. Update the article-event status17\nFlow Summary: Article-Event Status17\nFlow Summary: End-to-End Article Notification19\nFlow Summary: Portal Notification Maintenance21\nStep 1: Receive the notification table24\nStep 11: Acknowledge the SQS message24\nFlow Summary: Event-Type Decision24\nFlow Summary: Portal Notification Processing25\nFlow Summary: User Notification Retrieval27\nLPMI Notification Service\nAPI Flows, Processing Logic, and Error Handling"}, {"id": "d3-s2", "doc": 3, "title": "Overview", "html": "<p>This document describes the end-to-end LPMI notification architecture across three API flows: article email notifications, portal notification maintenance, and user-specific notification retrieval. It explains the responsibilities of AEM, REST controllers, Amazon SQS, scheduled processing, DynamoDB, Thymeleaf, and Amazon SES; documents the main processing and status transitions; and identifies delivery and error-handling risks that require architectural review.<\/p><p><strong>1. Introduction<\/strong><\/p><p>The LPMI Notification Service processes content-publishing events received from Adobe Experience Manager, maintains notifications displayed in the LPMI Portal, identifies relevant portal users from article market and role metadata, and delivers personalized email notifications through Amazon Simple Email Service.<\/p><p>The implementation uses REST APIs, Amazon SQS queues, scheduled processing, DynamoDB and article-event persistence, Thymeleaf email templates, and Amazon SES. The REST APIs support three distinct stages of the notification lifecycle:<\/p><p><strong>POST /publish<\/strong> initiates the article email-notification flow. It receives LPMI content events, places them on the Global LPMI SQS queue, retrieves the latest article data from AEM, and stores eligible article events for scheduled processing. The scheduler identifies recipients from article market and role metadata, creates localized email messages, and publishes them to the Email SQS queue for delivery through Amazon SES.<\/p><p><strong>POST /<\/strong><strong>publishNotifications<\/strong> maintains the notifications displayed in the LPMI Portal. It sends each create, update, or delete event to the Publish Notification SQS queue. For create and update events, the service retrieves the latest notification data from AEM and saves it in the LPMI notification table; for delete events, it removes the matching notification record.<\/p><p><strong>POST /<\/strong><strong>getNotificationsByUserName<\/strong> retrieves notifications applicable to the current portal user. It filters records by role, market, region, language, and content path; calculates read or unread status; removes notifications with null or future start dates; sorts the remaining records by start date in descending order; and returns the latest 50 notifications to the Portal UI.<\/p><p><strong>Purpose of /publish<\/strong><\/p><p>The publish API processes LPMI article-publishing events and initiates an asynchronous email-notification workflow. For each eligible event, it retrieves the latest article data from AEM, stores the event with its payload, identifies recipients by market and role, creates localized email messages, and sends them through Amazon SQS and Amazon SES.<\/p><p><strong>email notification workflow<\/strong>.<\/p><p><strong>What it does<\/strong><\/p><p>Receives content events.<\/p><p>Adds a sequenceId to each event.<\/p><p>Sends LPMI events to the Global LPMI SQS queue.<\/p><p>The Global SQS consumer processes the event and performs page or cache invalidation.<\/p><p>For an LPMI article update, it retrieves the latest article data from AEM.<\/p><p>Saves the article and AEM payload in the ArticleEvent table with status NEW.<\/p><p>The hourly scheduler selects eligible NEW and FAILED articles.<\/p><p>It identifies users based on the article’s markets and roles.<\/p><p>Creates a localized EmailMessage for every eligible user.<\/p><p>Sends those messages to Email SQS.<\/p><p>EmailConsumer reads each message and sends the email through Amazon SES.<\/p><p>The article event is updated to PROCESSED or FAILED.<\/p><p><strong>Simple purpose statement<\/strong><strong> <\/strong><strong>document<\/strong><\/p><p>The /publish API processes LPMI article publishing events and initiates the asynchronous email-notification flow. It retrieves the latest article information from AEM, stores the article event, identifies eligible users based on market and role, and sends localized email notifications through SQS and Amazon SES.<\/p>", "text": "This document describes the end-to-end LPMI notification architecture across three API flows: article email notifications, portal notification maintenance, and user-specific notification retrieval. It explains the responsibilities of AEM, REST controllers, Amazon SQS, scheduled processing, DynamoDB, Thymeleaf, and Amazon SES; documents the main processing and status transitions; and identifies delivery and error-handling risks that require architectural review.\n1. Introduction\nThe LPMI Notification Service processes content-publishing events received from Adobe Experience Manager, maintains notifications displayed in the LPMI Portal, identifies relevant portal users from article market and role metadata, and delivers personalized email notifications through Amazon Simple Email Service.\nThe implementation uses REST APIs, Amazon SQS queues, scheduled processing, DynamoDB and article-event persistence, Thymeleaf email templates, and Amazon SES. The REST APIs support three distinct stages of the notification lifecycle:\nPOST /publish initiates the article email-notification flow. It receives LPMI content events, places them on the Global LPMI SQS queue, retrieves the latest article data from AEM, and stores eligible article events for scheduled processing. The scheduler identifies recipients from article market and role metadata, creates localized email messages, and publishes them to the Email SQS queue for delivery through Amazon SES.\nPOST /publishNotifications maintains the notifications displayed in the LPMI Portal. It sends each create, update, or delete event to the Publish Notification SQS queue. For create and update events, the service retrieves the latest notification data from AEM and saves it in the LPMI notification table; for delete events, it removes the matching notification record.\nPOST /getNotificationsByUserName retrieves notifications applicable to the current portal user. It filters records by role, market, region, language, and content path; calculates read or unread status; removes notifications with null or future start dates; sorts the remaining records by start date in descending order; and returns the latest 50 notifications to the Portal UI.\nPurpose of /publish\nThe publish API processes LPMI article-publishing events and initiates an asynchronous email-notification workflow. For each eligible event, it retrieves the latest article data from AEM, stores the event with its payload, identifies recipients by market and role, creates localized email messages, and sends them through Amazon SQS and Amazon SES.\nemail notification workflow.\nWhat it does\nReceives content events.\nAdds a sequenceId to each event.\nSends LPMI events to the Global LPMI SQS queue.\nThe Global SQS consumer processes the event and performs page or cache invalidation.\nFor an LPMI article update, it retrieves the latest article data from AEM.\nSaves the article and AEM payload in the ArticleEvent table with status NEW.\nThe hourly scheduler selects eligible NEW and FAILED articles.\nIt identifies users based on the article’s markets and roles.\nCreates a localized EmailMessage for every eligible user.\nSends those messages to Email SQS.\nEmailConsumer reads each message and sends the email through Amazon SES.\nThe article event is updated to PROCESSED or FAILED.\nSimple purpose statement document\nThe /publish API processes LPMI article publishing events and initiates the asynchronous email-notification flow. It retrieves the latest article information from AEM, stores the article event, identifies eligible users based on market and role, and sends localized email notifications through SQS and Amazon SES."}, {"id": "d3-s3", "doc": 3, "title": "Flow Summary: Article Email Notifications", "html": "<div class=\"tablewrap\"><table><tr><td>cStep<\/td><td>Stage<\/td><td>What happens<\/td><\/tr><tr><td>1<\/td><td><strong>POST /publish<\/strong><\/td><td>Receives LPMI content events from AEM and adds a sequenceId to each content item.<\/td><\/tr><tr><td>2<\/td><td><strong>Global LPMI SQS<\/strong><\/td><td>Queues each LPMI content item for asynchronous processing and page or cache invalidation.<\/td><\/tr><tr><td>3<\/td><td><strong>Retrieve article from AEM<\/strong><\/td><td>For LPMI article updates, fetches the latest article data, retrying transient failures.<\/td><\/tr><tr><td>4<\/td><td><strong>Save <\/strong><strong>ArticleEvent<\/strong><strong> as NEW<\/strong><\/td><td>Stores the article and its AEM payload in the ArticleEvent table with status NEW.<\/td><\/tr><tr><td>5<\/td><td><strong>Hourly scheduler<\/strong><\/td><td>Selects the current day&#x27;s NEW and FAILED article events.<\/td><\/tr><tr><td>6<\/td><td><strong>Find users by market and role<\/strong><\/td><td>Converts role tags into MyPeople JR codes and selects eligible users in pages of 200.<\/td><\/tr><tr><td>7<\/td><td><strong>Email SQS<\/strong><\/td><td>Receives localized EmailMessage payloads, sent in batches of five.<\/td><\/tr><tr><td>8<\/td><td><strong>Email Consumer<\/strong><\/td><td>Validates each message and renders the localized Thymeleaf email.<\/td><\/tr><tr><td>9<\/td><td><strong>Amazon SES<\/strong><\/td><td>Sends the email and retries throttling-related errors.<\/td><\/tr><\/table><\/div><p>Table 1. Article Email Notification Flow<\/p><p><strong>3. Detailed current flow<\/strong><\/p>", "text": "cStep\nStage\nWhat happens\n1\nPOST /publish\nReceives LPMI content events from AEM and adds a sequenceId to each content item.\n2\nGlobal LPMI SQS\nQueues each LPMI content item for asynchronous processing and page or cache invalidation.\n3\nRetrieve article from AEM\nFor LPMI article updates, fetches the latest article data, retrying transient failures.\n4\nSave ArticleEvent as NEW\nStores the article and its AEM payload in the ArticleEvent table with status NEW.\n5\nHourly scheduler\nSelects the current day's NEW and FAILED article events.\n6\nFind users by market and role\nConverts role tags into MyPeople JR codes and selects eligible users in pages of 200.\n7\nEmail SQS\nReceives localized EmailMessage payloads, sent in batches of five.\n8\nEmail Consumer\nValidates each message and renders the localized Thymeleaf email.\n9\nAmazon SES\nSends the email and retries throttling-related errors.\nTable 1. Article Email Notification Flow\n3. Detailed current flow"}, {"id": "d3-s4", "doc": 3, "title": "Step 1: Receive the article publishing request", "html": "<p>The flow begins when an external system, such as AEM, sends an HTTP POST request to the publish endpoint:<\/p><p>@PostMapping(value = &quot;/publish&quot;, consumes = &quot;application/json&quot;, produces = &quot;application/json&quot;)<\/p><p>The request body contains a content array. Each element represents an individual content publishing event.<\/p><p><strong>Key request fields<\/strong><\/p><p>id<\/p><p>contentPath<\/p><p>selector<\/p><p>type<\/p><p>eventType<\/p><p>contentType<\/p><p>The controller reads the content array and processes every content item separately.<\/p><p>Function:<\/p><p>publish()<\/p>", "text": "The flow begins when an external system, such as AEM, sends an HTTP POST request to the publish endpoint:\n@PostMapping(value = \"/publish\", consumes = \"application/json\", produces = \"application/json\")\nThe request body contains a content array. Each element represents an individual content publishing event.\nKey request fields\nid\ncontentPath\nselector\ntype\neventType\ncontentType\nThe controller reads the content array and processes every content item separately.\nFunction:\npublish()"}, {"id": "d3-s5", "doc": 3, "title": "Step 2: Add a sequence ID", "html": "<p>For every content item, the controller generates and adds a sequenceId.<\/p><p>objectNode.put(&quot;sequenceId&quot;, generateID());<\/p><p>The sequenceId is used to track the content item as it moves through the asynchronous processing flow.<\/p><p>After adding the sequence ID, the content item is converted into a JSON string.<\/p><p>String message = objectNode.toString();<\/p><p><strong>Function:<\/strong><\/p><p>processContentItem()<\/p>", "text": asynchronous processing flow.\nAfter adding the sequence ID, the content item is converted into a JSON string.\nString message = objectNode.toString();\nFunction:\nprocessContentItem()"}, {"id": (&quot;lpmi&quot;.equalsIgnoreCase(contentTypeNode.asText()))<\/p><p>Only content items having:<\/p><p>contentType = lpmi<\/p><p>are sent to the Global LPMI SQS queue.<\/p><p>Other content types are ignored by this condition.<\/p>", "text": "The controller checks whether the content belongs to LPMI.\nif (\"lpmi\".equalsIgnoreCase(contentTypeNode.asText()))\nOnly content items having:\ncontentType = lpmi\nare sent to the Global LPMI SQS queue.\nOther content types are ignored by this condition."}, {"id": "d3-s7", "doc": 3, "title": "Step 4: Publish the message to the Global LPMI SQS queue", "html": "<p>The controller calls:<\/p><p>sqsMessageSender.sendGlobalMessage(message);<\/p><p>SQSMessageSender sends the serialized content item to the SQS queue configured by:<\/p><p>sqs.queue.global.lpmi<\/p><p>This separates the HTTP request processing from the article-processing logic.<\/p><p>Function:<\/p><p>SQSMessageSender.sendGlobalMessage()<\/p>", "text": "The controller calls:\nsqsMessageSender.sendGlobalMessage(message);\nSQSMessageSender sends the serialized content item to the SQS queue configured by:\nsqs.queue.global.lpmi\nThis separates the HTTP request processing from the article-processing logic.\nFunction:\nSQSMessageSender.sendGlobalMessage()"}, {"id": "d3-s8", "doc": 3, "title": "Step 5: Consume the Global LPMI SQS message", "html": "<p>SQSMessageReceiver listens to the Global LPMI SQS queue.<\/p><p>@SqsListener(&quot;${sqs.queue.global.lpmi}&quot;)<\/p><p>The listener receives the message and calls:<\/p><p>processMessage(message, acknowledgement);<\/p><p>The message payload is converted from JSON text into a Jackson JsonNode.<\/p><p>JsonNode requestBody = mapper.readTree(payload);<\/p><p>The receiver then processes the content item according to its type.<\/p><p>Functions:<\/p><p>receiveGlobalMessage()<\/p><p>processMessage()<\/p><p>processContentItem()<\/p>", "text": "SQSMessageReceiver listens to the Global LPMI SQS queue.\n@SqsListener(\"${sqs.queue.global.lpmi}\")\nThe listener receives the message and calls:\nprocessMessage(message, acknowledgement);\nThe message payload is converted from JSON text into a Jackson JsonNode.\nJsonNode requestBody = mapper.readTree(payload);\nThe receiver then processes the content item according to its type.\nFunctions:\nreceiveGlobalMessage()\nprocessMessage()\nprocessContentItem()"}, {"id": "d3-s9", "doc": 3, "title": "Step 6: Process the message based on content type", "html": "<p>The receiver extracts these fields:<\/p><p>contentPath<\/p><p>type<\/p><p>eventType<\/p><p>contentType<\/p><p>It then chooses the appropriate action.<\/p><p><strong>FAQ<\/strong><\/p><p>For type = faq:<\/p><p>deletePagePathService.deletePagePath(contentPath, false);<\/p><p><strong>Article<\/strong><\/p><p>For type = article and contentType = lpmi:<\/p><p>deletePagePathService.deletePagePathGdrpLpmi(    contentPath,    contentType,    eventType,    true);<\/p><p>If the article event represents an update:<\/p><p>if (&quot;update&quot;.equalsIgnoreCase(eventType)) {<\/p><p>saveIfNotExists(requestBody);<\/p><p>}<\/p><p>Therefore, the email article-event record is created only when:<\/p><p>type = &quot;/content/dam/gdrp/documents&quot;,    false);<\/p><p><strong>Other content<\/strong><\/p><p>For type = other and contentType = lpmi:<\/p><p>deletePagePathService.deletePagePathGdrpLpmi(    contentPath,    contentType,    eventType,    false);<\/p>", "text": "The receiver extracts these fields:\ncontentPath\ntype\neventType\ncontentType\nIt then chooses the appropriate action.\nFAQ\nFor contentType,    eventType,    true);\nIf the article event represents an update:\nif (\"update\".equalsIgnoreCase(eventType)) {\nsaveIfNotExists(requestBody);\n}\nTherefore, the email article-event "title": "Step 7: Check whether the article event already exists", "html": "<p>For an LPMI article update, the receiver converts the incoming message into an ArticleEventRequest.<\/p><p>ArticleEventRequest request =    objectMapper.readValue(requestBody, ArticleEventRequest.class);<\/p><p>Before creating a new record, it checks the database using the article ID:<\/p><p>if (eventrepository.existsById(request.getId())) {<\/p><p>return true;<\/p><p>}<\/p><p>If the ID already exists, the method does not insert another record.<\/p><p>This supports duplicate-event prevention based on the article ID.<\/p><p>Function:<\/p><p>saveIfNotExists()<\/p>", "text": "For an LPMI article update, the receiver converts the incoming message into an ArticleEventRequest.\nArticleEventRequest request =    objectMapper.readValue(requestBody, ArticleEventRequest.class);\nBefore creating a new record, it checks the database using the article ID:\nif (eventrepository.existsById(request.getId())) {\nreturn true;\n}\nIf the ID already exists, the method does not insert another record.\nThis supports duplicate-event prevention based on the article ID.\nFunction:\nsaveIfNotExists()"}, {"id": "d3-s11", "doc": 3, "title": "Step 8: Retrieve the latest article data from AEM", "html": "<p>For a new article event, the service calls AEM ID\nLink information\nThe complete AEM response is stored as the event payload for later email processing."}, {"id": "d3-s12", "doc": 3, "title": "Step 9: Retry the AEM request when necessary", "html": "<p>The implementation allows a maximum of three AEM call attempts.<\/p><p>int maxRetries = 3;<\/p><p>Retry processing is performed for exceptions currently classified as:<\/p><p>IOException<\/p><p>SocketTimeoutException<\/p><p>RuntimeException<\/p><p>Exponential backoff is applied between attempts.<\/p><p>First retry delay: 1000 milliseconds<\/p><p>Second retry delay: 2000 milliseconds<\/p><p>The related functions are:<\/p><p>fetchAemWithRetry()<\/p><p>isRetryable()<\/p><p>backoff()<\/p>", "text": "The implementation allows a maximum of three AEM call attempts.\nint maxRetries = 3;\nRetry processing is performed for exceptions currently classified as:\nIOException\nSocketTimeoutException\nRuntimeException\nExponential backoff is applied between attempts.\nFirst retry delay: 1000 milliseconds\nSecond retry delay: 2000 milliseconds\nThe related functions are:\nfetchAemWithRetry()\nisRetryable()\nbackoff()"}, {"id": "d3-s13", "doc": 3, "title": queue processing."}, {"id": "d3-s15", "doc": 3, "title": "Step 12: Run the hourly email scheduler", "html": "<p>The email scheduler runs at the beginning of every hour.<\/p><p>@Scheduled(cron = day and retrieves article events with these statuses:<\/p><p>NEW<\/p><p>FAILED<\/p><p>Repository operation:<\/p><p>eventrepository.findByStartDateBetweenAndStatusIn(    startOfDay,    endOfDay,    statuses);<\/p><p>Selection is based on the article startDate extracted from the AEM payload.<\/p><p>Function:<\/p><p>processTodayArticles()<\/p>", "text": "The email scheduler runs at the beginning statuses);\nSelection is based on the article startDate extracted from the AEM payload.\nFunction:\nprocessTodayArticles()"}, {"id": "d3-s16", "doc": 3, "title": "Step 13: Extract article targeting title<\/p><p>Article link<\/p><p>Article ID<\/p><p>If a matching article cannot be found, processing stops with:<\/p><p>No news found in AEM<\/p><p>Function:<\/p><p>extractNewsFromAem()<\/p>", "text": structure:\n{app.env.url}/article?id={articleId}&linkPath={contentPath}\nBoth the article ID and content path are URL encoded.\nThis allows the email recipient to open the correct article in the LPMI portal."}, {"id": "d3-s20", "doc": 3, "title": "Step 17: Select eligible users", "html": "<p>Users are fetched in pages of 200 records.<\/p><p>int pageSize = 200;<\/p><p>The repository query depends on the available targeting information.<\/p><p><strong>Market and role are available<\/strong><\/p><p>userRepository.findByMarketsAndRoles(    markets,    roles,    pageable);<\/p><p><strong>Only roles are available<\/strong><\/p><p>userRepository.findByRoles(    roles,    pageable);<\/p><p><strong>Only markets are available<\/strong><\/p><p>userRepository.findByMarkets(    markets,    pageable);<\/p><p><strong>No market or role targeting is available<\/strong><\/p><p>userRepository.findDistinctUsers(pageable);<\/p><p>This means the article can target:<\/p><p>Users matching both pageable);\nOnly roles are available\nuserRepository.findByRoles(    roles,    pageable);\nOnly markets are available\nuserRepository.findByMarkets(    markets,    pageable);\nNo market or role targeting is available\nuserRepository.findDistinctUsers(pageable);\nThis means the article can target:\nUsers matching both market and role\nUsers matching only role\nUsers matching only market\nAll distinct users\nFunction:\nfetchUsersAndProcess()"}, {"id": "d3-s21", "doc": 3, "title": "Step 18: Build an email message for each user", "html": "<p>Users without an email address are
