                       Security Control Description\n\nCS-SL-GN-10   Must ensure that the latest version of the execution environment is used.\nCS-SL-GN-20   Must ensure that only trusted entities have specific function access.\nCS-SL-GN-30   Ensure that while configuring the function, must determine the smallest set of\n                permissions strictly needed by the function to execute successfully.\nCS-SL-GN-40   Must not use long-lived credentials or hardcoded secrets in functions.\nCS-SL-GN-50   Must ensure that confidential information and credentials are not stored in the\n                  function’s runtime.\nCS-SL-GN-60   Must store environment variables/runtime information with encryption in a\n               secure store.\nCS-SL-GN-70   Must limit access to connected cloud resources and validation of input\n               parameters to secure Serverless functions to prevent injection attacks.\nCS-SL-GN-80   Must ensure that all external libraries and dependencies used by any function\n                are shared with the Security team to analyze and authorize its use.\n\n\n6.2 Network\n\n\nControl Ref #                        Security Control Description\n\nCS-SL-NW-10  Ensure that any external connection must be protected by a web application\n                    firewall.\nCS-SL-NW-20  Ensure that Functions that need access to internal resources must be\n               connected to your VPC.\n\n\n6.3 Encryption\n\n\nControl Ref #                        Security Control Description\n\nCS-SL-EN-10   Must ensure that it always protects the data by leveraging encryption in transit\n               as well at rest.\nCS-SL-EN-20   Ensure that Secrets shall always only exist in memory and must never be\n                logged or written clear text to storage areas.\n\n\n\n\n\n                                              Stellantis classification\n                                  C2 – Internal                               Page 23 of 44"}, {"id": "d7-s25", "doc": 7, "title": "Page 25 · SSIT-S009-G001 STELLANTIS CLOUD SECURITY CONTROLS GUIDELINE", "html": "<div class=\"pdftext\">        SSIT-S009-G001 STELLANTIS CLOUD SECURITY CONTROLS GUIDELINE\n\n6.4 Access Control\n\n\nControl Ref #                        Security Control Description\n\nCS-SL-AC-10   Must ensure that access to each function is restricted through required\n                   privileges assigned to the IAM role only.\nCS-SL-AC-20   Ensure and leverage that service account created for each one of the\n                 functions with required IAM roles.\nCS-SL-AC-30   Ensure that each Server-less/Cloud function within the respective cloud\n               account should have a 1:1 relationship with an IAM role.\nCS-SL-AC-40   Must ensure that functions do not have administrative privilege.\n\n\n\n 7. API Security\n\nThe below mentioned are minimal recommended Cloud Security Controls for API. Additional\nsecurity control must be envisaged and enforced based on the application/platform requirements\n\nand review of the Cloud Security team.\n\n\n\n7.1 API Gateway Security\n\n\n Control Ref #                        Security Control Description\n\n CS-AP-GN-10   Must ensure that use of self-signed certificates is only allowed for cross-\n                 communications between each component of the API infrastructure. These\n                    self-signed certificates expire after 365 days, hence, must ensure to rotate\n                   the certificate before it expires through automation.\n CS-AP-GN-20   Must ensure that APIs created with Cloud API Gateway are only accessible\n                    via private endpoints.\n CS-AP-GN-30   Use of API Connect must be privileged for the exposure to the consumer.\n CS-AP-GN-40   Must protect API Gateways with web application firewall.\n CS-AP-GN-50   Must host API Gateways in a VPC (virtual private cloud). Without exposing\n                   the APIs and microservices to the internet, the APIs can be accessed\n                  through HTTPS/HTTP2 and WebSocket requests.\n CS-AP-GN-60   Must use only one access control like IAM or use token authentication.\n CS-AP-GN-70   API Gateway’s self-signed certificate needs to be backed up by PEM\n                   (Privacy Enhanced Mail) encoded private key and a server-side certificate\n                  provided by trusted Certificate authority.\n CS-AP-GN-80   Must ensure to have separate API Gateways for mobile and non-mobile\n                   users.\n CS-AP-GN-90   API Gateway must accept connections only from API Connect, with mTLS\n                  (mutual TLS).\n CS-AP-GN-100  MFA must be enforced when accessing API gateways and developer\n                    portals that allow registration of new APIs, keys, or apps.\n\n\n\n\n                                              Stellantis classification\n                                  C2 – Internal                               Page 24 of 44<\/div>", "text": "        SSIT-S009-G001 STELLANTIS CLOUD SECURITY CONTROLS GUIDELINE\n\n6.4 Access Control\n\n\nControl Ref #                        Security Control Description\n\nCS-SL-AC-10   Must ensure that access to each function is restricted through required\n                   privileges assigned to the IAM role only.\nCS-SL-AC-20   Ensure and leverage that service account created for each one of the\n                 functions with required IAM roles.\nCS-SL-AC-30   Ensure that each Server-less/Cloud function within the respective cloud\n               account should have a 1:1 relationship with an IAM role.\nCS-SL-AC-40   Must ensure that functions do not have administrative privilege.\n\n\n\n 7. Additional\nsecurity control must be envisaged and enforced based on the application/platform requirements\n\nand review of the Cloud Security team.\n\n\n\n7.1 API Gateway Security\n\n\n Control Ref #                        Security Control Description\n\n CS-AP-GN-10   Must ensure that use of self-signed certificates is only allowed for cross-\n                 communications between each component of the API infrastructure. Enforce\n                   least privilege grant only the minimum permissions needed.\nCS-AS-AP-20  Must ensure that PaaS API is accessed only through cloud provider’s or\n              customer-owned private connectivity.\nCS-AS-AP-30  Must ensure that public network access to API services is disabled.\nCS-AS-AP-40  Use allow-lists (whitelisting) over block-lists for network access.\nCS-AS-AP-50     If there is an API server, it should only be accessible from a limited set of IP\n               address ranges.\nCS-AS-AP-60   Ensure that cloud IAM authentication for API endpoint is enforced.\nCS-AS-AP-70  Must ensure that leverage and enforce IAM roles to allow applications to\n                securely make API requests from the instances, without requiring managing\n                 the security credentials that the applications use.\nCS-AS-AP-80   Ensure that, to reduce attack vectors, API-Keys must be restricted only to\n                  trusted hosts, HTTP referrers and applications.\nCS-AS-AP-90  Must ensure and enforce the use of HTTPS when calling the API to access\n                 objects in Storage Accounts.\nCS-AS-AP-100  Ensure that Client-side encryption is enforced for Application APIs performing\n                encryption of sensitive data before storing.\nCS-AS-AP-110  Ensure that logging is enabled to monitor API calls.\nCS-AS-AP-120  Ensure Log detailed internal errors for monitoring and debugging.\nCS-AS-AP-130 Must ensure that each application should use its own secret vault for every\n               environment — like Development, Pre-Production, and Production — so that\n                 secrets are not shared across environments. This helps reduce the risk if one\n               environment is compromised and ensures that sensitive data from Production\n                 doesn’t leak into less secure environments like Development.\nCS-AS-AP-140 Must ensure that service processes are configured to run as a user with a\n                      strictly limited set of privileges (i.e., not running as root, administrator, or\n                  equivalent).\nCS-AS-AP-150 Must leverage service specific REST APIs on HTTPS to ensure that data flow\n                     is secure while in transit between cloud providers services.\nCS-AS-AP-160 Must enforce, the use of HTTPS when calling the APIs as well REST\n                  API/similar API like gRPC (Google Remote Procedure Call) to access objects\n                    in Storage Accounts by enabling native safe file transfer for the Storage\n               Account.\n\n\n\n\n\n                                              Stellantis classification\n                                  C2 – Internal                               Page 25 of 44<\/div>", "text": "        SSIT-S009-G001 STELLANTIS CLOUD SECURITY CONTROLS GUIDELINE\n\n\n7.2 API Security\n Control Ref #                       Security Control Description\n\nCS-AS-AP-10  Must ensure that only authorized users or systems can access API. Identity and Access Management\n\nThe below mentioned are minimal recommended Cloud Security Controls for Identity and Access\nManagement. Additional  security control must be envisaged and enforced based on the\napplication/platform requirements and review of the Cloud Security team.\n\n\n8.1 General\n\n\n Control Ref #                        Security Control Description\n\n CS-IA-GN-10   Must ensure that the “Separation of Duties” principle is being followed while\n                  assigning the access and privileges. “Separation of Duties”, also known as\n                  “Segregation of Duties”, is the concept of having more than one person\n                 perform a critical IT administrative task. For example, there should be the\n                  separation of administrator provisioning access and the user of the IT asset.\n\n\n\n8.2 Access Role\n\n\n Control Ref #                        Security Control Description\n\n CS-IA-PA-10    Ensure that Stellantis defined custom role created for all privilege\n                assignments to the user account or application as well system accounts.\n CS-IA-PA-20    Must ensure that no direct privilege is provided for the users/administrator\n                   or application account. The privileges need to be assigned through the\n                  respective role.\n CS-IA-PA-30    Must use Role-Based Access Control (RBAC) for assigning permissions to\n                   users, groups, and applications as Stellantis defined policy.\n CS-IA-PA-40    Must ensure that use of managed role privilege policies after having\n                    carefully evaluated that they have not assigned with exceeding rights.\n CS-IA-PA-50    Must adhere to the principle of “Least Privilege” for assigning privileges to\n                  the user/ application account through privilege roles.\n CS-IA-PA-60    Must ensure that consumers/end-user privileges do not manage or control\n                  the underlying infrastructure through the right privilege assignment.\n CS-IA-PA-70    Ensure that a privileged user identity must be separate from general\n                purpose identity for the user.\n CS-IA-PA-80     All administrators must have a dedicated account for cloud administrative\n                  tasks to limit the probability that an attack compromises administrator\n                 account.\n CS-IS-PA-90    Must provide only temporary escalated privileges (such as sudo in Linux\n                 environment) for users who need to perform occasional privileged tasks.\n CS-IS-PA-100   Must ensure that Multi-Factor Authentication (MFA) is enabled for Privileged\n                 Users.\n\n\n\n                                              Stellantis classification\n                                  C2 – Internal                               Page 26 of 44<\/div>", "text": "        SSIT-S009-G001 STELLANTIS CLOUD SECURITY CONTROLS GUIDELINE\n\n\n\n8. If the account is not needed, then the same must be\n                  deactivated.\n CS-IS-PA-120   Ensure that any application/database schemas or user created by CSP for\n                   learning and testing purposes are removed from the production\n                 environment.\n\n\n8.3 Identity and Password Management\n\n\n Control Ref #                        Security Control Description\n\n CS-IA-IP-10    Ensure that Identity creation must be according to Stellantis approved\n                    policy. Identity pattern for human and application access provisioning must\n                   follow Stellantis guidelines.\n CS-IA-IP-20    Must ensure that Stellantis corporate login credentials using SSO are used\n                  instead of local accounts.\n CS-IA-IP-30    Must ensure that contact Information with a company phone number and\n                 email for a user account are configured.\n CS-IA-IP-40    Must ensure and enforce Stellantis approved IAM password policy e.g.,\n              minimum length, password complexity as well prevention of password reuse\n                    etc.\n CS-IA-IP-50    Must ensure that MFA is enabled for the &#x27;root&#x27; and its equivalent user\n                account as well Privileged Users.\n CS-IA-IP-60    Must ensure that the group email alias is used for the root Login Account.\n CS-IA-IP-70    Must use Stellantis password vault for securing “root” login account and\n                 corresponding password.\n CS-IA-IP-80    Ensure that access to the Cloud Service Provider’s management portal /\n                 console and command Line interface should be designed and configured to\n                use MFA.\n CS-IA-IP-80    Ensure that in addition to MFA, a conditional access verification must be set\n               up by checking workstation conformity and user geolocation for highly\n                    privileged accounts.\n CS-IA-IP-90    Must ensure that users are notified on their primary and secondary emails\n               on password resets (this applicable even for superuser / root account).\n\n8.4 Dormant User\n\n\n Control Ref #                        Security Control Description\n\n CS-IA-DM-10   The IAM policy must be configured to identify if the user account has not\n               been used for 90 days since last access is marked as dormant.\n CS-IA-DM-20   Must ensure credentials (account id) unused for 90 days or greater are\n                   disabled.\n\n\n\n\n\n                                              Stellantis classification\n                                  C2 – Internal                               Page 27 of 44<\/div>", "text": "        SSIT-S009-G001 STELLANTIS CLOUD SECURITY CONTROLS GUIDELINE\n\n CS-IS-PA-110   Ensure that the default system accounts are assessed, and its default\n                password is changed.                        Security Control Description\n\n CS-IA-AT-10    Must ensure leveraging access and time bound refresh tokens to balance\n                   security and usability of each resource.\n CS-IA-AT-20    Must ensure that Service provider’s time limited access signature tokens\n                 are allowed only over https for storage account access.\n CS-IA-AT-30    Ensure that the authentication token is transferred to a secure way and\n               must be validated by application.\n\n\n\n8.6 Service Account\n\n\n Control Ref #                        Security Control Description\n\n CS-IA-SA-10    Must ensure that Service Provider’s service account remains non-interactive\n                    for authentication (it should not allow direct login or manual access, this\n                  helps ensure that the account is only used for automated authentication and\n                reduces the risk of misuse or unauthorized access).\n CS-IA-SA-20    Must ensure that separation of duty Is enforced while assigning user\n              managed Service Account related roles to users.\n CS-IA-SA-30    Must ensure that user managed Service Account has the least privilege.\n CS-IA-SA-40    Must ensure that service accounts are meant for machine-to-machine flow.\n             No personal account should be used for machine-to-machine flow.\n\n\n\n8.7 Centralized Directory Services\n\n\n Control Ref #                         Security Control Description\n\n CS-IA-DS-10      Must ensure that IAM users are managed centrally via AD (Active\n                      Directory) or centralized domain.\n CS-IA-DS-20      Must ensure that any IAM user with interactive access that is created and\n                managed outside corporate SSO needs to be disabled/removed.\n CS-IA-DS-30      Access for admins and end users to the IAM must be done via identity\n                      federation.\n CS-IA-DS-40      Must ensure that access privileges are managed centrally.\n\n\n\n\n\n                                              Stellantis classification\n                                  C2 – Internal                               Page 28 of 44<\/div>", "text": "        SSIT-S009-G001 STELLANTIS CLOUD SECURITY CONTROLS GUIDELINE\n\n8.5 Authentication Tokens\n\n Control Ref # Logging and Monitoring\n\nLogs are helpful as well mandatory during cyber crisis or misconfiguration investigations, hence\n\nlogging needs to be enabled for all required services and configuration items.\n\n\nThe below mentioned are minimal recommended Cloud Security Controls for Logging and\nMonitoring.  Additional  security  control must be envisaged and enforced based on  the\n\napplication/platform requirements and review of the Cloud Security team.\n\n\n9.1 General\n\n\n Control Ref #                        Security Control Description\n\n CS-LM-GN-10   Must ensure that logging and monitoring is enabled for servers, storage,\n                  network, databases, containers, key management, IAM, serverless and\n                code repository.\n CS-LM-GN-20   Must ensure that every Cloud computing environment should have an\n                 immutable centralized log repository with storage volume adapted to all\n                    retention needs in Cloud.\n CS-LM-GN-30   Must ensure that and consider using native cloud monitor tools to collect\n                     additional logs and eventually - configure alerts to respond to them.\n CS-LM-GN-40   Ensure that regardless of the CSP’s native logging and monitoring tool\n                  used, security events must be forwarded to Stellantis SIEM log repository\n                and its monitoring.\n CS-LM-GN-50   Must ensure that logging status of all log sources is monitored.\n CS-LM-GN-60   Must ensure that monitor log rotation and its archival processes are in line\n                   with Stellantis guidelines.\n CS-LM-GN-70   Must ensure that alerts are triggered in case of a logging process failure.\n CS-LM-GN-80   Must ensure that each logging host’s clock is synchronized to a common\n                  time source.\n CS-LM-GN-90   Must ensure that logs are protected from unauthorized access as they may\n                  hold records of system and network security.\n\n\n9.2 IaaS\n\n\n Control Ref #                        Security Control Description\n\n CS-LM-IS-20    Ensure that the access logging feature enabled on load balancers and log\n                 captures information about each TCP and HTTP request made for backend\n                   instances.\n\n\n\n\n\n                                              Stellantis classification\n                                  C2 – Internal                               Page 29 of 44<\/div>", "text": "        SSIT-S009-G001 STELLANTIS CLOUD SECURITY CONTROLS GUIDELINE\n\n9.                        Security Control Description\n\n CS-LM-IS-20    Ensure that the access logging feature enabled on load balancers and log\n                 captures information about each TCP and HTTP request made for backend\n                   instances.\n\n\n\n\n\n                                              Stellantis classification\n                                  C2 – Internal                               Page 29 of 44"}, {"id": "d7-s31", "doc": 7, "title": "Page 31 · SSIT-S009-G001 STELLANTIS CLOUD SECURITY CONTROLS GUIDELINE", "html": "<div class=\"pdftext\">        SSIT-S009-G001 STELLANTIS CLOUD SECURITY CONTROLS GUIDELINE\n\n9.3 Network\n\nControl Ref #                                      Security Control Description\n\nCS-LM-NW-10  Must enable Network Monitor for all subscriptions and regions.\nCS-LM-NW-20  Must enable cloud account-wide logging and centralized monitoring.\nCS-LM-NW-30  Must leverage threat analysis and network monitoring tools that CSP\n                 provides.\nCS-LM-NW-40   Virtual Private Cloud / Virtual Network flow logging must be configured in all\n                   Virtual Networks.\nCS-LM-NW-50  Ensure that egress/Ingress of the network endpoints exposed are logged and\n               stream the logs to SIEM for analysis.\nCS-LM-NW-60  Must ensure that leverage CSP&#x27;s native Flow Logs in order to capture\n                 information about the IP traffic going to and from network interfaces in Virtual\n                 Private Cloud for accepted and rejected network traffic.\nCS-LM-NW-70  Must enable periodic compliance checks of the relevant cloud configurations.\nCS-LM-NW-80  Must configure and monitor network configuration change alerts.\n\n9.4 Data Protection\n\n\n Control Ref #                        Security Control Description\n\n CS-LM-DP-10   Data object logs must be configured and facilitated continuous monitoring\n               and alerting on anomalous activity in access logs and help to identify and\n                 prevent misconfigurations that may lead to data leakage and data loss.\n CS-LM- DP-20  Must ensure to activate logging on data ingestion operations to highlight\n                  misconfigurations or compromise for data objects.\n\n9.5 Identity and Access Management\n\n\n Control Ref #                        Security Control Description\n\n CS-LM-IA-10   Must ensure that actions performed by user, or a service should be logged\n                          i.e., creation, deletion, modification, or execution of an asset to be logged\n                   with log retention defined according to Stellantis policy.\n CS-LM-IA-20   Must ensure that logging and trigger event for all IAM policy changes are\n                  enabled.\n CS-LM-IA-30   Must ensure that an active identity monitor system is in place that can\n                   quickly detect suspicious behavior activity and trigger an alert for further\n                    investigation.\n CS-LM-IA-40   Must ensure that identify, trace, and take a proactive approach for attempts\n                    to sign in without being traced, brute force attacks against a particular\n                 account, attempts to sign in from multiple locations, sign in from infected\n                 devices and suspicious IP addresses.\n CS-LM-IA-50   Must ensure that at least a multi-region Trail is configured on the account to\n                    collect management events.\n CS-LM-IA-60   Must configure using native cloud tools in order to collect additional logs\n               and eventually configure alerts to respond to them.\n\n\n\n                                              Stellantis classification\n                                  C2 – Internal                               Page 30 of 44<\/div>", "text": "        SSIT-S009-G001 STELLANTIS CLOUD SECURITY CONTROLS GUIDELINE\n\n9.3 Network\n\nControl Ref #                        Security Control Description\n\n CS-LM-SL-10   Ensure that Serverless functions are enabled for logging and reporting to\n               CSP’s native metric tool.\n\n\n9.7 PaaS\n\n\n Control Ref #                        Security Control Description\n\n CS-LM-PS-10   Must ensure that logging on native/guest database accounts is enabled in\n                  order to monitor how and when these databases are accessed.\n CS-LM-PS-20   Ensure that database audit logs should be enabled based on the data\n                     classification and or based on the requirements.\n CS-LM-PS-30   Ensure that web applications dealing with confidential or highly confidential\n                   data, logging must be enabled for traffic to track received requests and\n                  actions taken.\n CS-LM-PS-40   Must ensure that diagnostic log is enabled for data analytics tools.\n\n\n9.8 Key Management\n\n\n Control Ref #                        Security Control Description\n\n CS-LM-KM-10  Must ensure logging on CSP’s native Key Management service is enabled\n                    to detect any anomaly.\n\n\n9.9 Container\n                                                                                                \n Control Ref #                       Security Control Description\n               \nCS-LM-CT-10   Ensure that log retention is configured according to data requirements.\nCS-LM-CT-20   Must ensure that logging and monitoring of the registry activity is enabled.\n\n\n9.10 Cloud Storage\n                                                                                                \n Control Ref #                       Security Control Description\n               \nCS-LM-ST-10   Must ensure that enable and monitor access logs of the cloud storage\n                  service.\n\n\n\n\n                                              Stellantis classification\n                                  C2 – Internal                               Page 31 of 44<\/div>", "text": "        SSIT-S009-G001 STELLANTIS CLOUD SECURITY CONTROLS GUIDELINE\n\n9.6 Serverless\n\n\n Control Ref #                        Security Control Description\n\n CS-LM-SL-10   Ensure that Serverless functions are enabled for logging and reporting to\n               CSP’s native metric tool.\n\n\n9.7 PaaS\n\n\n Control Ref #                        Security Control Description\n\n CS-LM-PS-10   Must ensure that logging on native/guest database accounts is enabled in\n                  order to monitor how and when these databases are accessed.\n CS-LM-PS-20   Ensure that database audit logs should be enabled based on the data\n                     classification and or based on the requirements.\n CS-LM-PS-30   Ensure that web applications dealing with confidential or highly confidential\n                   data, logging must be enabled for traffic to track received requests and\n                  actions taken.\n CS-LM-PS-40   Must ensure that diagnostic log is enabled for data analytics tools.\n\n\n9.8 Key Management\n\n\n Control Ref #                        Security Control Description\n\n CS-LM-KM-10  Must ensure logging on CSP’s native Key Management service is enabled\n                    to detect any anomaly.\n\n\n9.9 Container\n                                                                                                \n Control Ref #                       Security Control Description\n               \nCS-LM-CT-10   Ensure that log retention is configured according to data requirements.\nCS-LM-CT-20   Must ensure that logging and monitoring of the registry activity is enabled.\n\n\n9.10 Cloud Storage\n                                                                                                \n Control Ref #                       Security Control Description\n               \nCS-LM-ST-10   Must ensure that enable and monitor access logs of the cloud storage\n                  service.\n\n\n\n\n                                              Stellantis classification\n                                  C2 – Internal                               Page 31 of 44"}, {"id": "d7-s33", "doc": 7, "title": "Page 33 · SSIT-S009-G001 STELLANTIS CLOUD SECURITY CONTROLS GUIDELINE", "html": "<div class=\"pdftext\">        SSIT-S009-G001 STELLANTIS CLOUD SECURITY CONTROLS GUIDELINE\n\n9.11 Code Repository\n                                                                                                \n Control Ref #                       Security Control Description\n               \nCS-LM-CR-10  Must ensure that logging and monitoring of the repository activity is enabled.\n\n\n10. PaaS Security\n\n\nPaaS (Platform as a Service) offers a framework and an application development platform,\n\nallowing users to easily create apps that run on cloud computing technologies. PaaS services\nmay include development tools, database management, business analytics, Operating Systems,\nServers, Storage and Networking Firewalls/security.\n\n\nThe below mentioned are minimal recommended Cloud Security Controls for PaaS Security.\nAdditional security control must be envisaged and enforced based on the application/platform\nrequirements and review of the Cloud Security team.\n\n\n10.1 General\n\n Control Ref #                        Security Control Description\n\n CS-PS-GN-10   Must ensure that separation of Dev, Prod, QA is followed by leveraging\n               CSP’s recommended approach like accounts, subscriptions, folders, etc.\n CS-PS-GN-20   Must ensure if the PaaS service offers native encryption, then it must be\n                 enabled irrespective of the confidentiality level of the data being hosted in\n                   the service.\n CS-PS-GN-30   Must ensure authentication to PaaS services using managed identity\n                    credentials which are fully managed and rotated.\n CS-PS-GN-40   Must prevent using local authentication methods for PaaS services.\n CS-PS-GN-50   Must ensure using Role based assess control to manage PaaS services.\n CS-PS-GN-60   Wherever necessary enable conditional access for the PaaS services.\n CS-PS-GN-70   Must ensure Service Principal Management is periodically assessed to\n                    validate for its authentication, access rights to enhance the security\n                   posture.\n CS-PS-GN-80   Must ensure secrets, credentials and encryption keys are stored in key\n                      vault.\n CS-PS-GN-90   Enable service provider component (equivalent to Lockbox feature in\n                  Azure) as an additional layer of restrictive control for access of the data by\n                   service provider personnel even during maintenance or support activities.\n CS-PS-GN-100  Make sure restrictions/whitelisting on outbound traffic are enforced to\n                  prevent data loss.\n\n\n\n\n                                              Stellantis classification\n                                  C2 – Internal                               Page 32 of 44<\/div>", "text": "        SSIT-S009-G001 STELLANTIS CLOUD SECURITY CONTROLS GUIDELINE\n\n9.11 Code Repository\n                                                                                                \n Control Ref #                       Security Control Description\n               \nCS-LM-CR-10  Must ensure that logging and monitoring of the repository activity is enabled.\n\n\n10. PaaS Security\n\n\nPaaS (Platform as a Service) offers a framework and an application development platform,\n\nallowing users to easily create apps that run on cloud computing technologies. PaaS services\nmay include development tools, database management, business analytics, Operating Systems,\nServers, Storage and Networking Firewalls/security.\n\n\nThe below mentioned are minimal recommended Cloud Security Controls for PaaS Security.\nAdditional security control must be envisaged and enforced based on the application/platform\nrequirements and review of the Cloud Security team.\n\n\n10.1 General\n\n Control Ref #                        Security Control Description\n\n CS-PS-GN-10   Must ensure that separation of Dev, Prod, QA is followed by leveraging\n               CSP’s recommended approach like accounts, subscriptions, folders, etc.\n CS-PS-GN-20   Must ensure if the PaaS service offers native encryption, then it must be\n                 enabled irrespective of the confidentiality level of the data being hosted in\n                   the service.\n CS-PS-GN-30   Must ensure authentication to PaaS services using managed identity\n                    credentials which are fully managed and rotated.\n CS-PS-GN-40   Must prevent using local authentication methods for PaaS services.\n CS-PS-GN-50   Must ensure using Role based assess control to manage PaaS services.\n CS-PS-GN-60   Wherever necessary enable conditional access for the PaaS services.\n CS-PS-GN-70   Must ensure Service Principal Management is periodically assessed to\n                    validate for its authentication, access rights to enhance the security\n                   posture.\n CS-PS-GN-80   Must ensure secrets, credentials and encryption keys are stored in key\n                      vault.\n CS-PS-GN-90   Enable service provider component (equivalent to Lockbox feature in\n                  Azure) as an additional layer of restrictive control for access of the data by\n                   service provider personnel even during maintenance or support activities.\n CS-PS-GN-100  Make sure restrictions/whitelisting on outbound traffic are enforced to\n                  prevent data loss.\n\n\n\n\n                                              Stellantis classification\n                                  C2 – Internal                               Page 32 of CONTROLS GUIDELINE\n\n10.2 Cloud Storage\n\n\n Control Ref #                       Security Control Description\n\nCS-PS-ST-10   Ensure that leveraging of Cloud IAM policies to control access to Object\n               Storage (bucket/Blob) and objects in Cloud Storage.\nCS-PS-ST-20  Must ensure that enforcement of fine-grained access control to individual\n                 objects within an Object Storage (bucket/Blob) using ACLs.\nCS-PS-ST-30   Ensure that depending on the classification of the data, data must be\n                 protected. KMS + CMK must be used for C4 and C3 classified data. KMS must\n              be used for non-confidential or any other classified data.\nCS-PS-ST-40  Must ensure that leveraging of object/file versioning to protect your storage\n                data from being overwritten or accidentally deleted.\nCS-PS-ST-50  Must ensure that the Object Storage/folders created are “private” by default\n              and verify if you have appropriate permissions to make anything “public.”\nCS-PS-ST-60  Must ensure that cloud deployed application access Object Storage/folders\n                 only through internal network or VPC.\nCS-PS-ST-70   Ensure that client-side encryption must be enabled at application level prior to\n                uploading data to cloud storage based on the data classification of Stellantis.\n\n\n10.3 Kubernetes\n\n\n Control Ref #                       Security Control Description\nCS-PS-KB-10   Ensure that Role Based Access Control adhered.\nCS-PS-KB-20   Restrict access to ETCD to only authorized Kubernetes components and\n                 administrators\nCS-PS-KB-30   Ensure that Kubernetes nodes are isolated based on the functionality (like\n                using VPC or Subnet or Security group).\nCS-PS-KB-40   Ensure that cloud IAM authentication for API server is enforced.\nCS-PS-KB-50  Must ensure that Kubernetes cluster access to cloud provider API follows\n                   principle of least privilege.\nCS-PS-KB-60   Ensure that network traffic is monitored to limit communications.\nCS-PS-KB-70  Must use process whitelisting for Kubernetes access.\nCS-PS-KB-80  Must ensure “Kubelet” security by disabling anonymous access.\n\n\n10.4 Relational Data Service\n\n\n Control Ref #                       Security Control Description\nCS-PS-RD-10  When creating a DB Instance, must ensure to specify the Region where the\n                 service (and related data) must be provided (and stored).\nCS-PS-RD-20  Ensure that the database instance is placed in a virtual private cloud (VPC)\n              making it accessible only from the internal network and not exposed\n                  externally.\nCS-PS-RD-30  Must authenticate DB instance using service providers Identity and Access\n             Management (IAM)/domain federated user for database authentication.\nCS-PS-RD-40  Ensure that there is no use of local database users.\n\n\n\n                                              Stellantis classification\n                                  C2 – Internal                               Page 33 of 44<\/div>", "text": "        SSIT-S009-G001 STELLANTIS CLOUD SECURITY CONTROLS GUIDELINE\n\n10.2 Cloud Storage\n\n\n Control Ref # Link: SSIT-S009 Cloud Security\n               Standard\nCS-PS-RD-100 Must leverage customer-managed keys for data encryption for confidential and\n                  highly confidential data storing.\nCS-PS-RD-110 Must always enforce TLS connections between database server and client\n                  applications in order to protect against &quot;man in the middle&quot; attacks by\n                encrypting the data stream between the server and your application.\n\n\n10.5 Data Warehouse\n\n\n Control Ref #                       Security Control Description\nCS-PS-DW-10  Must ensure that separate administrative users are created for Data\n               warehouse.\nCS-PS-DW-20  Ensure that inbound traffic to Data warehouse is tightened using Security\n                groups.\nCS-PS-DW-30  Must consider column level access control for distinct groups for the same\n                   table.\nCS-PS-DW-40  Data must be encrypted using CMK for confidentiality and high confidential for\n                data loads.\nCS-PS-DW-50  Must ensure that restrictive privileges to groups and users are granted.\n\n10.6 NoSQL\n\n\n Control Ref #                       Security Control Description\n\nCS-PS-SV-10  Must ensure that the least access privilege rule is implemented and adhered\n                     to.\nCS-PS-SV-20  Must ensure encryption of the data using CMK at rest in the storage layer\n               depending on data confidentiality.\nCS-PS-SV-30   Ensure that HTTPS is enforced for Elastic Beanstalk based on application\n                requirements.\nCS-PS-SV-40  Must ensure that the health of Java, .Net, Container, PHP and other\n                  applications are monitored in the health console.\nCS-PS-SV-50  Must restrict Beanstalk user access and service role to only the resources it\n              needs to run the applications.\n\n10.10 Simple Email Service\n\n\n Control Ref # VDI Security\n\nVirtual Desktop infrastructure (VDI) is a software tool to centrally create and manage virtual\n\ndesktops. There are two types of virtual desktop infrastructure (VDI) deployment methods:\npersistent VDI and nonpersistent VDI and security control specified in this document are common\nfor both types of VDIs.’\n\n\nThe below mentioned are minimal recommended Cloud Security Controls for VDI. Additional\nsecurity control must be envisaged and enforced based on the application/platform requirements\nand review of the Cloud Security team.\n\n\n\n11.1 General\n\n\n Control Ref #                        Security Control Description\n\n CS-VD-GN-10  Must ensure that Golden Images of VDI are updated every 3 months.\n CS-VD-GN-20  Must ensure that the adherence of Stellantis patching policy and its\n              management for VDI images.\n CS-VD-GN-30  Must ensure that Multi Factor Authentication is enforced for VDI access.\n CS-VD-GN-40  Must ensure that Conditional access which applies access controls based\n               on signals like group membership, IP address, type of device to enforce\n                    policies followed.\n CS-VD-GN-50  Must ensure that access of peripherals like printers and scanners is need\n                 based.\n CS-VD-GN-60  Must ensure that file transfers like FTP/SFTP from VDI to non-VDI\n                 environment (outside of Stellantis) are restricted.\n CS-VD-GN-70  Ensure that encryption is enforced for data/files created/accessed based on\n                     Stellantis confidentiality policy.\n CS-VD-GN-80  Must ensure that a monitoring mechanism for connections to VDI exists to\n                     identify anomalous access behavior.\n\n\n12. Application Security\n\nStellantis is responsible for security of all applications owned by the company. This includes new\nprojects, program developments, major enhancements, program changes, emergency changes,\nscheduled releases, and non-scheduled releases; all are in scope for Stellantis (FCA) Application\nSecurity Program (ASP).\n\n\nIt critical that developers understand the Application security requirements based on the\n\n\n\n\n                                              Stellantis classification\n                                  C2 – Internal                               Page 36 of 44<\/div>", "text": "        SSIT-S009-G001 STELLANTIS CLOUD SECURITY CONTROLS GUIDELINE\n\n11.         monthly by Stellantis approved scanner (e.g., Qualys)\nCS-AS-GN-190   Open-source libraries must be scanned as a part of the SAST of the\n                    project.\nCS-AS-GN-200  Must breaches.\nCS-AS-GN-210  Must ensure that your application is not deployed within the default Virtual\n                   Private Cloud in order to follow security best practices and protect your\n                  instances against unauthorized access.\nCS-AS-GN-220  Must ensure that encryption with customer-managed keys (CMK) is\n                  configured whenever the application is dealing HTTPS only setting.\nCS-AS-GN-250  Must ensure that vault use per application per environment (e.g.,\n                Development, Pre-Production and Production) so as not to share secrets\n from the server,\n                   including scripts and executable code.\n\n\n\n\n                                            Stellantis classification\n                                 C2 –     SSIT-S009-G001 STELLANTIS CLOUD SECURITY CONTROLS GUIDELINE\n\n CS-AS-GN-330  Must ensure that reconfiguration of HTTP service banners (and others as\n                    required) for not to report Web server, OS type and version is taken care.\n CS-AS-GN-340  Must ensure that service processes are configured to run as a user with a\n                         strictly limited set of privileges (i.e., not running as root, administrator, or\n                     equivalent).\n CS-AS-GN-350   Ensure that web content files are read only and not written by service\n                   processes.\n CS-AS-GN-360  Must configure the Web server process to run as a user with a strictly\n                      limited set of privileges.\n CS-AS-GN-370   Ensure that anti-spambot protection, if appropriate (e.g., CAPTCHAs,\n                    nofollow, or keyword filtering) are configured.\n CS-AS-GN-380   Ensure that assessment and disable of non-interactive accounts are\n                  performed.\n CS-AS-GN-390  Must ensure that log files are stored in a location that is sized\n                     appropriately. Ideally, log files should be stored on a separate partition.\n CS-AS-GN-400  Must ensure a limit on the amount of hard drive space that is dedicated for\n                   uploads,  if uploads to the Web server are allowed.\n CS-AS-GN-410   Ensure to utilize service provider&#x27;s DDoS protection services to prevent\n             DDoS attacks.\n CS-AS-GN-420     It is required that the security score of the application environment is\n                  maintained at 90 or higher at all the times.\n CS-AS-GN-430  Must ensure that any Critical Application deployed in the cloud is subjected\n                     to PenTesting before going live. Vulnerabilities detected upon the PenTest\n                must be remediated per CISO requirements\n\n\n\n12.2 Code Repository\n\n Control Ref #                       Security Control Description\n\nCS-AS-CR-30  Must ensure that Stellantis IAM policies are enforced to control access to the\n              code repositories.\nCS-AS-CR-40  Ensure that the “root” user for connecting to the repository is restricted. (The\n              use of the &#x27;root&#x27; or any highly privileged account for connecting to application\n                  repositories must be strictly restricted. Such accounts should only be used for\n              emergency or administrative tasks, and access must be logged, monitored,\n              and approved through a formal process).\nCS-AS-CR-50  Must ensure that repositories are created “private” by default and monitor for\n                  accidentally enabled “public” repositories.\nCS-AS-CR-60  Must ensure periodic scanning of the repositories for hardcoded passwords\n              and sensitive information.\nCS-AS-CR-70  Must ensure and enforce use of two-factor authentication when accessing the\n              code repository or Stellantis approved VPN solution.\nCS-AS-CR-100 Must enforce least privilege policy for who can make changes to code\n                  repository.\nCS-AS-CR-105 Must ensure that changes performed by user in code repositories are\n                   attributable.\nCS-AS-CR-110 Must ensure that repositories have a Markdown file (e.g., SECURITY.md file)\n               comprise with a security policy which would offers instruction on reporting\n                  security vulnerabilities in a project by user to Repository maintainers.\n\n\n\n                                              Stellantis CONTROLS GUIDELINE", "html": "<div class=\"pdftext\">        SSIT-S009-G001 STELLANTIS CLOUD SECURITY CONTROLS GUIDELINE\n\nCS-AS-CR-120 Must ensure that “repository” creation/deletion is limited to authorized user.\nCS-AS-CR-130 Must ensure that “issue” deletion is limited to specific users.\nCS-AS-CR-140 Must ensure that all copies (forks) of code are tracked and accounted.\nCS-AS-CR-150 Must ensure that inactive users are reviewed and removed automatically\n              based on the period defined by the Stellantis DevOps team.\nCS-AS-CR-160 Must ensure that Code Repository access is limited based on IP addresses\n                   (whitelisting by Stellantis).\nCS-AS-CR-170 Must ensure that only user with the &quot;@stellantis.com&quot; domain or Stellantis\n                federated IDs are allowed to join the repositories.\nCS-AS-CR-180 Must ensure that an organization’s identity is confirmed with a “verified” or\n                “approved” or “trusted” badge in code repository (depends on the code\n                  repository being used.\nCS-AS-CR-190 Must ensure that Source Code Management (SCM) email notifications are\n                   restricted to Stellantis mail domain.\nCS-AS-CR-200 Must ensure that Stellantis-Code Repository provided SSH certificates are\n               enforced for access to code repository.\n\n\n12.3 Mobile Application\n\nThe below mentioned are minimal recommended Security Controls  for Mobile Application\ndevelopment.  Additional  security control must be envisaged and enforced based on the\napplication/platform requirements and review of the Cloud Security team.\n\n\n\n Control Ref #                        Security Control Description\n\n CS-AS-MB-10   Ensure that Stellantis Application Security DevSecOps Program prescribed\n                  Mobile Secure Coding Guidelines must be followed for Android as well iOS.\n CS-AS-MB-20   Ensure and must configure automatic session locking on enterprise assets\n                     after a defined period of inactivity. For general purpose operating systems,\n                   the period must not exceed 15 minutes. For mobile end-user devices, the\n                   period must not exceed 2 minutes.\n CS-AS-MB-30   Must ensure that separate enterprise workspaces are used on mobile end-\n                  user devices, where supported (example implementations include using an\n                 Apple Configuration Profile or Android Work Profile to separate enterprise\n                    applications and data from personal applications and data.\n CS-AS-MB-40   Ensure that, in order to reduce attack vectors, API-Keys must be restricted\n                   only to trusted hosts, HTTP referrers and applications.\n CS-AS-MB-50   Must ensure that no hardcode secrets in source code or configuration files.\n CS-AS-MB-60      It must ensure that code obfuscation and reverse engineering protection\n                  should be looked for for mobile applications intended to run on untrusted\n                   endpoints, such as customer endpoints.\n CS-AS-MB-70   Must ensure to use the permissions really required by the application.\n                  Overly permissioned applications are susceptible to permission re-\n                   delegation attacks.\n CS-AS-MB-80   Must ensure that Client-side Biometric authentication is tightly tied to\n                    authentication hardware not only software API.\n\n\n\n                                              Stellantis CONTROLS GUIDELINE", "html": "<div class=\"pdftext\">        SSIT-S009-G001 STELLANTIS CLOUD SECURITY CONTROLS GUIDELINE\n\n CS-AS-MB-90   Ensure that all sensitive information must, without exception, be protected\n                by encryption in transport (i.e., TLS) where confidential information is pre-\n                  encrypted before transport, then decrypted by the receiver.\n CS-AS-MB-100  Must ensure that two-factor authentication is enabled for all enterprise\n                    application access on personal mobile devices.\n\n\n13. Generative AI and Agentic AI Security\n\nGenerative artificial intelligence is an artificial intelligence capable of generating text, images, or\nother media, using generative models. Generative AI models learn the patterns and structure of\ntheir input training data and then generate new data that has similar characteristics.\n\n\nThe below mentioned are minimal recommended Cloud Security Controls for Generative AI.\nAdditional security control must be envisaged and enforced based on the application/platform\n\nrequirements and review of the Cloud Security team.\n\n\n13.1 General\n\nGenerative AI technology, especially models trained on vast amounts of data, poses distinct risks\nconcerning the privacy of sensitive data.\n\n  Control Ref #                        Security Control Description\n\n CS-GA-GN-10   Ensure that PII data is either removed or obfuscated from data sets before\n                     training the Gen AI service.\n\n CS-GA-GN-20   Must ensure that data-at-rest is encrypted with customer-managed keys\n                based on data classification.\n CS-GA-GN-30   Must ensure data-in-transit is encrypted with TLS 1.2 or higher.\n CS-GA-GN-40   Must ensure data is sanitized and only necessary data as per use case is\n                  fed into Gen AI service.\n CS-GA-GN-50   Must ensure the least-privilege principle is followed for giving access to Gen\n                  AI services.\n CS-GA-GN-60   Must ensure RBAC and ABAC (attribute-based access control) method is\n                   followed for giving access to Gen AI services and access between zones.\n CS-GA-GN-70   Must ensure logging and monitoring of access logs and activity logs for Gen\n                  AI services are implemented.\n CS-GA-GN-80   Must ensure to select private Gen AI service which is isolated and not\n                 shared by any other party other than Stellantis\n CS-GA-GN-90   Wherever supported ensure that Federated Identities are used for\n                    authenticating to PaaS services.\n CS-GA-GN-100  Enable service provider component (equivalent to Lockbox feature in Azure)\n                as an additional layer of restrictive control for access of the data by service\n                   provider personnel even during maintenance or support activities.\n CS-GA-GN-110  Where possible make sure that the connection from a virtual network\n                 (VPC/Vnet) to a PaaS endpoint is private.\n\n\n                                              Stellantis classification\n                                  C2 – Internal                               Page 41 of 44<\/div>", "text": "        SSIT-S009-G001 STELLANTIS CLOUD SECURITY CONTROLS GUIDELINE\n\n CS-AS-MB-90   Ensure that all sensitive information must,     SSIT-S009-G001 STELLANTIS CLOUD SECURITY CONTROLS GUIDELINE\n\n CS-GA-GN-120  Where possible make sure restrictions/whitelisting is enforced on PaaS\n                   endpoints.\n CS-GA-GN-130  Enable telemetry (the automated process of collecting, transmitting, and\n                   analyzing logs i.e. detailed records of events from remote systems for\n                   monitoring and analysis) and logging on all AI components\n CS-GA-GN-140  Use AI/ML-based anomaly detection to monitor model inputs/outputs.\n CS-GA-GN-150  Trigger alerts on policy violations, data exfiltration, or usage anomalies\n CS-GA-GN-160  Apply offensive security techniques (e.g., fuzzing, adversarial testing) to\n                      identify vulnerabilities in AI models and workflows.\n CS-GA-GN-170  Must test AI systems for susceptibility to prompt injection attacks by\n                   simulating malicious input scenarios and validating model responses.\n CS-GA-GN-180  Must monitor AI outputs for signs of goal misalignment and implement\n                  safeguards to prevent unintended behavior or objective shifts.\n\n\n14. Backup and Restoration Standard\n\n\nFor backup and restore requirements for cloud assets, you may refer the appropriate section of\n\nthe below document:\n\n\n   SSIT-S006 Backup and Restoration Standard\n    https://docinfogroupe.stellantis.com/ead/doc/ref.00909_24_03774/v.dp/pj\n\n\n15. Contingency Management Standard\n\n\nFor Business Continuity requirements, you may refer to the below document:\n\n\n   SSIT-S008 Contingency Management Standard\n    https://docinfogroupe.stellantis.com/ead/doc/ref.00909_24_03816/v.dp/pj\n\n\n\n\n\n                                              Stellantis classification\n                                  C2 – Internal                               Page 42 of 44<\/div>", "text": "        SSIT-S009-G001 STELLANTIS CLOUD SECURITY CONTROLS GUIDELINE\n\n CS-GA-GN-120  Where possible make sure restrictions/whitelisting is enforced on PaaS\n                   endpoints.\n CS-GA-GN-130  Enable telemetry (the automated process of collecting, transmitting, and\n                   analyzing logs i.e. detailed records of events from remote systems for\n                   monitoring and analysis) and logging on all AI components\n CS-GA-GN-140  Use AI/ML-based anomaly detection to monitor model inputs/outputs.\n CS-GA-GN-150  Trigger alerts on policy violations, data exfiltration, or usage anomalies\n CS-GA-GN-160  Apply offensive security techniques (e.g., fuzzing, adversarial testing) to\n                      identify vulnerabilities in AI models and workflows.\n CS-GA-GN-170  Must test AI systems for susceptibility to prompt injection attacks by\n                   simulating malicious input scenarios and validating model responses.\n CS-GA-GN-180  Must monitor AI outputs for signs of goal misalignment and implement\n                  safeguards to prevent unintended behavior or objective shifts.\n\n\n14. Backup and Restoration Standard\n\n\nFor backup and restore requirements for cloud assets, you may refer the appropriate section of\n\nthe below document:\n\n\n   SSIT-S006 Backup and Restoration Standard\n    https://docinfogroupe.stellantis.com/ead/doc/ref.00909_24_03774/v.dp/pj\n\n\n15. Tokens\n BC   Business Continuity    CH   Container Hosts          CR  Code Repository\n DM  Dormant User        DR  Data at Rest            DE  Data Stream\n DS   Directory Services     DT  Data in Transit           DU  Data in Use\n DW  Datawarehouse       EN  Encryptions             ES  SES (Simple Email Service)\n FW   Firewall           GN  General                          IF    Internet          Page 3 sur 35"}, {"id": "d8-s4", "doc": 8, "title": "Page 4 · Solution architecture requirements, general principles", "html": "<div class=\"pdftext\">Solution architecture requirements, general principles\n\nSTELLANTIS has a Cloud first based strategy. So, the architecture proposed for the solution\nshould be a Cloud-based solution based on standard platforms and interfaces.\nThe architecture of the new platform is based upon the statements including the following:\n\n- The system architecture must be scalable, can be expanded easily and should provide an open\narchitecture with a modular design that supports incorporation of new modules, integration of\nlegacy systems without the need for a major redesign.\n\n- The solution must implement the technical baseline integrating all the technical prerequisites\n(architecture, interfaces, security ...).\n\n- The solution should be able to consume SOAP and REST web services with mutual authentication.\n\n- The Platform should be able to expose APIs in Rest / JSON mode\n\n- The system needs to be able to interface with legacy system and the STELLANTIS partner’s\ninformation system (real-time, scheduled batch, and on-demand interfaces…). Data must be\nexchanged between systems easily.\n\n- Batch processing and new release delivery should not affect availability and response times.\n\n- Perform batch transfers by using STELLANTIS SFTP as general rule (some exceptions could be\nconsidered). Also, Provider have to accept to use a file Transfer Manager (i.e. Connect Direct) if\nrequested by STELLANTIS for some or all transfers. Indeed, a maximum volume will be indicated\nby STELLANTIS. The system must be able to compress data during exchanges if relevant. The\nsolution on the provider side must be able also to accept input compressed files (or file groups).\n\n- There should be no constraints of installation or configuration of the workstations, allowing its\naccess in heterogeneous device environments (positions constrained by STELLANTIS Group\nsecurity standards or those of the providers having access to the application).\n\n- Failover architecture to help to ensure high availability of the network manager installation is\nrequired.\n\n- Security by design must be applied since the beginning of projects.\n\n\n\n\n\n                                                                     Page 4 sur 35<\/div>", "text": "Solution architecture requirements, general principles\n\nSTELLANTIS has a Cloud first based strategy. So, the architecture proposed for the solution\nshould be a Cloud-based solution based on standard platforms and interfaces.\nThe architecture of the new platform is based upon the statements including the following:\n\n- The system architecture must be scalable, can be expanded easily and should provide an open\narchitecture with a modular design that supports incorporation of new modules, integration of\nlegacy systems without the need for a major redesign.\n\n- The solution must implement the technical baseline integrating all the technical prerequisites\n(architecture, interfaces, security ...).\n\n- The solution should be able to consume SOAP and REST web services with mutual authentication.\n\n- The Platform should be able to expose APIs in Rest / JSON mode\n\n- The system needs to be able to interface with legacy system and the STELLANTIS partner’s\ninformation system (real-time, scheduled batch, and on-demand interfaces…). Data must be\nexchanged between systems easily.\n\n- Batch processing and new release delivery should not affect availability and response times.\n\n- Perform batch transfers by using STELLANTIS SFTP as general rule (some exceptions could be\nconsidered). Also, Provider have to accept to use a file Transfer Manager (i.e. Connect Direct) if\nrequested by STELLANTIS for some or all transfers. Indeed, a maximum volume will be indicated\nby STELLANTIS. The system must be able to compress data during exchanges if relevant. The\nsolution on the provider side must be able also to accept input compressed files (or file groups).\n\n- There should be no constraints of installation or configuration of the workstations, allowing its\naccess in heterogeneous device environments (positions constrained by STELLANTIS Group\nsecurity standards or those of the providers having access to the application).\n\n- Failover architecture to help to ensure high availability of the network manager installation is\nrequired.\n\n- Security by design must be applied since the beginning of projects.\n\n\n\n\n\n                                                                     Page 4 sur 35"}, {"id": "d8-s5", "doc": 8, "title": "Page 5 · -   Architecture Schema", "html": "<div class=\"pdftext\">1  Hosting\n\n     -   Architecture Schema\n     -   Cloud first\n     -   PaaS managed services / multi-Datacenter / Business Continuity Plan\n     -   Business Continuity plan/ Backup Restore\n     -   Cost optimization / flexibility\n     -   Reversibility plan\n\n1.1  Architecture Description of the solution\n   EXECUTIVE LEVEL DESCRIPTION\n    Architecture diagram of the solution\n   What is the architecture diagram?\n\n   REQUIREMENT\n   The Supplier is requested to supply complete and detailed functional and technical architecture\n    description of their solution. Not mandatory for SaaS, where a high-level schema can be provided.\n   CONTENTS EXPECTED IN RESPONSE TO THE REQUIREMENT (GUIDELINES)\n     -   Architecture diagrams if possible\n     -   Detail of components, and their interfaces, both to external system and within the schema\n     -   Technical details like server types, network, etc.\n     -   Specify components that are open source or not\n     -     ... whatever can be useful to evaluate and understand the architecture of the proposed\n        solution\n\n\n1.2 Cloud first: the hosting of the solution\n   EXECUTIVE LEVEL DESCRIPTION\n    This requirement covers the hosting of the solution provided by the supplier.\n      Is the application design for Cloud hosting at first or is it an on-premises app moved to\n    the Cloud?\n\n   REQUIREMENT\n   The hosting of the solution provided by the supplier should be in the public Cloud.\n      If not possible or depending on the use case - in agreement with STELLANTIS and depending on\n    the chosen technologies - if the solution is designed in STELLANTIS data centers or in Supplier’s\n    Private Cloud, the technical architecture of the solution must be validated by STELLANTIS.\n    For reasons of cost and compliance for example, STELLANTIS can impose hosting in its own data\n    centers, or in a cloud hosting service owned by STELLANTIS.\n      If hosted within STELLANTIS, the software versions used  in the technical stack must be\n   communicated prior to the design phase.\n    Hosting solution must follow the Security Laws.\n   CONTENTS EXPECTED IN RESPONSE TO THE REQUIREMENT (GUIDELINES)\n    In the case of a major public Cloud provider, the use of the AWS Cloud or Microsoft Azure or other\n   major provider in the market under STELLANTIS agreement will be preferred but it could be hosted\n    in the provider’s private Cloud and need to be validated by STELLANTIS.\n\n\n                                                                         Page 5 sur 35<\/div>", "text": "1  Hosting\n\n     - in agreement with STELLANTIS and depending on\n    the chosen technologies - if the solution is designed in STELLANTIS data centers or in Supplier’s\n    Private Cloud, the technical architecture of the solution must be validated by STELLANTIS.\n    For reasons of cost and compliance for example, STELLANTIS can impose hosting in its own data\n    centers, or in a cloud hosting service owned by STELLANTIS.\n      If hosted within STELLANTIS, the software versions used  in the technical stack must be\n   communicated prior to the design phase.\n    Hosting solution must follow the Security Laws.\n   CONTENTS EXPECTED IN RESPONSE TO THE REQUIREMENT (GUIDELINES)\n    In the case of a major public Cloud provider, the use of the AWS Cloud or Microsoft Azure or other\n   major provider in the market under STELLANTIS agreement will be preferred but it could be hosted\n    in the provider’s private Cloud and need to be validated by STELLANTIS.\n\n\n                                                                         Page 5 sur 35"}, {"id": "d8-s6", "doc": 8, "title": "Page 6 · 1.3 PaaS managed services / multi-Datacenter / Business Continuity Plan", "html": "<div class=\"pdftext\">1.3 PaaS managed services / multi-Datacenter / Business Continuity Plan\n   EXECUTIVE LEVEL DESCRIPTION\n    This requirement covers the Cloud Computing Models used by the solution and the redundancy of\n    the solution.\n           -   High level: Software as a Service (SaaS)\n           -   High level: Platform as a Service (PaaS)\n           -  Low level: Container as a Service (CaaS)\n           -  Low level: Infrastructure as a Service (IaaS)\n\n    Are you using high-level managed services offered by the Cloud provider? Are you using\n    a kind of PaaS or CaaS services for application code, database, assets? Is it a proprietary\n    Cloud provider technology? Are you using multi-region or multi-datacenter to replicate\n     application code and/or data?\n\n\n   REQUIREMENT\n   The architecture of the new platform is based upon a failover architecture to help ensure high\n    availability of the solution. A multi-datacenter is required.\n   The provider must expressively understand and accept that the location of the data, especially\n    personal data but not limited to them, can be an issue, due to legal or opportunity privacy\n    constraints. Upon STELLANTIS request, provider must be able to store all or part of the data in\n    different geographic locations without change in cost and/or impact on performances and\n    software way of work.\n   The provider should describe the model used for the solution and the product.\n    For reasons of cost and compliance, high-level managed services are often preferred and at least\n   CaaS can be requested and the proprietary platform model which are under licenses need to be\n    exposed.\n   The IaaS oriented solution are often Hand Managed platform. This model needs to be validated\n    with STELLANTIS.\n   CONTENTS EXPECTED IN RESPONSE TO THE REQUIREMENT (GUIDELINES)\n   The use of the proposed models by the provider should be described.\n   The use of multi-datacenter.\n   The understanding of geographic data storage issue and the complying with the requirement\n   The description of the level of services.\n   Here are some examples of bricks/products on the marketplace with their models.\n\n         SaaS: Salesforce, Zuora, Office 365, Adobe Experience Manager, Github …\n         PaaS: Fargate and ECS (AWS), Aurora DB (AWS), Flexible DB (Azure) …\n         CaaS: Openshift (IBM), EKS (AWS), AKS (Azure), Kubernetes (no proprietary or license free)\n          IaaS: Virtual Machines, File Systems, Load Balancers …\n\n1.4  Business Continuity plan/ Backup Restore\n   EXECUTIVE LEVEL DESCRIPTION\n\n\n                                                                         Page 6 sur 35<\/div>", "text": "1.3 PaaS managed services / multi-Datacenter / Business Continuity Plan\n   EXECUTIVE LEVEL DESCRIPTION\n    This requirement covers the Cloud Computing Models used by the solution and the redundancy of\n    the solution.\n           -   High level: Software as a Service (SaaS)\n           -   High level: Platform as a Service (PaaS)\n           -  Low level: Container as a Service (CaaS)\n           -  Low level: Infrastructure as a Service (IaaS)\n\n    Are you using high-level managed services offered by the Cloud provider? Upon STELLANTIS request, provider must be able to store all or part of the data in\n    different geographic locations without change in cost and/or impact on performances and\n    software way of work.\n   The provider should describe the model used for the solution and the product.\n    For reasons of cost and compliance, high-level managed services are often preferred and at least\n   CaaS can be requested and the proprietary platform model which are under licenses need to be\n    exposed.\n   The IaaS oriented solution are often Hand Managed platform. This model needs to be validated\n    with STELLANTIS.\n   CONTENTS EXPECTED IN RESPONSE TO THE REQUIREMENT (GUIDELINES)\n   The use of the proposed models by the provider should be described.\n   The use of multi-datacenter.\n   The understanding of geographic data storage issue and the complying with the requirement\n   The description of the level of services.\n   Here are some examples of bricks/products on the marketplace with their models.\n\n         SaaS: Salesforce, Zuora, Office 365, Adobe Experience Manager, Github …\n         PaaS: Fargate and ECS (AWS), Aurora DB (AWS), Flexible DB (Azure) …\n         CaaS: Openshift (IBM), EKS (AWS), AKS (Azure), Kubernetes (no proprietary or license free)\n          IaaS: Virtual Machines, File Systems, Load Balancers …\n\n1.4  Business Continuity plan/ Backup Restore\n   EXECUTIVE LEVEL DESCRIPTION\n\n\n                                                                         Page 6 sur 35"}, {"id": "d8-s7", "doc": 8, "title": "Page 7 · This requirement covers the part concerning the strategy of Backup restoration & Disaster", "html": "<div class=\"pdftext\">    This requirement covers the part concerning the strategy of Backup restoration &amp; Disaster\n   Recovery Plan.\n   The DRP applies in case of a major disaster, for example a crash of infrastructure due to all the\n    datacenters becoming unavailable.\n    For all other cases, for example in case of a crash of infrastructure linked to actions done by the\n    project team, the SLA applies.\n\n   What happens in case of a datacenter failure? Is there a Disaster Recovery Plan?\n    Recovery Time Objective? Recovery Point Objective? How are data backed up?\n\n   REQUIREMENT\n       •  RPO (recovery point objective): 24 Hours (in case of a crash of the infrastructure, the last\n         24H data created/updated are lost)\n       •  RTO (recovery time objective): 72 Hours (in case of a crash of the infrastructure, platform\n           not available during 3 days)\n       •  The way data, configuration and specific development are secured and backup\n       •  Backup strategy: Real-time or delay. If delay, please indicate this delay\n                -   Incremental: daily\n                -    Full: weekly\n       •   Risks on customer side if a DRP is activated\n       •   Limitation of this DRP: who can activate? How? Etc.\n                -   Restoration: Provider should describe how to do partial restoration or segmentation\n       •   Import / Export: Provider should describe how to import / export data according to\n            selection criteria (idem segmentation criteria)\n       •  Data isolation: By default, platform must use a logic data isolation at Brand &amp; Country\n             levels, especially for import/export or backup of data\n   STELLANTIS Group must have the possibility to locally host a platform containing the full copy of\n    the main structured data recorded in the platform (Accounts, Contacts, Sales, Activities…  ),\n   metadata and configuration attributes (habilitation, etc..). This backup should allow STELLANTIS\n   Group to easily perform a data/configuration restoration.\n   CONTENTS EXPECTED IN RESPONSE TO THE REQUIREMENT (GUIDELINES)\n   The provider should precise in detail:\n                -  RPO (recovery point objective)\n                -  RTO (recovery time objective)\n   And the strategy concerning the Backup restoration &amp; Disaster Recovery Plan.\n\n\n1.5  Cost optimization / flexibility\n   EXECUTIVE LEVEL DESCRIPTION\n    This requirement covers the financial optimization of the solution provided.\n      Is the infrastructure cost known and tracked? Is there an objective / KPI shared with the\n    dev team about cost? Is there alert on cost? Is the application scale (in/out – up-down)\n    depending on the load? Is it done automatically and/or with a provisioning roadmap?\n\n   REQUIREMENT\n\n\n\n                                                                         Page 7 sur 35<\/div>", "text": "    This requirement covers the part concerning the strategy of Backup restoration & Disaster\n   Recovery Plan.\n   The DRP applies in case of a major disaster, for example a crash of infrastructure due to all the\n    datacenters becoming unavailable.\n    For all other cases, for example in case of a crash of infrastructure linked to actions done by the\n    project team, the SLA applies.\n\n   What happens in case of a datacenter failure? Is there a Disaster Recovery Plan?\n    Recovery Time Objective? Recovery Point Objective? How are data backed up?\n\n   REQUIREMENT\n       •  RPO (recovery point objective): 24 Hours (in case of a crash of the infrastructure, the last\n         24H data created/updated are lost)\n       •  RTO (recovery time objective): 72 Hours (in case of a crash of the infrastructure, platform\n           not available during 3 days)\n       •  The way data, configuration and specific development are secured and backup\n       •  Backup strategy: Real-time or delay. If delay, please indicate this delay\n                -   Incremental: daily\n                -    Full: weekly\n       •   Risks on customer side if a DRP is activated\n       •   Limitation of this DRP: who can activate? How? Etc.\n                -   Restoration: Provider should describe how to do partial restoration or segmentation\n       •   Import / Export: Provider should describe how to import / export data according to\n            selection criteria (idem segmentation criteria)\n       •  Data isolation: By default, platform must use a logic data isolation at Brand & Country\n             levels, especially for import/export or backup of data\n   STELLANTIS Group must have the possibility to locally host a platform containing the full copy of\n    the main structured data recorded in the platform (Accounts, Contacts, Sales, Activities…  ),\n   metadata and configuration attributes (habilitation, etc..). This backup should allow STELLANTIS\n   Group to easily perform a data/configuration restoration.\n   CONTENTS EXPECTED IN RESPONSE TO THE REQUIREMENT (GUIDELINES)\n   The provider should precise in detail:\n                -  RPO (recovery point objective)\n                -  RTO (recovery time objective)\n   And the strategy concerning the Backup restoration & Disaster Recovery Plan.\n\n\n1.5  Cost optimization / flexibility\n   EXECUTIVE LEVEL DESCRIPTION\n    This requirement covers the financial optimization of the solution provided.\n      Is the infrastructure cost known and tracked? Is it done automatically and/or with a provisioning roadmap?\n\n   REQUIREMENT\n\n\n\n                                                                         Page 7 sur 35"}, {"id": "d8-s8", "doc": 8, "title": "Page 8 · The provider must be able to warn STELLANTIS in the event of the fixed price being exceeded as", "html": "<div class=\"pdftext\">   The provider must be able to warn STELLANTIS in the event of the fixed price being exceeded as\n    well as the associated reasons.\n    In the event of an additional infrastructure modification, the supplier must validate with\n   STELLANTIS the increase in associated infrastructure costs, if necessary.\n   CONTENTS EXPECTED IN RESPONSE TO THE REQUIREMENT (GUIDELINES)\n   There is a cost tracking and notification in the event of a risk of budget overruns.\n    Transparency in cost management if necessary.\n\n\n1.6  Reversibility plan\n   EXECUTIVE LEVEL DESCRIPTION\n    This requirement covers the Reversibility plan for technical, economic or strategic reasons.\n      Is the app locked with the Cloud hosting service? Is the effort to move from a Cloud\n     provider to another known and tracked?\n\n   REQUIREMENT\n      It is necessary to study the possibility and feasibility, in the event of an exogenous and external\n    scenario, for instance in the event of a break in a commercial relationship in a country, of installing\n    the application or the platform at STELLANTIS or to another provider. The provider acknowledges\n    that its ability to effectuate the reversibility operations constitutes an essential element of the\n    Contract for STELLANTIS.\n   CONTENTS EXPECTED IN RESPONSE TO THE REQUIREMENT (GUIDELINES)\n      If feasible, describe the possibilities and efforts required to move the application (code &amp; data) to\n   another supplier.\n\n   The reversibility operations shall specifically include the following:\n    Guidelines:\n    Restitution by the provider of\n       •  Customer Data, in the manner format and timing agreed to by the Parties. The provider\n              shall, unless legally prohibited, delete all copies of Customer Data in its possession, custody\n           or control;\n       •   Personal Information, in the manner format and timing agreed to by the Parties. The\n            Supplier shall, unless legally prohibited, delete all copies of Personal Information in its\n            possession, custody or control;\n       •  Documents entrusted to the provider for the performance of the works, in the manner\n           format and timing agreed to by the Parties;\n       •   Results.
