The\ncumulative rollback plan will describe the services and the respective tasks to be accomplished by the\nprovider, on one hand, and STELLANTIS or a third-party contractor, on the other hand.\nTechnical assistance of the supplier enabling STELLANTIS or a third-party contractor to acquire the\nnecessary knowledge (upon request)\nThis task consists in enabling STELLANTIS or the third-party contractor to become familiar with the\nmethods and tools used by the Provider to perform ensure the maintenance of the solution.\n\n\n\n\n\n                                                                         Page 9 sur 35"}, {"id": "d8-s10", "doc": 8, "title": "Page 10 · 2  Security & privacy by design", "html": "<div class=\"pdftext\">2  Security &amp; privacy by design\n\n     -  GDPR/ Personal Data encryption (inside Database) / DCP encryption (inside Database)\n     -   identity federation\n     -   https\n     -  Web App Firewall\n     -  No unsecure software (e.g. WordPress)\n     -   Cloud Security\n     -   Traceability\n     -   Security audits realized\n     -   General security requirements\n\n2.1 GDPR/ Personal Data encryption (inside Database) / DCP encryption\n     (inside Database)\n   EXECUTIVE LEVEL DESCRIPTION\n    This requirement covers the protection of natural persons with regard to the processing of\n    personal data and on the free movement of such data.\n    Are there any personal data inside the database? Are they encrypted? How can they be\n    decrypted? Where is the cipher key? Who can update the key? Is there a known and\n    working process to revoke and replace the key in case of data or server failure?\n\n   REQUIREMENT\n   STELLANTIS Group will pay particular attention to security requirements and conditions notably\n    for data privacy rules, data center security and ability to audit security conditions.\n   Data location and data privacy requirements: All data remains the property of STELLANTIS Group.\n   The Provider should indicate to STELLANTIS Group the data location and all backups. The Provider\n    should comply with local data privacy rules and put in place monitoring to remain compliant. The\n    suppliers will also describe how it:\n       •  Guarantees confidentiality of STELLANTIS Group data\n       •   Secures from external intrusion\n       •  Manages data encryption\n       •   Ensures to remain compliant with each local data privacy rules.\n   The proposed solution will have to comply with general guidelines from STELLANTIS in terms of\n    architecture and security rules and local GDPR or Personal data policy The solution will have reuse\n    (or interface with) some digital assets from STELLANTIS for specific functions (authentication,\n    survey tool...)\n\n\n    For end customer consent management, solution must comply with Security Law, and provide but\n    not limited to following functions:\n           -   Displaying consent pop-ups and widgets to users;\n           -   Collecting and storing information about visitor consent decisions, and keeping record of\n          changes thereof;\n           -   Before consent is given, collecting only pre-approved data by firing only accepted tags.\n           -   Interfaces security type patterns of the stat of art will be implemented.\n   CONTENTS EXPECTED IN RESPONSE TO THE REQUIREMENT (GUIDELINES)\n\n\n\n\n                                                                        Page 10 sur 35<\/div>", "text": "2  Security & privacy by design\n\n     -  GDPR/ Personal Data encryption (inside Database) / DCP encryption (inside Database)\n     -   identity federation\n     -   https\n     -  Web App Firewall\n     -  No unsecure software (e.g. WordPress)\n     -   Interfaces security type patterns of the stat of art will be implemented.\n   CONTENTS EXPECTED IN RESPONSE TO THE REQUIREMENT (GUIDELINES)\n\n\n\n\n                                                                        Page 10 sur 35"}, {"id": "d8-s11", "doc": 8, "title": "Page 11 · ID                         Privacy Requirements (“Data” means the personal data)", "html": "<div class=\"pdftext\"> ID                         Privacy Requirements (“Data” means the personal data)\n\nDP01  Customer will always be the only Data owner.\n\nDP02  Provider will be liable for any penalties due to noncompliance to laws related to the provided services.\n\n       Customer is immediately informed of the incident and all the remedies implemented if a data breach or aDP03        security vulnerability is identified in the Data processing or in any system used for providing the services.\n\nDP04  Data used for authentication shall be protected with effective cryptographic security measures.\n\nDP05   All Data communication in transit shall be encrypted using the latest encryption procedures.\n\n         In case of Data processing with a high or very high level of confidentiality, such as localization data, identity\nDP06  documents, bank data, special categories of personal data, they shall be encrypted at rest using the latest\n        encryption procedures.\n\n       Customer must assure Data destruction (using multipass secure erase) in case of storage media dismission,DP07       hardware replacement or hardware re-use.\n\n        Provider must provide Data deletion and retention timescales, including end-of-life destruction. This must applyDP08        also in case of contract termination.\n\n        Provider must securely delete all copies of Data within a timescale when requested (e.g. on demand, orDP09\n       Customer decides to withdraw from the service).\n\n        Provider must not share Customer Data with third parties or share across other services the Provider may offer.\nDP10  Provider is only authorized to process Data for the specific purposes for providing the service.\n      The Data collected for different purposes are processed separately.\n\n             If the service provided will collect Data Privacy authorizations, the logs concerning these authorizations must be\nDP11  maintained for the entire contract duration and must be provided to Customer on request and at the end of the\n        contract.\n\n        Provider must specify in what conditions third parties could have access to Customer data, includingDP12       government agencies.\n\nDP13  Provider excludes or limits copies of the Data (including printouts) and ensures proper destruction after the use.\n\n        Provider must keep in place audit trails (audit trail must be tamper-proof) and Customer must be enabled to\n        monitor establish whether and by whom Data have been read/input into data processing systems, modified or\nDP14       removed. Logs must include source IP address.\n       Logs must be available for at least one year.\n\n        Provider must allow Customer to get a copy of all data, at Customer request, in a usable and agreed format, inDP15       any case in a non-proprietary format.\n\n      Backup of Data shall be performed at least on a daily basis, and it shall be maintained an up-to-date backupDP16       copy of software used by Provider for the Data processing.\n\n        Suitable measures shall be adopted to ensure that Data access is restored within a specific deadline (no moreDP17       than seven days).\n\n      The Data will be stored applying measures securing it from unauthorized accesses, alterations, damages andDP18        destructions (e.g. protected from accidental destruction or loss).\n\n       Compliance to personal data laws and regulations must be assured. If for providing the service Data will be\nDP19  processed (even if only accessed) outside EU, Customer must be advised and privacy roles and authorization\n        eventually requested by laws must be in place.\n\nDP20  Provider must support Customer for any forensic investigation that could be necessary.\n\n        Provider must specify which companies (including subprocessors) and where they will process (even if only\n       accessed) Customer Data in, as well as when and why Data will be transferred to these locations.DP21        Provider must provide about the circumstances in which Customer Data may be transferred, also temporarily, to\n        other countries. Provider must limit the transfer of Data to countries that Customer declared as appropriate.\n\n\n\n\n\n                                                                      Page 11 sur 35<\/div>", "text": " ID                         Privacy Requirements (“Data” means the personal data)\n\nDP01  Customer will always be the only Data owner.\n\nDP02  Provider will be liable for any penalties due to noncompliance to laws related to the provided services.\n\n       Customer is immediately informed of the incident and all the remedies implemented if a data breach or aDP03        security vulnerability is identified in the Data processing or in any system used for providing the services.\n\nDP04  Data used for authentication shall be protected with effective cryptographic security measures.\n\nDP05   All Data communication in transit shall be encrypted using the latest encryption procedures.\n\n         In case of Data processing with a high or very high level of confidentiality, such as localization data, identity\nDP06  documents, bank data, special categories of personal data, they shall be encrypted at rest using the latest\n        encryption procedures.\n\n       Customer must assure Data destruction (using multipass secure erase) in case of storage media dismission,DP07       hardware replacement or hardware re-use.\n\n        Provider must provide Data deletion and retention timescales, including end-of-life destruction. "d8-s12", "doc": 8, "title": "Page 12 · Provider will guarantee the following:", "html": "<div class=\"pdftext\">        Provider will guarantee the following:\n     A system controlling access to the Data.\n         Built-in mechanism requesting each person having access to the Data to renew the password.\n     A unique login (the “User ID”) and password (the “credentials”) for each person (also for Provider’s users)\n        involved in the Data processing.\n      The password, known only to the person it is assigned to (the “User”), has the following minimum\n         characteristics:\n         1. it shall have at least 8 characters;\n         2. it shall contain lowercase and uppercase letters combined with digits or special characters;\n         3. it does not contain the User ID;\nDP22   4. it shall be modified autonomously and mandatorily by the User upon first connection and after the password\n         reset;\n         5. it shall be modified at least every 60 days.\n      The User ID assigned to a User must not be reassigned to another person in charge of the processing even at\n      a different time.\n      The credentials shall be deactivated if they have not been used for at least 6 months (except for those that have\n      been authorized for technical management purpose).\n      The credentials shall also be promptly deactivated if the person in charge of the processing is disqualified from\n       accessing the Data.\n      The persons in charge of the processing shall be instructed not to leave unattended and make accessible\n        electronic equipment during processing sessions.\n\n\n\n        Authorization system:\n         1. where authorization profiles with different scope have been set out for the persons in charge of the\n        processing, an authorization system shall be used;\n         2. authorization profiles for each person or homogeneous set of persons in charge of the processing shall beDP23        set out and configured prior to start of the processing in such a way as to only enable access to the Data that\n       are necessary to perform processing operations;\n         3. it shall be regularly verified, at least at yearly intervals, that the prerequisites for retaining the relevant\n        authorization profiles still apply.\n\n\n        Organizational Measures - Provider guarantees that:\n         1. Data access will be assigned on the basis of the “need to know” principle;\n         2. it will limit the number of persons authorized to perform activities connected with the Data processing;\n         3. it will train the authorized persons on data protection regulations, security measures taken by Provider and\n        security policies implemented in case of security emergencies;DP24         4. the persons authorized to use a data processing system have access only to the Data they have right of\n       access and the Data cannot be read, copied, modified, removed or used without authorization during the\n       processing and afterwards during the storage;\n         5. it will keep an up-to-date list of persons authorized to have access to the Data, and make such list available\n         to Customer upon Customer motivated request.\n\n\n                                  System Administrators\n\nDP25  Unable Data access to the System Administrator. If it’s not feasible, Customer must be aware of it.\n\nDP26  Make a careful assessment on the qualifications of the person/s the role of System Administrator is assigned to.\n\n       Appoint individually the System Administrator and analytically list the activities the System Administrator willDP27        carry out giving the relevant authorization profile.\n\nDP28  Have an internal document, to be kept updated with the personal details of the System Administrator.\n\n      Make available to Customer the above mentioned document in DP28 in case of an audit of the Data ProtectionDP29        Authority and/or upon request of Customer.\n\n       Check, at least annually, System Administrator&#x27;s activities to verify that they are compliant with theDP30        organizational, technical and security measures provided by the Privacy Law.\n\n        Register System Administrator’s logical access controls to processing systems and electronic databases. The\nDP31   registrations (access logs) have to be complete and unalterable. It has to be possible to verify their integrity in\n       accordance with the verification purposes they are intended to achieve.\n\n\n\n\n If it’s not feasible, Customer must be aware of it.\n\nDP26  Make a careful assessment on the qualifications of the person/s the role of System Administrator is assigned to.\n\n       Appoint individually the System Administrator and analytically list the activities the System Administrator willDP27        carry out giving the relevant authorization profile.\n\nDP28  Have an internal document, to be kept updated with the personal details of the System Administrator.\n\n      Make available to Customer the above mentioned document in DP28 in case of an audit of the Data ProtectionDP29        Authority and/or upon request of Customer.\n\n       Check, at least annually, System Administrator's activities to verify that they are compliant with theDP30        organizational, technical and security measures provided by the Privacy Law.\n\n        Register System Administrator’s logical access controls to processing systems and electronic databases. The\nDP31   registrations (access logs) have to be complete and unalterable. It has to be possible to verify their integrity in\n       accordance with the verification purposes they are intended to achieve.\n\n\n\n\n                                                                      Page 12 sur 35"}, {"id": "d8-s13", "doc": 8, "title": "Page 13 · Retain the access logs set forth in DP31 for a suitable period of time no less than one year. The ac", "html": "<div class=\"pdftext\">         Retain the access logs set forth in DP31 for a suitable period of time no less than one year. The access logs\n DP32  must include timestamps and event descriptions.\n        The logs must be provided to Customer in case of request.\n\n\n2.2 User Management/Identity federation\n   EXECUTIVE LEVEL DESCRIPTION\n    This requirement covers the Identity and Access Management and the system of trust between\n    the parties.\n    Where are the end users (application administrators and application users) lists stored?\n      Is it in a database inside the application? In this case, where is the database? Or is there\n    any identity federation with an external identity provider? What are the protocols used\n    (SAML, OpenID connect…)? Is the user list known by the project manager? His he aware\n     of any user creation/deletion?\n\n   REQUIREMENT\n       •   Provider users that need to access to any STELLANTIS tool (JIRA, Service Now, etc.) need a\n          STELLANTIS identity management solution (LDAP, SAML, IDP...)\n       •   Provider users, Central, NSC, importers and dealer users with a need to access to the\n          STELLANTIS instance on data of the platform, need a STELLANTIS identity management\n            solution (LDAP, SAML, IDP...)\n    Similarly, users profiling must comply with current regulations and policies provided by STELLANTIS\n    in the study of the solution by the supplier.\n   By default, authentication process is centralized in the STELLANTIS tool.\n   STELLANTIS can ask provider to develop a profiling or to accept a profiling made by STELLANTIS or\n   both depending on the users class.\n   The personal data will be encrypted by the application before insertion in the database with an\n   AES 256 algorithm. The encryption key must be managed securely.\n    Personal data will be encrypted by the application for interfaces with an AES 256 algorithm. The\n    encryption key must be managed securely.\n   The supplier undertakes to implement all necessary solutions in accordance with the state of the\n    art in order to secure the application.\n   CONTENTS EXPECTED IN RESPONSE TO THE REQUIREMENT (GUIDELINES)\nThe provider has to describe the user management features.\n\n\n\n   ID             Area             Supplier’s requirements\n\n\n                                      Supplier shall adopt STELLANTIS’s Identity and Access Management (“IAM”)\n  SP20       Access Control         for any Service Provider’s service used by STELLANTIS’s User IDs (e.g.,\n                                  employees, contractors…)\n                                      Supplier shall design application specific user roles and profiles on a need to\n                              know basis (e.g., admin, read only…) that will be implemented in the  SP23       Access Control                                        Supplier’s solution and mapped in STELLANTIS Identity Access\n                              Management accordingly.\n\n\n\n\n                                                                        Page 13 sur 35<\/div>", "text": "         Retain the access logs set forth in DP31 for a suitable period of time no less than one year. Is it the only way to access\n    the app? Is there any redirection from http to https? Which certificate authority is used?\n   What is the level of the certificate? Is there a known and working process to update the\n     certificate?\n\n   REQUIREMENT\n           -   Publicly exposed flows must be in https.\n           -   The internal private flows must be in https except exemption validated by STELLANTIS.\n           -   Public feeds must use a publicly recognized CA.\n           -   External  private  flows must use a dedicated  certification  authority  validated by\n           STELLANTIS.\n           -   Public HTTPS certificates can be generated by the provider.\n           -     If STELLANTIS is responsible for the platform domain name, the supplier must use the\n          STELLANTIS certificate creation process\n   CONTENTS EXPECTED IN RESPONSE TO THE REQUIREMENT (GUIDELINES)\n   The provider needs to specify these aspects.\n   Example of Mutual TLS (or 2waySSL or flow using certificates):\n\n\n                                       Supplier shall configure all network connections to be based on Transport\n                                   Layer Security protocol if needed. The minimum version of TLS protocol\n                                           shall be the last version and it will be configured to avoid any fallback to  SP40       Network Security                                     lower versions.\n                                Backend servers shall reject any TLS negotiation request with anonymous\n                                  key exchange algorithms.\n                                       Supplier shall configure all connections (i.e. Server to Server, Client to\n  SP43        Access Control      Server) to be authenticated using strong authentication methods (e.g.,\n                                      mutually authenticated TLS)\n\n\n2.4 Web application firewall\n   EXECUTIVE LEVEL DESCRIPTION\n    This requirement covers the network security control.\n      Is there a software WAF inside the app, and / or outside the APP? Is it managed by the\n     provider or by the team? How often the rules are updated? Is there a dashboard and\n     alerting in case of WAF warning? Is there any IP-rate limitation rules? Is the WAF\n     available in all environments? How rules are propagated from an environment to\n    another? Are OWASP rules implemented?\n\n\n   REQUIREMENT\n    For web applications, the supplier must have a WAF (Web Application Firewall) capabilities with\n    state of the art features activated.\n   The application must not be publicly directly available without the WAF.\n\n\n\n                                                                        Page 14 sur 35<\/div>", "text": "2.3  Https\n   EXECUTIVE LEVEL DESCRIPTION\n    This requirement covers the security of the flows.\n    Are all exposed websites of the application available to https? How the dev team is\n    informed, maintain, and patch such a software?\n\n   REQUIREMENT\n   The supplier must only use software whose versions are maintained and up to date, and which do\n    not have security vulnerabilities. The supplier agrees to update the software throughout the life of\n    the project.\n   CONTENTS EXPECTED IN RESPONSE TO THE REQUIREMENT (GUIDELINES)\n   The supplier must have a security alert receipt process and must be able to apply the necessary\n    patches without damaging the application. A description of this process is requested.\n\n\n           System Acquisition,     Supplier shall develop FCA solutions following the Security and Industry-\n SP35      Development and      standard best practices for software development (e.g., OWASP MSP,\n               Maintenance     OWASP ASVS, etc.).\n\n\n2.6 Cloud security\n   EXECUTIVE LEVEL DESCRIPTION\n    This requirement covers the security in place for the application in the Cloud (as part of a Cloud\n    application).\n    Are there one or several accounts/subscriptions for the application in the cloud provider?\n   How is the production environment isolated from the non-production environments?\n   How is the Cloud network security (VPC, private subnets, security groups…)?  Is there a\n    VPN? Is there IP whitelisting? CC must be\n CP03        aware of these practices\n\n CP04  CP take in charge the responsibility for assuring the confidentiality, availability and integrity of CC data.\n\n CP05  CPs must provide SLAs for creating, suspending and deleting accounts.\n\n       CPs must ensure adequate quality of service, also on the basis of the actions of other CCs or their\n CP06        CUs.\n\n CP07  CPs must explain the impacts on the business in case of a major outage at the CP.\n\n      CP will not be able to change the terms of data processing operations during the lifetime of the contract\n CP09  without the CC’s knowledge and agreement. If the changes are not accepted, CC can terminate the\n          contract without additional charges.\n\n CP10  CC’s systems must be segregated from other systems of different CP’s customers.\n\n CP11  A detailed description of the architecture used for providing the service must be provided and agreed.\n\n CP12  CC could perform vulnerability assessment and penetration tests.\n\n\n2.7  Traceability\n   EXECUTIVE LEVEL DESCRIPTION\n    This requirement covers the functionalities put in place concerning traceability and how the traces\n    of the status and movements of information are kept.\n      Is the user action on the back-office tracked (who, when, what)? Are the users informed\n    they are tracked? How long the traceability logs are kept? SP56      Operations Security                                      Security log set (e.g., login/logout activity ...) shall be agreed during security\n                                   design activities.\n\n\n\n\n\n                                                                        Page 16 sur 35"}, {"id": "d8-s17", "doc": 8, "title": "Page 17 · 2.8  Security audits realized", "html": "<div class=\"pdftext\">2.8  Security audits realized\n   EXECUTIVE LEVEL DESCRIPTION\n    This requirement covers the different assessment concerning security\n      Is there any security audits and penetration test realized? Are the reports known by the\n    dev team? Is there a plan to fix failures detected by the audit? Are they realized on a\n     regular basis? At each minor/major release? Are they realized by an internal or external\n    team?\n\n   REQUIREMENT\n    According to STELLANTIS guideline:\n       •   security assessment has to be performed before the Solution’s go live (on-line)\n       •    if security assessment raises security issues,\n                -   issues must be communicated to the project team\n                -   Project team to assess issues criticality and to correct them before the Solution’s go\n                   live (on-line)\n       •  Code audit and Pentest\n            Preparation:\n                -   STELLANTIS Security audit team can do a test campaign with the source code (white\n                box), or without the source code of the application (black box).\n                -   In both cases, the test is made on the production version of the source code of the\n                application.\n                -   Security team will keep the Supplier informed of Pentest’s schedule on pre-production\n              environment\n                -   The Supplier must inform any third party that a test will begin. The supplier must\n              complete forms if some hosting providers require this before starting the test (AWS,\n             Akamai for ex.)\n           Processing\n                -  No brute force for password\n                -   Audit on pre-production environment\n                -   Report on any issue to STELLANTIS project team\n           Detailed report and audio presentation for detailed explanations\n                -   Security audit team to provide a detailed report of the preformed security assessment\n                explaining the followed process, the conducted actions, the obtained results, specialist\n                interpretations and advice\n                -   Organize and schedule a complete and full presentation of its detailed report and how\n               to secure the found issue.\n                -   Before go live (on-line), Supplier to perform issues correction for those which where\n                 qualified as mandatory\n\n   CONTENTS EXPECTED IN RESPONSE TO THE REQUIREMENT (GUIDELINES)\n\n\n                                      Supplier shall execute an end-to-end VA/PT of the services/solutions\n                                    provided to STELLANTIS at least 2 times every contractual year.\n  SP58          Security Test                                               All outcomes shall be shared with FCA along with remediation plans (if\n                                       applicable) without additional costs.\n\n\n\n\n                                                                        Page 17 sur 35<\/div>", "text": "2.8  Security audits realized\n   EXECUTIVE LEVEL DESCRIPTION\n    This requirement covers the different assessment concerning security\n      Is there any security audits and penetration test realized? LEVEL DESCRIPTION\n    This requirement covers the General Security Requirements identified by the functionalities like\n    Operations Security, Network Security, Asset Management and Cryptography.\n   REQUIREMENT\n    Provider needs to cover the state of art in term of General Security Requirements and need to be\n    compliant.\n   CONTENTS EXPECTED IN RESPONSE TO THE REQUIREMENT (GUIDELINES)\n   The supplier must ensure that the solution made is compliant with STELLANTIS requirements and\n   must clarify if any of these aspects is not possible, not feasible:\n\n\n                                 feasible.\n\n                                      Supplier must ensure that all security patches shall be applied as soon as\n SP10      Operations Security                                      possible and without undue delay.\n\n                                      Supplier must ensure:\n                                  -Any high priority/critical security vulnerability identified by STELLANTIS is\n SP11      Operations Security                                   remediated within 1 day of remediation availability\n                                                -All other vulnerabilities are remediated within 10 days\n\n                                      Supplier Define segregate Security Zone for homogenous Security and\n SP12       Network Security                                  Business Services\n\n                                      Supplier shall ensure segregation (e.g. FW, Subnet ACL) to allow access only\n SP13       Network Security                                         to authorized Users or Connections\n\n                                      Supplier shall define FW rules subject to a defined and auditable Supplier’s\n SP14       Network Security       authorization process. Such FW rules shall be jointly reviewed with\n                             STELLANTIS during Service Review Meetings.\n\n SP15       Network Security      Supplier shall revalidate all FW Rules at least annually.\n\n                                      Supplier shall monitor not used FW rules. Rules not triggered at least once\n SP16       Network Security                                   every 6 months shall be reviewed and ultimately removed.\n\n                                      Supplier shall implement all applicable (Industry-Standard) security features\n SP17       Network Security        in order to guarantee real-time Security Control (e.g. IDS/IPS, WAF, anti\n Is the application\n     applicate the microservices, loose coupling principles? Is it a ported app from On-Prem\n     to Cloud or is it a Cloud native app?\n\n   REQUIREMENT\n   The software must be adapted to the technologies of the moment.\n   CONTENTS EXPECTED IN RESPONSE TO THE REQUIREMENT (GUIDELINES)\n   As far as possible, it uses headless CMS (BO which generates static JAMSTACK content, deployed\n    directly on Cloud servers, Single Page Application (applications entirely in JavaScript) supported by\n   frameworks.\n\n\n3.2 Auto scaling - Scalable platform strategy\n   EXECUTIVE LEVEL DESCRIPTION\n    This requirement covers the scalability.\n   How charge peak is absorbed by the app? Is there a capacity planning? Is it scale\n    up/down or in/out? Is auto scaling managed by a dedicated service, or is it coded from\n     scratch by the app?\n\n   REQUIREMENT\n   The platform must be designed in order to be able to easily integrate new functions/modules in\n    the future, including the induced traffic increases.\n   The platform must be able to handle unexpected traffic spikes.\n   CONTENTS EXPECTED IN RESPONSE TO THE REQUIREMENT (GUIDELINES)\n    •  Enhance customer journey and business capabilities of the solution\n    •   Allow reuse of the platform for other markets (other countries and/or brands)\n    •   Customer-side applications need to have the ability to automatically expand/retract capacity\n        to cope with large concurrency requirements;\n\n\n\n\n\n                                                                        Page 20 sur 35<\/div>", "text": "3  Software Architecture\n\n     -  New Software design (Cloud friendly, SPA, framework JS, microservices)\n     -   Auto scaling\n     -   Design for failure\n     -   Open-source\n     -   Docker\n     -   API integration with other systems (or web services)\n     -   Batch processing\n     -   Develop with any device / anywhere / for every user’s device\n     -   Deployment or ramp up for new brand/country (multi-tenant)\n     -   Programming language\n\n3.1  Software design (Cloud friendly, SPA, framework JS, microservices)\n   EXECUTIVE LEVEL DESCRIPTION\n    This requirement covers the software design part.\n   What is the kind of application (static website, Single Page App, API)? Is the application\n     applicate the microservices, loose coupling principles? Is it a ported app from On-Prem\n     to Cloud or is it a Cloud native app?\n\n   REQUIREMENT\n   The software must be adapted to the technologies of the moment.\n   CONTENTS EXPECTED IN RESPONSE TO THE REQUIREMENT (GUIDELINES)\n   As far as possible, it uses headless CMS (BO which generates static JAMSTACK content, deployed\n    directly on Cloud servers, Single Page Application (applications entirely in JavaScript) supported by\n   frameworks.\n\n\n3.2 Auto scaling - Scalable platform strategy\n   EXECUTIVE LEVEL DESCRIPTION\n    This requirement covers the scalability.\n   How charge peak is absorbed by the app? Is there a capacity planning? Is it scale\n    up/down or in/out? Is auto scaling managed by a dedicated service, or is it coded from\n     scratch by the app?\n\n   REQUIREMENT\n   The platform must be designed in order to be able to easily integrate new functions/modules in\n    the future, including the induced traffic increases.\n   The platform must be able to handle unexpected traffic spikes.\n   CONTENTS EXPECTED IN RESPONSE TO THE REQUIREMENT (GUIDELINES)\n    •  Enhance customer journey and business capabilities of the solution\n    •   Allow reuse of the platform for other markets (other countries and/or brands)\n    •   Customer-side applications need to have the ability to automatically expand/retract capacity\n        to cope with large concurrency requirements;\n\n\n\n\n\n                                                                        Page 20 sur 35"}, {"id": "d8-s21", "doc": 8, "title": "Page 21 · 3.3  Design for failure", "html": "<div class=\"pdftext\">3.3  Design for failure\n   EXECUTIVE LEVEL DESCRIPTION\n    This requirement covers the ability of the system to withstand failures of other components, in\n    other words the resiliency of the application.\n   What is the app behavior when an external system is down? Is there a general strategy\n     to handle error? What are the user impacts? Is there a mapping of all app dependencies?\n\n   REQUIREMENT\n   Have the ability to avoid user impacts in case of issues on single parts of the global solution, and/or\n    covering the issue with dedicated messages to the customer.\n   CONTENTS EXPECTED IN RESPONSE TO THE REQUIREMENT (GUIDELINES)\n    Description of the mechanisms implemented.\n   From the application point of view:\n       •   behavior of the application  if an API does not respond,  if the application  is under\n          maintenance\n   From the infrastructure point of view:\n       •   Physical redundancy (network, disk, data center). Here ends the traditional model\n       •   Virtual redundancy: an application is distributed over several identical virtual machines\n            within a cluster of VMs\n       •  Redundancy of VMs clusters (or Availability Zone). These clusters are divided into clusters\n            of clusters\n       •  Redundancy of clusters of clusters (or Region). A single supplier manages these regions\n       •  Redundancy of access providers (e.g., Rackspace) in the unlikely event that AWS  is\n           completely shut down\n\n\n3.4 Open-source &amp; licensed system\n   EXECUTIVE LEVEL DESCRIPTION\n    This requirement covers the Open-source &amp; licensed system aspect.\n    Does the app use a licensed system or open-source? Does the license limitation are\n    known by all app actors? Is there a review of external code used by the project to be sure\n     there is no licensing problem? Does the team have ability to contribute to an open-source\n     project? Is there any public communication about app using or contributing to free or\n    open-source projects?\n\n   REQUIREMENT\n    In case of specific development, the provider should privilege usage of FOSS (Free and Open-\n   Source Software) solutions and in particular components of STELLANTIS Group technical platform:\n   (Example of products, non-exhaustive list: Linux, Open JDK, Spring-boot, Spring, Nacos, JWT,\n    MyBatis, Quartz, Apache, Kafka, RabbitMQ, REDIS, MySQL, MongoDB, Junit, Jenkins, Maven,\n    behat, selenium, Drupal, Php / Symfony, JavaScript frameworks, Vue.js, Element-ui, Echarts,\n    nodejs, ElasticSearch, …)\n   CONTENTS EXPECTED IN RESPONSE TO THE REQUIREMENT (GUIDELINES)\n    Description of the situation.\n\n\n\n                                                                        Page 21 sur 35<\/div>", "text": "3.3  Design for failure\n   EXECUTIVE LEVEL DESCRIPTION\n    This requirement covers the ability of the system to withstand failures of other components, in\n    other words the resiliency of the application.\n   What is the app behavior when an external system is down? Is there a general strategy\n     to handle error? What are the user impacts? Is there a mapping of all app dependencies?\n\n   REQUIREMENT\n   Have the ability to avoid user impacts in case of issues on single parts of the global solution, and/or\n    covering the issue with dedicated messages to the customer.\n   CONTENTS EXPECTED IN RESPONSE TO THE REQUIREMENT (GUIDELINES)\n    Description of the mechanisms implemented.\n   From the application point of view:\n       •   behavior of the application  if an API does not respond,  if the application  is under\n          maintenance\n   From the infrastructure point of view:\n       •   Physical redundancy (network, disk, data center). Here ends the traditional model\n       •   Virtual redundancy: an application is distributed over several identical virtual machines\n            within a cluster of VMs\n       •  Redundancy of VMs clusters (or Availability Zone). These clusters are divided into clusters\n            of clusters\n       •  Redundancy of clusters of clusters (or Region). A single supplier manages these regions\n       •  Redundancy of access providers (e.g., Rackspace) in the unlikely event that AWS  is\n           completely shut down\n\n\n3.4 Open-source & licensed system\n   EXECUTIVE LEVEL DESCRIPTION\n    This requirement covers the Open-source & licensed system aspect.\n    Does the app use a licensed system or open-source? Does the license limitation are\n    known by all app actors? Is there a review of external code used by the project to be sure\n     there is no licensing problem? Does the team have ability to contribute to an open-source\n     project? Is there any public communication about app using or contributing to free or\n    open-source projects?\n\n   REQUIREMENT\n    In case of specific development, the provider should privilege usage of FOSS (Free and Open-\n   Source Software) solutions and in particular components of STELLANTIS Group technical platform:\n   (Example of products, non-exhaustive list: Linux, Open JDK, Spring-boot, Spring, Nacos, JWT,\n    MyBatis, Quartz, Apache, Kafka, RabbitMQ, REDIS, MySQL, MongoDB, Junit, Jenkins, Maven,\n    behat, selenium, Drupal, Php / Symfony, JavaScript frameworks, Vue.js, Element-ui, Echarts,\n    nodejs, ElasticSearch, …)\n   CONTENTS EXPECTED IN RESPONSE TO THE REQUIREMENT (GUIDELINES)\n    Description of the situation.\n\n\n\n                                                                        Page 21 sur 35"}, {"id": "d8-s22", "doc": 8, "title": "Page 22 · 3.5 Docker & Virtualization", "html": "<div class=\"pdftext\">3.5 Docker &amp; Virtualization\n   EXECUTIVE LEVEL DESCRIPTION\n    This requirement covers the Virtualization.\n   What kind of virtualization is used? On which environment?\n\n   REQUIREMENT\n   The provided solution will be available as a Docker image (and the Docker files configuration will\n   be managed in the SCM) - except for components of the solution based on software managed\n    services provided by a PaaS public Cloud or a SaaS Solution.\n   CONTENTS EXPECTED IN RESPONSE TO THE REQUIREMENT (GUIDELINES)\n    Description of the situation.\n\n\n3.6 API integration with other systems (or web services)\n   EXECUTIVE LEVEL DESCRIPTION\n    This requirement covers the API management.\n\n   How consumed API are secured (oAuth2, basic auth, 2waySSL …)?\n\n\n   REQUIREMENT\n   The provider should have the technology allowing to call APIs to recover the information needed\n   from STELLANTIS for the needs to be defined\n   CONTENTS EXPECTED IN RESPONSE TO THE REQUIREMENT (GUIDELINES)\n    Description of the situation.\n\n\n3.7  Batch processing\n   EXECUTIVE LEVEL DESCRIPTION\n    This requirement covers the Batch processing of the platform.\n   How is the batch processing managed? Does it impact the end-user experience?\n\n   REQUIREMENT\n   Batch processing: alert and precise execution report should be possible.\n   The performance of the solution must not generate user impacts during batch processing\n   CONTENTS EXPECTED IN RESPONSE TO THE REQUIREMENT (GUIDELINES)\n   Batch processing and new release delivery should not affect availability and response times\n\n\n3.8 Deployment or ramp up for new brand/country (multi-tenant)\n   EXECUTIVE LEVEL DESCRIPTION\n\n\n                                                                        Page 22 sur 35<\/div>", "text": "3.5 Docker & Virtualization\n   EXECUTIVE LEVEL DESCRIPTION\n    This requirement covers the Virtualization.\n   What kind of virtualization is used? On which environment?\n\n   REQUIREMENT\n   The provided solution will be available as a Docker image (and the Docker files configuration will\n   be managed in the SCM) - except for components of the solution based on software managed\n    services provided by a PaaS public Cloud or a SaaS Solution.\n   CONTENTS EXPECTED IN RESPONSE TO THE REQUIREMENT (GUIDELINES)\n    Description of the situation.\n\n\n3.6 API integration with other systems (or web services)\n   EXECUTIVE LEVEL DESCRIPTION\n    This requirement covers the API management.\n\n   How consumed API are secured (oAuth2, basic auth, 2waySSL …)?\n\n\n   REQUIREMENT\n   The provider should have the technology allowing to call APIs to recover the information needed\n   from STELLANTIS for the needs to be defined\n   CONTENTS EXPECTED IN RESPONSE TO THE REQUIREMENT (GUIDELINES)\n    Description of the situation.\n\n\n3.7  Batch processing\n   EXECUTIVE LEVEL DESCRIPTION\n    This requirement covers the Batch processing of the platform.\n   How is the batch processing managed? Does it impact the end-user experience?\n\n   REQUIREMENT\n   Batch processing: alert and precise execution report should be possible.\n   The performance of the solution must not generate user impacts during batch processing\n   CONTENTS EXPECTED IN RESPONSE TO THE REQUIREMENT (GUIDELINES)\n   Batch processing and new release delivery should not affect availability and response times\n\n\n3.8 Deployment or ramp up for new brand/country (multi-tenant)\n   EXECUTIVE LEVEL DESCRIPTION\n\n\n                                                                        Page 22 sur 35"}, {"id": "d8-s23", "doc": 8, "title": "Page 23 · This requirement covers deployment or ramp up for new brand/country (multi-tenant).", "html": "<div class=\"pdftext\">    This requirement covers deployment or ramp up for new brand/country (multi-tenant).\n   How easy is it to deploy a new brand or country? Do we need to duplicate infrastructure\n     for each new deployment? Is the solution multi or single tenant?\n\n   REQUIREMENT\n   Management of countries/languages\n   By default, the solution must be multi-brand, multi-country and multilingual. The management of\n    multilingualism (translations) and regionalization (date and time formats, user interface) must use\n   runtime setup, and not a technical delivery.\n   CONTENTS EXPECTED IN RESPONSE TO THE REQUIREMENT (GUIDELINES)\n       •  The CMS/solution code (code base) is the same for each brand instance and it is using a\n             multi-site deployment approach (SaaS model)\n       •  Each instantiated site (i.e., each brand) could have his dedicated database containing\n            settings and contents if necessary.\n\n\n3.9 Programming language\n   EXECUTIVE LEVEL DESCRIPTION\n    This requirement aims to give visibility on the languages that make up the solution.\n   What is the main programing language used? Is there any other language used for other\n    minor tasks (like ops)? What are the frameworks? Is the roadmap of the language and\n    frameworks known? What versions are used?\n\n   REQUIREMENT\n   The language(s) must be among those most used in order to avoid management constraints as\n   much as possible.\n   CONTENTS EXPECTED IN RESPONSE TO THE REQUIREMENT (GUIDELINES)\n    Information on the programming languages, frameworks and versions used.\n    Thus, they should not be too low in the TIOBE ranking.\n    https://www.tiobe.com/tiobe-index/\n\n\n\n\n\n                                                                        Page 23 sur 35<\/div>", "text": "    This requirement covers deployment or ramp up for new brand/country (multi-tenant).\n   How easy is it to deploy a new brand or country? What versions are used?\n\n   REQUIREMENT\n   The language(s) must be among those most used in order to avoid management constraints as\n   much as possible.\n   CONTENTS EXPECTED IN RESPONSE TO THE REQUIREMENT (GUIDELINES)\n    Information on the programming languages, frameworks and versions used.\n    Thus, they should not be too low in the TIOBE ranking.\n    https://www.tiobe.com/tiobe-index/\n\n\n\n\n\n                                                                        Page 23 sur 35"}, {"id": "d8-s24", "doc": 8, "title": "Page 24 · -   Environment", "html": "<div class=\"pdftext\">4  Build\n\n     -   Environment\n     -   Continuous Integration\n     -   Continuous Delivery\n     -   Automated tests and datasets\n     -   Blue / Green deployment\n     -    Full automation (&gt; 80%)\n     -    Infra as code\n\n4.1 Environments\n   EXECUTIVE LEVEL DESCRIPTION\n    This requirement covers specificities related to environments.\n   Name all environments needed for the project, and their characteristics (DEV, INT, REC,\n    UAT, QUALIF, PREPROD, PROD…)\n    Can you describe your environment alignment strategies on data between themselves?\n      Is there any cost associated to the new environment?\n\n   REQUIREMENT\n   The solution, whether used in SaaS, PaaS, CaaS, must use several environments.\n   The supplier must provide STELLANTIS:\n       •   At least 3 environments: development, staging and live\n       •  An environment allowing to do UAT test with access for STELLANTIS users\n       •  The differences between the environments, if they are not identical, specify it (sizing,\n             costs, etc.)\n       •    If bricks are shared between environments (e.g., databases shared between production\n          and preproduction).\n       •   Technical characteristics\n   CONTENTS EXPECTED IN RESPONSE TO THE REQUIREMENT (GUIDELINES)\n    Description of the situation.\n\n4.2  Continuous Integration (SCM, Dependencies ...)\n   EXECUTIVE LEVEL DESCRIPTION\n    This requirement covers the Source Code Management (ex: Github …).\n      Is it possible to build the application with an automated process? What are the triggers\n     of a build (code commit, merge, user action)? How the dev team is informed of a failed\n     build? What are the conditions for a build to fails? What tools is used to build the app?\n    Where is the CICD tool chain hosted? How reliable and resilient is the tool chain?\n   What are the continuous integration process in place? What is the frequency of the\n     deliveries?\n\n   REQUIREMENT\n   The provider is asked to use some tool allowing continuous integration.\n   SCM Tools\n   The supplier will use the SCM tools provided by STELLANTIS to manage the source code:\n\n\n\n                                                                        Page 24 sur 35<\/div>", "text": "4  Build\n\n     -   Environment\n     -   Continuous Integration\n     -   Continuous Delivery\n     -   Automated tests and datasets\n     -   Blue / Green deployment\n     -    Full automation (> 80%)\n     -    Infra as code\n\n4.1 Environments\n   EXECUTIVE LEVEL DESCRIPTION\n    This requirement covers specificities related to environments.\n   Name all environments needed for the project, and their characteristics (DEV, INT, REC,\n    UAT, QUALIF, PREPROD, PROD…)\n    Can you describe your environment alignment strategies on data between themselves?\n      Is there any cost associated to the new environment?\n\n   REQUIREMENT\n   The solution, whether used in SaaS, PaaS, CaaS, must use several environments.\n   The supplier must provide STELLANTIS:\n       •   At least 3 environments: development, staging and live\n       •  An environment allowing to do UAT test with access for STELLANTIS users\n       •  The differences between the environments, if they are not identical, specify it (sizing,\n             costs, etc.)\n       •    If bricks are shared between environments (e.g., databases shared between production\n          and preproduction).\n       •   Technical characteristics\n   CONTENTS EXPECTED IN RESPONSE TO THE REQUIREMENT (GUIDELINES)\n    Description of the situation.\n\n4.2  Continuous Integration (SCM, Dependencies ...)\n   EXECUTIVE LEVEL DESCRIPTION\n    This requirement covers the Source Code Management (ex: Github …).\n      Is it possible to build the application with an automated process? What are the triggers\n     of a build (code commit, merge, user action)? How the dev team is informed of a failed\n     build? What are the conditions for a build to fails? What tools is used to build the app?\n    Where is the CICD tool chain hosted? How reliable and resilient is the tool chain?\n   What are the continuous integration process in place? What is the frequency of the\n     deliveries?\n\n   REQUIREMENT\n   The provider is asked to use some tool allowing continuous integration.\n   SCM Tools\n   The supplier will use the SCM tools provided by STELLANTIS to manage the source code:\n\n\n\n                                                                        Page 24 sur 35"}, {"id": "d8-s25", "doc": 8, "title": "Page 25 · •  STELLANTIS provides private GitHub Repository", "html": "<div class=\"pdftext\">       •  STELLANTIS provides private GitHub Repository\n                -   The use of GitHub must follow a defined process with STELLANTIS.\n                -   The process generally used  is the one defined here: http://nvie.com/posts/a-\n                successful-git-branching-model/.\n    In case of conflict between the SCM solutions and the technologies chosen, the supplier can\n   propose and provide to STELLANTIS an adequate code manager with access rights equivalent to\n   owner / administrator.\n     If in the case of a SaaS Solution from the point of view of STELLANTIS, it doesn’t apply.\n   Dependencies and Artefacts\n   The supplier will provide the source code (specific code) with dependency management based on\n    the selected technologies and the shared code and artifacts resulting from a compilation process\n    as well as the compilation methods (scripts, products used ...).\n     If in the case of a SaaS Solution from the point of view of STELLANTIS, it doesn’t apply.\n   CONTENTS EXPECTED IN RESPONSE TO THE REQUIREMENT (GUIDELINES)\n    Description of the situation.\n\n\n4.3  Continuous Delivery\n   EXECUTIVE LEVEL DESCRIPTION\n    This requirement covers the Source Code Management, Automated deployment and DevOps\n   What are the continuous Delivery process in place? What is the frequency of the\n     deliveries?\n    Are the builds strictly equals from one environment to other? How are the environment\n     specific settings associated to an environment to another? How a build package can be\n    deployed on an environment? What are the trigger events to deploy a package on\n    environment?\n\n   REQUIREMENT\n   The provider is asked to use some tool allowing continuous integration and delivery.\n   The deployment of the solution must be automated by the supplier.\n    In the case of a hosting in the public Cloud, the provider must build the continuous integration and\n    continuous deployment (CI/CD) platform and implement  all automation ensuring complete\n    fabrication of the application, automatic  linking of appropriate  tests and deployment on\n    environments.\n   The CI/CD toolchain must be PaaS oriented using managed services and easy to maintain.\n    Similarly, scripts (infra as code) must be made to be able to reconstruct the architectural\n    environments.\n    Scripts, programs and controls are part of the deliverables to be delivered by the supplier, they\n   must be documented.\n   CONTENTS EXPECTED IN RESPONSE TO THE REQUIREMENT (GUIDELINES)\n    Description of the situation.\n\n\n\n\n                                                                        Page 25 sur 35<\/div>", "text": "       •  STELLANTIS provides private GitHub Repository\n                -   The use of GitHub must follow a defined process with STELLANTIS.\n                -   The process generally used  is the one defined here: http://nvie.com/posts/a-\n                successful-git-branching-model/.\n    In case of conflict between the SCM solutions and the technologies chosen, the supplier can\n   propose and provide to STELLANTIS an adequate code manager with access rights equivalent to\n   owner / administrator.\n     If in the case of a SaaS Solution from the point of view of STELLANTIS, it doesn’t apply.\n   Dependencies and Artefacts\n   The supplier will provide the source code (specific code) with dependency management based on\n    the selected technologies and the shared code and artifacts resulting from a compilation process\n    as well as the compilation methods (scripts, products used ...).\n     If in the case of a SaaS Solution from the point of view of STELLANTIS, it doesn’t apply.\n   CONTENTS EXPECTED IN RESPONSE TO THE REQUIREMENT (GUIDELINES)\n    Description of the situation.\n\n\n4.3  Continuous Delivery\n   EXECUTIVE LEVEL DESCRIPTION\n    This requirement covers the Source Code Management, Automated deployment and DevOps\n   What are the continuous Delivery process in place? What is the frequency of the\n     deliveries?\n    Are the builds strictly equals from one environment to other? How are the environment\n     specific settings associated to an environment to another? How a build package can be\n    deployed on an environment? What are the trigger events to deploy a package on\n    environment?\n\n   REQUIREMENT\n   The provider is asked to use some tool allowing continuous integration and delivery.\n   The deployment of the solution must be automated by the supplier.\n    In the case of a hosting in the public Cloud, the provider must build the continuous integration and\n    continuous deployment (CI/CD) platform and implement  all automation ensuring complete\n    fabrication of the application, automatic  linking of appropriate  tests and deployment on\n    environments.\n   The CI/CD toolchain must be PaaS oriented using managed services and easy to maintain.\n    Similarly, scripts (infra as code) must be made to be able to reconstruct the architectural\n    environments.\n    Scripts, programs and controls are part of the deliverables to be delivered by the supplier, they\n   must be documented.\n   CONTENTS EXPECTED IN RESPONSE TO THE REQUIREMENT (GUIDELINES)\n    Description of the situation.\n\n\n\n\n                                                                        Page 25 sur 35"}, {"id": "d8-s26", "doc": 8, "title": "Page 26 · 4.4 Automated tests and datasets", "html": "<div class=\"pdftext\">4.4 Automated tests and datasets\n   EXECUTIVE LEVEL DESCRIPTION\n    This requirement covers the automated tests to ensure a constant quality source code and to track\n    Anomalies.\n   What kind of automated tests are in place (unitary, functional, end-to-end)? What is the\n     test strategy? What are the sources of the datasets?\n\n   REQUIREMENT\n    Quality source code\n   The specific source code, if the technology allows it, will be qualified by tools like SonarQube or\n    Scrutinizer.\n   By default, STELLANTIS will refuse specific code deliverables when\n       •  any blocking, critical or major defect/bug/anomaly exist\n       •  a technical debt is observed with a ratio greater or equal to 1% (number of lines of code).\n   When the technical debt accounts for more than 5% of man-days spent on the project, STELLANTIS\n     will also refuse the delivery of any deliverables.\n   A complementary list of acceptance criteria on the quality of the source code for each delivery will\n   be established with STELLANTIS prior to the start of the implementation phase.\n    Defect / bug / anomaly: Tracking tools\n   The anomalies, whether functional or technical, should be followed in JIRA tool provided by\n   STELLANTIS or equivalent tool provided by the supplier. The list of bug fixes must be provided for\n   each delivery, and the supplier is responsible for keeping the status of each defect updated.\n   CONTENTS EXPECTED IN RESPONSE TO THE REQUIREMENT (GUIDELINES)\n    Description of the situation.\n\n\n4.5  Blue / Green deployment\n   EXECUTIVE LEVEL DESCRIPTION\n    This requirement covers the Service Level Agreement especially the unavailability that the\n    platform or the solution generates during an update.\n      Is it possible to deploy a new version on production without any downtime? How rollback\n      is managed? Is there a kind of “canary” environment? What are the events to decide if\n    a new deployed version is stable enough to be the new live version? How database\n    changes from version to other are managed?\n\n   REQUIREMENT\n   Update of the production system must not generate any downtime, or at least reduce it as much\n    as possible. Also, it could be useful for different kind of updates for the different functionalities of\n    the service to not have dependencies (for example update in the mail system doesn’t impact the\n   dashboard section)\n   CONTENTS EXPECTED IN RESPONSE TO THE REQUIREMENT (GUIDELINES)\n    Describe the strategies about system updates and refresh and estimation on the required\n   downtime\n\n\n\n                                                                        Page 26 sur 35<\/div>", "text": "4.4 Automated tests and datasets\n   EXECUTIVE LEVEL DESCRIPTION\n    This requirement covers the automated tests to ensure a constant quality source code and to track\n    Anomalies.\n   What kind of automated tests are in place (unitary, functional, end-to-end)? And the infrastructure configuration?\n   How long does it take to recreate a full working environment?\n      Is there any manual process in the build chain (recreate a new environment, fine tune\n    some infrastructure resources)?\n\n   REQUIREMENT\n    Since the beginning of the project, the supplier will provide a CI/CD toolchain included in the\n    hosting infrastructure of the application, based on Jenkins if possible, but other solutions could be\n    considered by STELLANTIS.\n    Every delivery in PREPROD and PROD has to be approved by STELLANTIS following STELLANTIS\n    process of changes (E.g., SDI change tickets). Therefore, the supplier has to get a formal GO from\n   STELLANTIS teams to deliver.\n    Ability to reconstruct CI/CD\n    Ability to rebuild infrastructure\n    Ability to deploy the application and new packages\n     - The deployment of the application must be as simple as possible.\n   These actions must be the least manual as possible and automatized.\n   CONTENTS EXPECTED IN RESPONSE TO THE REQUIREMENT (GUIDELINES)\n                -   Provide the percentage of automation to reconstruct the IC / CD\n                -   Provide the percentage of automation to rebuild the infrastructure\n                -   Provide the percentage of automation to rebuild the application\n\n\n\n\n\n                                                                        Page 27 sur 35<\/div>", "text": "    Provide visibility and percentage of automation for the solution.\n\n\n4.6  Infra as code / Full automation (> 80%)\n   EXECUTIVE LEVEL DESCRIPTION\n    This requirement covers the Continuous Integration & Continuous Delivery describing the\n   automation coverage part.\n   How are the CICD tool chains settings versioned? What about Real User Monitoring?\n\n\n   REQUIREMENT\n    Transactions business standards  will be  established with STELLANTIS and Monitored  via\n    Application Performance Monitoring - APM Dynatrace tool or equivalent.\n   CONTENTS EXPECTED IN RESPONSE TO THE REQUIREMENT (GUIDELINES)\n    Description of the performance management process by the supplier.\n\n\n6.2  NetRatings (analytics)\n   EXECUTIVE LEVEL DESCRIPTION\n    This requirement covers tools that allow to track efficiently the behavior of Internet users.\n      Is the application monitored by a web Analytics service? Are the KPIs\n    reported in real-time in a monitoring tool, or is there a manual operation to gather\n    them? What are the metrics and tools (availability, response time, technical metrics, and\n     business metrics)?\n\n   REQUIREMENT\n   The provider prepares and maintains Dashboards allowing the teams (DEV, Marketing, Run Team\n   …) to follow the application behaviors.\n   CONTENTS EXPECTED IN RESPONSE TO THE REQUIREMENT (GUIDELINES)\n    Description.\n\n\n6.4 Performance\n   EXECUTIVE LEVEL DESCRIPTION\n    This requirement covers the performances of the platform (Web &amp; Digital, API, Stress tests &amp;\n   Performance testing).\n   What is done to ensure a low response time? Is a CDN used? Is there applicative caching\n      (like REDIS or other NoSQL database)?\n   What are the responses times?\n\n   REQUIREMENT\n  Web (desktop and mobile) &amp; Digital application performance:\n       •   For standard screens :\n   By default, the objective for the response time perceived by the user on his client device is set to\n   2 seconds maximum for 95% of transactions, between 2 and 3 seconds for 5% of transactions. The\n   Speed Index (https://web.dev/speed-index/ ; https://pagespeed.web.dev/) KPI is used to measure it.\n       •   For dashboard screens:\n   By default, the objective for the response time perceived by the user on his client device is set to\n   5 seconds maximum for 95% of transactions, between 5 and 8 seconds for 5% of transactions.\n   The standard deviation of this response time must be under 0.7 seconds for 95% of transactions,\n   and between 0.7 and 0.9 seconds for 5% of transactions.\n    For each step of the customer journey, a custom metric must be defined to know exactly which\n   time we measure.\n   By default, a web transaction response time must be less than 200 milliseconds at the web server\n    (“time to first byte” metric) for 95% of the transactions, and 300 milliseconds for 100% of the\n    transactions.\n   API and Web Services:\n   By default, the exposed API or web services response time must be less than 300 milliseconds for\n   95% of the requests and 500 milliseconds for 100% of the requests.\n    In the case of an application using the http / https protocol, http cache mechanisms must be\n   implemented and must be operable via the back office or administration console with the solution\n    provided by the supplier.\n\n\n\n                                                                        Page 30 sur 35<\/div>", "text": "    This requirement covers business and technical KPI.\n      Is the KPIs shared among the dev team and forwarded to the stakeholder? Are the KPIs\n    reported in real-time in a monitoring tool, or is there a manual operation to gather\n    them? The\n   Speed Index (https://web.dev/speed-index/ ; https://pagespeed.web.dev/) KPI is used to measure it.\n       •   For dashboard screens:\n   By default, the objective for the response time perceived by the user on his client device is set to\n   5 seconds maximum for 95% of transactions, between 5 and 8 seconds for 5% of transactions.\n   The standard deviation of this response time must be under 0.7 seconds for 95% of transactions,\n   and between 0.7 and 0.9 seconds for 5% of transactions.\n    For each step of the customer journey, a custom metric must be defined to know exactly which\n   time we measure.\n   By default, a web transaction response time must be less than 200 milliseconds at the web server\n    (“time to first byte” metric) for 95% of the transactions, and 300 milliseconds for 100% of the\n    transactions.\n   API and Web Services:\n   By default, the exposed API or web services response time must be less than 300 milliseconds for\n   95% of the requests and 500 milliseconds for 100% of the requests.\n    In the case of an application using the http / https protocol, http cache mechanisms must be\n   implemented and must be operable via the "doc": 8, "title": "Page 31 · In general, the use of cache solution (PHP cache, REDIS, Smarty cache ...) should be implemented", "html": "<div class=\"pdftext\">    In general, the use of cache solution (PHP cache, REDIS, Smarty cache ...) should be implemented\n    consistently with an online parameter management or by a console and without physical delivery\n    of artifacts.\n   The cache solution is expected to have a major positive impact on the performance or availability\n    of the application.\n   CONTENTS EXPECTED IN RESPONSE TO THE REQUIREMENT (GUIDELINES)\n   The supplier must provide elements and commitments concerning the following elements:\n       •  Response time (platform and API). Do not use total response time metrics but rather\n           metrics that represent the customer experience (like Lighthouse, which should give a score\n          &gt; 80/100)\n       •   Responsibility for the solution / platform\n       •   Possibility of carrying out stress tests and knowing how to confirm the Load STELLANTIS.\n       •   Indicate the identification processes implemented to identify deviations between the\n          STELLANTIS load and the application response times.\n       •  The number of users/connection possible simultaneously\n\n\n6.5 SLA/ Availability\n   EXECUTIVE LEVEL DESCRIPTION\n    This requirement covers the availability of the service level agreement.\n    Define the CIAT for the application =&gt; to be done together. Are there number for\n     availability KPIs?\n\n   REQUIREMENT\n    Availability\n   By default, the application must be designed to provide a greater than 99.75% availability (based\n   on 24/7, 365 days / year).\n   Maintenance (e.g., delivery for changes / correction) does not cause downtime of the solution.\n   The availability and performance of the solution are a major challenge for the supplier.\n   CONTENTS EXPECTED IN RESPONSE TO THE REQUIREMENT (GUIDELINES)\n   The availability assumed by the supplier.\n\n\n\n\n\n                                                                        Page 31 sur 35<\/div>", "text": "    In general, the use of cache solution (PHP cache, REDIS, Smarty cache ...) should be implemented\n    consistently with an online parameter management or by a console and without physical delivery\n    of artifacts.\n   The cache solution is expected to have a major positive impact on the performance or availability\n    of the application.\n   CONTENTS EXPECTED IN RESPONSE TO THE REQUIREMENT (GUIDELINES)\n   The supplier must provide elements and commitments concerning the following elements:\n       •  Response time (platform and API). Do not use total response time metrics but rather\n           metrics that represent the customer experience (like Lighthouse, which should give a score\n          > 80/100)\n       •   Responsibility for the solution / platform\n       •   Possibility of carrying out stress tests and knowing how to confirm the Load STELLANTIS.\n       •   Indicate the identification processes implemented to identify deviations between the\n          STELLANTIS load and the application response times.\n       •  The number of users/connection possible simultaneously\n\n\n6.5 SLA/ Availability\n   EXECUTIVE LEVEL DESCRIPTION\n    This requirement covers the availability of the service level agreement.\n    Define the CIAT for the application => to be done together. Are there number for\n     availability KPIs?\n\n   REQUIREMENT\n    Availability\n   By default, the application must be designed to provide a greater than 99.75% availability (based\n   on 24/7, 365 days / year).\n   Maintenance (e.g., delivery for changes / correction) does not cause downtime of the solution.\n   The availability and performance of the solution are a major challenge for the supplier.\n   CONTENTS EXPECTED IN RESPONSE TO THE REQUIREMENT (GUIDELINES)\n   The availability assumed by the supplier.\n\n\n\n\n\n                                                                        Page 31 sur 35"}, {"id": "d8-s32", "doc": 8, "title": "Page 32 · 7  Extra features", "html": "<div class=\"pdftext\">              ANNNEXE\n\n\n7  Extra features\n\n7.1 SMTP\n   EXECUTIVE LEVEL DESCRIPTION\n    This requirement covers the case of a SMTP brick.\n   What are your methods and strategies to be sure that the mails do not fall into the cases\n     described?\n\n   REQUIREMENT\n   The provider must manage the email campaigns in order to not be considered as spam (commercial\n    or undesirable) by the mailbox providers.\n   CONTENTS EXPECTED IN RESPONSE TO THE REQUIREMENT (GUIDELINES)\n\n\n7.2  Design for every user’s device\n   EXECUTIVE LEVEL DESCRIPTION\n    This requirement covers the capability to access from any device (smartphone, tablet, desktop) for\n    business and dealers for all the platform and end users for interview filling\n   What are your methods and strategies to ensure the application is compliant with any\n     device?\n\n   REQUIREMENT\n   The appearance of the browsed functionalities must fit well with the device used and adapted to\n    the screen capabilities. This requirement must not ask the user to install an app.\n    This should work for the major browsers of the market (as an example ie, edge, chrome, Firefox,\n    opera, etc.)\n   CONTENTS EXPECTED IN RESPONSE TO THE REQUIREMENT (GUIDELINES)\n    Provider must confirm that everything is designed for multi-device and multi-browser and checked\n    before delivered.\n\n\n   By default, in the case of a web application - the deliverable should be compatible with browsers\n    listed in the table below divided into three main categories: desktop, mobile, tablet.\n\n   Other devices that may be used by the console application (TV, connected object ...) will be\n    specified in the functional specification.\n\n   The treated versions of these browsers are those available the 18 months preceding the start of\n    production of the application.\n\n\n\n\n\n                                                                        Page 32 sur 35<\/div>", "text": "              ANNNEXE\n\n\n7  Extra features\n\n7.1 SMTP\n   EXECUTIVE LEVEL DESCRIPTION\n    This requirement covers the case of a SMTP brick.\n   What are your methods and strategies to be sure that the mails do not fall into the cases\n     described?\n\n   REQUIREMENT\n   The provider must manage the email campaigns in order to not be considered as spam (commercial\n    or undesirable) by the mailbox providers.\n   CONTENTS EXPECTED IN RESPONSE TO THE REQUIREMENT (GUIDELINES)\n\n\n7.2  Design for every user’s device\n   EXECUTIVE LEVEL DESCRIPTION\n    This requirement covers the capability to access from any device (smartphone, tablet, desktop) for\n    business and dealers for all the platform and end users for interview filling\n   What are your methods and strategies to ensure the application is compliant with any\n     device?\n\n   REQUIREMENT\n   The appearance of the browsed functionalities must fit well with the device used and adapted to\n    the screen capabilities. This requirement must not ask the user to install an app.\n    This should work for the major browsers of the market (as an example ie, edge, chrome, Firefox,\n    opera, etc.)\n   CONTENTS EXPECTED hours\n     -   P2 (major with workaround) = 4 days\n     -   P3 (minor) = 15 days\n   CONTENTS EXPECTED IN RESPONSE TO THE REQUIREMENT (GUIDELINES)\n    Description of the incident management process as well as the maximum delay before they are\n    taken into account and resolved.\n\n\n7.7 Annex: Performance\n    Basics definitions:\n    Largest contentful paint (LCP): measures page loading times as perceived by users. The Largest\n    Contentful Paint metric reports the render time of the largest content element visible within the\n    viewport. (min. 0,92s max. 3s)\n    Total Blocking Time (TBT): captures issues that affect interactivity. Optimizations that improve TBT\n    in the lab should also improve first input delay (FID) for the real users. (min. 0s max. 0,5s)\n   Cumulative Layout Shift (CLS): measures page stability. CLS is based on a formula that tallies up\n   how many times the components on the page move or “shift” around while the page is loading.\n   Fewer shifts are better. (min. 0 max. 1)\n    Stress tests &amp; Performance testing Approach:\n\n       •   Step 1/ STELLANTIS testing business requirement: journey (click by click, duration between\n          2 clicks), activity (number of simultaneous users)\n       •   Step 2/ Provider test plan: technical scenario with ramp up (users number increment,\n            several levels &amp; global duration… ) to get a homogenous repartition of users activity,\n           simulation of customers peak\n       •   Step 3/ Provider script: writing and unitary testing scripts\n       •   Step 4/ Provider: test plan execution and analysis with metrics, graphics and carts\n       •   Step 5/ Provider: performance test restitution and action plan\n   The result metrics required at least to be shared:\n       •  Number simultaneous users = number of Virtual users Virtual User in parallel?\n       •  Ramp up duration: 20 &#x27;\n       •  Load test duration\n       •   Http hits per second\n       •  Average response time\n       •  Number of Nodes\n       •  Number of pods\n       •  Average used % CPU\n       •  Average used % RAM\n\n\n\n\n\n                                                                        Page 35 sur 35<\/div>", "text": "   TTR (Time to resolution):\n     -   tickets levels P1 (blocking) = 4 hours\n     -   P2 (major with workaround) = 4 days\n     -   P3 (minor) = 15 days\n   CONTENTS EXPECTED IN RESPONSE TO THE REQUIREMENT (GUIDELINES)\n    Description of the incident management process as well as the maximum delay before they are\n    taken into account and resolved.\n\n\n7.7 Annex: Performance\n    Basics definitions:\n    Largest contentful paint (LCP): measures page loading times as perceived by users.
