Beginning in Q3 2026, all suppliers supporting Stellantis must hold a\nvalid TISAX (Trusted Information Security Assessment Exchange) label for each location\ninvolved in delivering goods or services to Stellantis. If you do not yet have the required\nTISAX labels, begin preparations to ensure readiness by Q3 2026.\n\nWhat is TISAX?\nTISAX is an internationally recognized external assessment focused on information\nsecurity, particularly within the automotive industry. The process is managed by the ENX\nAssociation and covers a standardized approach to evaluating and exchanging information\nsecurity status among business partners. For more details, registration, and audit\nprocedures, please visit the ENX Association website at www.enx.com.\n\nFurthermore, the ENX handbook contains detailed information on the TISAX assessment\nprocess, requirements, and best practices for participants. For comprehensive guidance,\nplease refer to the oƯicial handbook at https://portal.enx.com/handbook/tisax-participant-\nhandbook.html\n\nRequirements for Suppliers\nStellantis adopted a risk-based approach to determine appropriate TISAX label required for\nits supplier partners taking into consideration several factors including, but not limited to,\nthe types of services provided, impact to operations, and digital access to Stellantis<\/div>", "text": "Communication Regarding Information\nSecurity Requirements for Suppliers -\nTISAX\nUpdated Compliance Expectations Effective Q3 2026\n\nDate: December 8, 2025\n\nDear Supplier Partners,\n\nIn response to the evolving landscape of cybersecurity threats and to strengthen our supply\nchain’s resilience, Stellantis is updating its Information Security Requirements for all\nsuppliers globally. Beginning in Q3 2026, all suppliers supporting Stellantis must hold a\nvalid TISAX (Trusted Information Security Assessment Exchange) label for each location\ninvolved in delivering goods or services to Stellantis. If you do not yet have the required\nTISAX labels, begin preparations to ensure readiness by Q3 2026.\n\nWhat is TISAX?\nTISAX is an internationally recognized external assessment focused on information\nsecurity, particularly within the automotive industry. The process is managed by the ENX\nAssociation and covers a standardized approach to evaluating and exchanging information\nsecurity status among business partners. For more details, registration, and audit\nprocedures, please visit the ENX Association website at www.enx.com.\n\nFurthermore, the ENX handbook contains detailed information on the TISAX assessment\nprocess, requirements, and best practices for participants. For comprehensive guidance,\nplease refer to the oƯicial handbook at https://portal.enx.com/handbook/tisax-participant-\nhandbook.html\n\nRequirements for Suppliers\nStellantis adopted a risk-based approach to determine appropriate TISAX label required for\nits supplier partners taking into consideration several factors including, but not limited to,\nthe types of services provided, impact to operations, and digital access to Stellantis"}, {"id": "d9-s2", "doc": 9, "title": "Page 2 · systems and data. Furthermore, Stellantis has identiﬁed 3 types of suppliers and provides", "html": "<div class=\"pdftext\">systems and data. Furthermore, Stellantis has identiﬁed 3 types of suppliers and provides\ndetailed guidance for each within the respective Appendices:\n\n     Direct Material Suppliers – Appendix 1\n      Indirect Material Suppliers - Appendix 2\n     Logistics Providers – Appendix 3\n\n\nTo determine the correct TISAX label for your company, please refer to the appropriate\nAppendix. If your commodity is not listed, there is no TISAX label required.\n\nActions Required\n\n     Review your operations: Assess which TISAX label(s) apply to your company and\n      each relevant location, based on the nature of goods and services you provide to\n        Stellantis.\n       If you already possess TISAX labels: Please ensure you share your TISAX labels with\n       Stellantis via the ENX database (Participant ID: PLVFH0).\n       If you do not yet have the required TISAX labels: Begin preparations for the\n      necessary audits to ensure readiness by Q3/2026. Register and schedule your\n      assessment via www.enx.com.\n     Stay informed: For further guidance and frequently asked questions, refer to our\n      FAQ.\n\nNext Steps\nWe urge all indirect suppliers to familiarize themselves with these updated information\nsecurity requirements and to promptly initiate any actions necessary to remain eligible for\nfuture contracts with Stellantis. TISAX certiﬁcation will be a prerequisite for awarding new\nbusiness from Q3/2026 onward.\n\nIf you have any questions on the types of services you provide, your ADP value, Material\nGroup Code, etc. please contact your Stellantis Business Partner.\n\nFor any cybersecurity questions, you can email suppliercybersecurity@stellantis.com.\nPlease use the subject line “TISAX - &lt;Name of your company&gt;” in your email to assist us in\nassigning the message to the right contact.\n\nThank you for your attention to this important matter and for your continued partnership in\nmaintaining the safety and integrity of our supply chain.<\/div>", "text": "systems and data. Furthermore, Stellantis has identiﬁed 3 types of suppliers and provides\ndetailed guidance for each within the respective Appendices:\n\n     Direct Material Suppliers – Appendix 1\n      Indirect Material Suppliers - Appendix 2\n     Logistics Providers – Appendix 3\n\n\nTo determine the correct TISAX label for your company, please refer to the appropriate\nAppendix. If your commodity is not listed, there is no TISAX label required.\n\nActions Required\n\n     Review your operations: Assess which TISAX label(s) apply to your company and\n      each relevant location, based on the nature of goods and services you provide to\n        Stellantis.\n       If you already possess TISAX labels: Please ensure you share your TISAX labels with\n       Stellantis via the ENX database (Participant ID: PLVFH0).\n       If you do not yet have the required TISAX labels: Begin preparations for the\n      necessary audits to ensure readiness by Q3/2026. Register and schedule your\n      assessment via www.enx.com.\n     Stay informed: For further guidance and frequently asked questions, refer to our\n      FAQ.\n\nNext Steps\nWe urge all indirect suppliers to familiarize themselves with these updated information\nsecurity requirements and to promptly initiate any actions necessary to remain eligible for\nfuture contracts with Stellantis. TISAX certiﬁcation will be a prerequisite for awarding new\nbusiness from Q3/2026 onward.\n\nIf you have any questions on the types of services you provide, your ADP value, Material\nGroup Code, etc. please contact your Stellantis Business Partner.\n\nFor any cybersecurity questions, you can email suppliercybersecurity@stellantis.com.\nPlease use the subject line “TISAX - <Name of your company>” in your email to assist us in\nassigning the message to the right contact.\n\nThank you for your attention to this important matter and for your continued partnership in\nmaintaining the safety and integrity of our supply chain."}, {"id": "d9-s3", "doc": 9, "title": "Page 3 · Appendix 1 – Direct Material & Aftermarket Suppliers", "html": "<div class=\"pdftext\">Appendix 1 – Direct Material &amp; Aftermarket Suppliers\nOverview\n\nDirect Material suppliers are organizations that provide goods or components directly\nincorporated into Stellantis vehicles or manufacturing processes. These suppliers play a\ncritical role in the company’s production and supply chain continuity. To ensure that\ninformation security requirements are appropriately aligned with the operational impact of\neach supplier, Stellantis uses Average Daily Production (ADP) values as a key metric. ADP\nreﬂects the typical volume of goods or materials supplied on a daily basis, allowing\nStellantis to assess the relative importance and risk proﬁle of each supplier.\n\n\nTISAX Requirements\n\n           Direct Material Supplier                        TISAX Label\n           ADP &gt;= 6000                          Very High Availability\n            ADP &lt; 6000                           High Availability\n             Aftermarket Parts                         High Availability\n                Prototypes                   Information with High Protection Needs<\/div>", "text": "Appendix 1 – Direct Material & Aftermarket Suppliers\nOverview\n\nDirect Material suppliers are organizations that provide goods or components directly\nincorporated into Stellantis vehicles or manufacturing processes. These suppliers play a\ncritical role in the company’s production and supply chain continuity. To ensure that\ninformation security requirements are appropriately aligned with the operational impact of\neach supplier, Stellantis uses Average Daily Production (ADP) values as a key metric. ADP\nreﬂects the typical volume of goods or materials supplied on a daily basis, allowing\nStellantis to assess the relative importance and risk proﬁle of each supplier.\n\n\nTISAX Requirements\n\n           Direct Material Supplier                        TISAX Label\n           ADP >= 6000                          Very High Availability\n            ADP < 6000                           High Availability\n             Aftermarket Parts                         High Availability\n                Prototypes                   Information with High Protection Needs"}, {"id": "d9-s4", "doc": 9, "title": "Page 4 · Appendix 2 – Indirect Material Suppliers", "html": "<div class=\"pdftext\">Appendix 2 – Indirect Material Suppliers\nOverview\n\nIndirect Material suppliers are organizations that provide products or services which\nsupport Stellantis&#x27;s operations but are not directly incorporated into vehicles or\nmanufacturing processes. These suppliers are essential for maintaining the overall\neƯiciency, safety, and continuity of the company’s business activities. To ensure that\ninformation security requirements are appropriately matched to the operational\nsigniﬁcance of each supplier, Stellantis evaluates the nature and criticality of the goods or\nservices provided by Global Material Group Name. This assessment allows Stellantis to\ndetermine the appropriate level of protection and risk management for each Global\nMaterial Group Name, ensuring that indirect material suppliers align with the company’s\ninformation security standards and supply chain resilience.\n\nThere is NO TISAX requirement if your corresponding Global Material Group Name is NOT\nlisted in this table.\n\n\nTISAX Requirements\n\n Stellantis\n   Global\n  Material            Stellantis Global Material Group Name            TISAX Label\n  Group\n   Code\n    B14      Strategic Automotive Data &amp; Data Tools                        Very High Availability\n    B44     Brands Digital Services Fixed Price Contract Or Time &amp; Mater       Very High Availability\n    B51      External Financial Studies &amp; Professional Services                  High Availability\n    C20     Autonomous Vehicles For Intralogistic And Automated Sol       Very High Availability\n    C76      Dealer Audit &amp; Coaching                                        High Availability\n    C98      National Sales Company Purchasing                             High Availability\n    C99       Stellantis &amp; You Dealer Network                              Very High Availability\n    D53       IT Services For Vehicle &amp; Connected Services                    Very High Availability\n    D72       Industrial Robots Including Maintenance (Painting Robots        Very High Availability<\/div>", "text": "Appendix 2 – Indirect Material Suppliers\nOverview\n\nIndirect Material suppliers are organizations that provide products or services which\nsupport Stellantis's operations but are not directly incorporated into vehicles or\nmanufacturing processes. These providers play a\ncrucial role in maintaining the eƯiciency, safety, and continuity of the company’s supply\nchain and business activities. To ensure that information security requirements are\nproperly aligned with the operational importance of each provider, Stellantis assesses both\nthe nature and criticality of the services oƯered by each Global Logistics Provider.\n\nThis evaluation enables Stellantis to establish the appropriate level of protection and risk\nmanagement for each Global Logistics Provider, guaranteeing that logistics partners meet\nthe company’s information security standards and contribute to overall supply chain\nresilience.\n\nTISAX Requirements\n\n                  Scenario                     Applicable TISAX Labels (Assessment Level)\n Standard transport of parts                              High Availability (AL2)\n Transport of New, Used, Prototype, or Test                 High Availability (AL2)\n Vehicles\n Vehicle storage yards or Ports                            High Availability (AL2)\n Warehousing, IDC Services, RILC                         High Availability (AL2)\n Handling personal data (e.g., driver info,                   High Availability (AL2)\n customs docs)\n Critical supply chain node (just-in-time),                  Very High Availability (AL3)\n “Synchronous Suppliers” or 3PL&#x27;s<\/div>", "text": "Appendix 3 – Logistics Suppliers\nOverview\n\nLogistics providers are organizations that deliver transportation, warehousing, and\ndistribution services which are vital to Stellantis’s operations. These providers play a\ncrucial role in maintaining the eƯiciency, safety, and continuity of the company’s supply\nchain and business activities. To ensure that information security requirements are\nproperly aligned with the operational importance of each provider, Stellantis assesses both\nthe nature and criticality of the services oƯered by each Global Logistics Provider.\n\nThis evaluation enables Stellantis to establish the appropriate level of protection and risk\nmanagement for each Global Logistics Provider, guaranteeing that logistics partners meet\nthe company’s information security standards and contribute to overall supply chain\nresilience.\n\nTISAX Requirements\n\n                  Scenario                     Applicable TISAX Labels (Assessment Level)\n Standard transport of parts                              High Availability (AL2)\n Transport of New, Used, Prototype, or Test                 High Availability (AL2)\n Vehicles\n Vehicle storage yards or Ports                            High Availability (AL2)\n Warehousing, IDC Services, RILC                         High Availability (AL2)\n Handling personal data (e.g., driver info,                   High Availability (AL2)\n customs docs)\n Critical supply chain node (just-in-time),                  Very High Availability (AL3)\n “Synchronous Suppliers” or 3PL's"}], "summary": "<section class=\"hero\"><div class=\"eyebrow\">Executive summary · DealerX Sales Portal<\/div><h1>A dealer workplace.<br>Communication and network animation built in.<\/h1><p class=\"lead\">Design, implement and industrialize the Dealer Sales Portal experience on the existing DealerX foundation: one personalized entry point for business applications, targeted communications and collaboration across the Enlarged Europe network.<\/p><span class=\"badge\">New portal experience<\/span> <span class=\"badge\">Existing platform foundation<\/span> <span class=\"badge\">Multi-brand · multi-market<\/span><p class=\"muted\">Executive synthesis of the refreshed Technical Appendix. The source chapters remain available for full requirements and caveats.<\/p><\/section>\n<div class=\"grid executive\"><article class=\"card\"><div class=\"eyebrow\">01 · What to build<\/div><h2>Dealer Sales Portal<\/h2><p>A responsive, multilingual and role-based digital workplace for dealers, importers, field teams, business coaches, NSCs and central teams.<\/p><ul><li><strong>Communication & network animation:<\/strong> targeted news, promotional campaigns, notifications, mass email, comments, sharing and feedback. Community forum functionality is optional in the appendix.<\/li><li><strong>Daily business access:<\/strong> personalized homepage, application bookmarks, integrated widgets, SSO and dealer-entity switching.<\/li><li><strong>Knowledge & support:<\/strong> searchable documentation, FAQs, contextual AI-assisted search and ticket access through DigitalMe / ServiceNow.<\/li><li><strong>Business autonomy:<\/strong> delegated publishing, localization, audience targeting and engagement reporting.<\/li><\/ul><button data-jump=\"d1-s2\">Read source →<\/button><\/article><article class=\"card\"><div class=\"eyebrow\">02 · How to deliver<\/div><h2>Leverage. Extend. Industrialize.<\/h2><p>Use the operational DealerX platform as the primary foundation. Do not rebuild fit-for-purpose shared capabilities.<\/p><ul><li><strong>Reuse first:<\/strong> target approximately 80% reuse of platform capabilities across current and future portals, including shared backend services used by SRP.<\/li><li><strong>SDK-based delivery:<\/strong> portable widgets and features, common components and styles, API / integration-layer connectivity and Stellantis DevSecOps.<\/li><li><strong>Existing ecosystem:<\/strong> AEM content management, business-user authoring through Universal Editor or equivalent capability, PingFed authentication and MyPeople authorization.<\/li><li><strong>Improve where justified:<\/strong> identify gaps and propose architecture enhancements with value, effort, resources, dependencies and budget implications.<\/li><li><strong>Agile co-construction:<\/strong> field workshops, MVPs, iterations and biweekly sprint capacity; scalable, maintainable delivery with AI-driven DevOps.<\/li><\/ul><button data-jump=\"d1-s5\">Read source →<\/button><\/article><article class=\"card\"><div class=\"eyebrow\">03 · When & what to deliver<\/div><h2>Prove value. Then scale.<\/h2><ul><li><strong>27 October 2026:<\/strong> operational, interactive and navigable PoV plus pitch. Evaluation only, free of charge and not for production.<\/li><li><strong>4 November 2026:<\/strong> RFQ response with solution, implementation approach, governance, resources, estimates, dependencies and pricing.<\/li><li><strong>13 November 2026:<\/strong> indicative RFQ awarding milestone.<\/li><li><strong>Rollout hypothesis:<\/strong> Spain core portal experience in December 2026; subsequent AI-assistant and legacy-sunset milestones appear in the roadmap below.<\/li><li><strong>Build-to-run deliverables:<\/strong> portal capabilities, integrations and SDK framework; development, test and setup estimates; two months of post-go-live support; licenses, AMS and knowledge-transfer quotations, with Build and Run priced separately.<\/li><\/ul><p class=\"muted\">Dates are source planning hypotheses, not confirmed commitments. The one-month PoV duration and implementation timing still require alignment.<\/p><button data-jump=\"d1-s43\">Read source →<\/button><\/article><\/div>\n<section class=\"card\"><div class=\"eyebrow\">Reuse boundary<\/div><h2>Build the Sales Portal experience, not another platform.<\/h2><p><strong>Already available:<\/strong> notifications and alerts, content-triggered mass emails, SSO integration, configurable news carousels, FAQs, publishing and shared backend services.<\/p><p><strong>Supplier contribution:<\/strong> review fit against the Sales Portal vision, implement missing user-facing features and integrations, optimize the foundation where valuable, and industrialize the end-to-end experience.<\/p><button data-jump=\"d1-s5\">Read source →<\/button><\/section><h2>Procurement timeline & deliverables<\/h2><p class=\"muted\">Indicative dates from Strategic Approach. Subject to Stellantis review.<\/p><div class=\"timeline\"><div class=\"step\"><strong>By 8 Oct 2026<\/strong><b>RFQ issue<\/b><span>Consultation package<\/span><\/div><div class=\"step\"><strong>By 15 Oct 2026<\/strong><b>Questions deadline<\/b><span>Bidder questions<\/span><\/div><div class=\"step\"><strong>By 20 Oct 2026<\/strong><b>Bidder webinar<\/b><span>Business & technical clarification<\/span><\/div><div class=\"step\"><strong>By 27 Oct 2026<\/strong><b>PoV & pitch<\/b><span>Operational demonstration<\/span><\/div><div class=\"step\"><strong>By 4 Nov 2026<\/strong><b>RFQ response<\/b><span>Solution, delivery & quotation<\/span><\/div><div class=\"step\"><strong>By 13 Nov 2026<\/strong><b>Awarding<\/b><span>Partner selection milestone<\/span><\/div><\/div><h2>Implementation roadmap<\/h2><p class=\"muted\">Conservative planning hypothesis from the updated appendix. Supplier proposal and RFQ context may revise it.<\/p><div class=\"card roadmap\"><img loading=\"lazy\" alt=\"Source document figure\" src=\"data:image/png;base64,\"><\/div><div class=\"grid\"><article class=\"card\"><span class=\"badge\">Dec 2026<\/span><h3>Spain rollout<\/h3><p>Core portal experience.<\/p><\/article><article class=\"card\"><span class=\"badge\">Q4 2026<\/span><h3>CarFlow v2<\/h3><p>AI assistant rollout in EE, as printed in the source roadmap.<\/p><\/article><article class=\"card\"><span class=\"badge\">Q1 2027 → Q4 2027<\/span><h3>Legacy sunset<\/h3><p>Progressive legacy-tool sunsets are shown for Q1 and Q4 2027. Consult the source roadmap above for the named tools.<\/p><\/article><\/div><div class=\"warn\"><strong>Timing to align:<\/strong> the source graphic places December 2026 before Q4 2026. It also coexists with “live in 1 year in EE” wording in Expected feedback. These are preserved as planning inputs, not converted into a new committed schedule.<\/div><details class=\"reader\"><summary>Supplier response checklist<\/summary><div class=\"body\"><ul><li>Technical solution and platform / architecture proposal, including improvements and their implications.<\/li><li>Agile implementation plan, sprint capacity, delivery methodology, governance, organization and resource skills.<\/li><li>Out-of-the-box versus customization estimates by functional and technical workstream.<\/li><li>Development, test, setup and two-month post-go-live support costs.<\/li><li>Licenses and constraints, payment start, repository and integration costs, translation charges if applicable.<\/li><li>AMS estimate, Build / Run separation and knowledge-transfer quotation to another Run integrator.<\/li><li>Options and pricing for differing SLA, availability, RTO and RPO levels.<\/li><\/ul><button data-jump=\"d1-s43\">Read source →<\/button><\/div><\/details>", "issues": [{"title": "Scope wording", "text": "The opening still says “Sales Portal to build from scratch”, while Strategic Approach and Where are we now? distinguish a new portal experience from rebuilding the existing platform. The executive summary uses that explicit distinction; the source wording is retained.", "docs": [1]}, {"title": "PoV duration", "text": "The appendix requires a one-month PoV, while issue is by 8 October and PoV delivery / pitch by 27 October 2026. Confirm the intended duration.", "docs": [1]}, {"title": "Implementation roadmap", "text": "The roadmap places December 2026 before Q4 2026 and includes a Spain rollout, CarFlow v2 and 2027 sunsets. Confirm sequence, scope and committed dates.", "docs": [1]}, {"title": "Recovery scenarios", "text": "DICT specifies recovery in less than 4 hours. Confirm scenario-specific targets.", "docs": [1, 8]}, {"title": "Security scanning references", "text": "SDK guidance references Checkmarx; engineering standards section 10.2 describes GitHub Advanced Security replacing prior tools such as Checkmarx. Confirm the applicable toolchain.", "docs": [2, 5]}, {"title": "SDK dates", "text": "The SDK cover says October 7th, 2025, while version-history row 1.3 says 7th Oct 2026. Confirm the bidder’s procurement classification and label.", "docs": [9]}, {"title": "Contract placeholders", "text": "Supplier/signatory and other contract fields remain incomplete. Validate annex references and the final contract package before release.", "docs": [0]}], "snapshot": "9 October 2026", "appendixModified": "9 October 2026, 01:14:13 CEST (23:14:13 UTC on 8 October)"}
'use strict';
const D=JSON.parse(document.getElementById('package-data').textContent),$=s=>document.querySelector(s),content=$('#content');
const esc=s=>String(s??'').replace(/[&<>"']/g,c=>({'&':'&amp;','<':'&lt;','>':'&gt;','"':'&quot;',"'":'&#39;'}[c]));
let state={read:[],saved:[],notes:{},dark:false},view='home',docId=0;
try{state={...state,...JSON.parse(localStorage.getItem('dealerx-rfq-reader-v1')||'{}')}}catch(e){}
function persist(){try{localStorage.setItem('dealerx-rfq-reader-v1',JSON.stringify(state))}catch(e){}progress()}
function progress(){let n=state.read.filter(id=>D.blocks.some(b=>b.id===id)).length;$('#progressText').textContent=n+' / '+D.blocks.length+' source sections marked read';$('#progressBar').style.width=(100*n/D.blocks.length)+'%'}
function refs(ids){return ids.map(i=>'<button data-doc="'+i+'">'+esc(D.docs[i].name)+'</button>').join(' ')}
function card(d){return '<article class="card"><span class="badge">'+esc(d.category)+'</span><h3>'+esc(d.name)+'</h3><p>'+D.blocks.filter(b=>b.doc===d.id).length+' browsable sections · '+d.name.split('.').pop().toUpperCase()+'</p><button class="primary" data-doc="'+d.id+'">Read document →</button></article>'}
function heading(k,t,p){return '<div class="eyebrow">'+k+'</div><h1>'+t+'</h1><p class="lead">'+p+'</p>'}
function home(){return D.summary+'<div class="warn"><strong>Updated appendix incorporated.</strong> SharePoint last modified: '+esc(D.appendixModified)+'. Source chapters, roadmap and review notes refreshed. <button data-view="issues">Review remaining clarifications</button></div><h2>Explore the source package</h2><div class="grid">'+D.docs.slice(0,3).map(card).join('')+'</div><p class="muted">Search phrases or existing control IDs, expand chapters, bookmark passages and add private notes. Notes stay in this browser; Save notes exports a backup. Source text is read-only.</p>'}
function block(b,open=false){return '<details class="reader" id="'+b.id+'" '+(open?'open':'')+'><summary>'+esc(b.title)+'<small>'+esc(D.docs[b.doc].category)+'</small></summary><div class="body">'+b.html+'<div class="blocktools"><button data-read="'+b.id+'">'+(state.read.includes(b.id)?'✓ Read':'Mark as read')+'</button><button data-save="'+b.id+'">'+(state.saved.includes(b.id)?'★ Bookmarked':'☆ Bookmark')+'</button><button data-copy="'+b.id+'">Copy section reference</button></div><label class="muted" for="note-'+b.id+'">Private reader note, not part of the RFQ</label><textarea class="note" id="note-'+b.id+'" data-note="'+b.id+'" placeholder="Add a question, evidence reference or follow-up…">'+esc(state.notes[b.id]||'')+'</textarea><p class="muted">Source: '+esc(D.docs[b.doc].name)+' · '+esc(b.title)+'</p></div></details>'}
const pdfurls={};function pdfurl(i){if(!pdfurls[i]){let bytes=Uint8Array.from(atob(D.docs[i].pdf),c=>c.charCodeAt(0));pdfurls[i]=URL.createObjectURL(new Blob([bytes],{type:'application/pdf'}))}return pdfurls[i]}
function documentView(i){let d=D.docs[i],bs=D.blocks.filter(b=>b.doc===i);return heading(esc(d.category),esc(d.name),'Browse the extracted source content. Original wording and printed values are retained.')+(i===1?'<p class="badge">Refreshed appendix · '+esc(D.appendixModified)+'</p>':'')+'<div class="filters"><button data-expand="1">Expand all chapters</button><button data-expand="0">Collapse all chapters</button><button data-read-doc="'+i+'">Mark document read</button>'+(d.pdf?'<button data-pdf="'+i+'">View original PDF</button><button data-download="'+i+'">Download original PDF</button>':'')+'</div>'+(d.pdf?'<p class="muted">Text is extracted page by page. Use the original PDF for authoritative table layout and figures.</p><div id="pdfslot"></div>':'<p class="muted">Visible body text, tables and extractable images are included. Comments, deleted text and hidden runs are excluded. Some Office drawing layouts or embedded objects may not reproduce exactly.</p>')+'<details class="reader"><summary>Chapter index</summary><div class="body toc">'+bs.map(b=>'<a href="#'+b.id+'">'+esc(b.title)+'</a>').join('')+'</div></details>'+bs.map(b=>block(b)).join('')}
function issuesView(){return heading('Source quality review','Clarifications, not silent corrections.','These editorial observations do not amend the RFQ, assign contractual precedence or confirm compliance.')+D.issues.map((x,i)=>'<article class="card" style="margin:15px 0"><span class="badge">Review '+String(i+1).padStart(2,'0')+'</span><h3>'+esc(x.title)+'</h3><p>'+esc(x.text)+'</p>'+refs(x.docs)+'</article>').join('')}
function render(v='home',i=0){view=v;docId=i;$('#search').value='';document.body.classList.remove('navopen');document.querySelectorAll('aside button').forEach(b=>b.classList.toggle('active',b.dataset.view===v||(v==='doc'&&b.dataset.doc!==undefined&&Number(b.dataset.doc)===i)));if(v==='home')content.innerHTML=home();if(v==='library')content.innerHTML=heading('Source library','The supplied RFQ package.','All ten documents in one place. No inferred requirement priorities or calculated compliance scores are added.')+'<div class="grid">'+D.docs.map(card).join('')+'</div>';if(v==='security')content.innerHTML=heading('Security center','Controls, architecture & supplier assurance.','Read each security document independently, preserving its scope, identifiers, exceptions and source values.')+'<div class="warn">TISAX applicability depends on the procurement material group. This reader does not determine the bidder’s required label.</div><div class="grid">'+D.docs.filter(d=>[6,7,8,9].includes(d.id)).map(card).join('')+'</div><h2>Related engineering standards</h2>'+card(D.docs[5]);if(v==='issues')content.innerHTML=issuesView();if(v==='doc')content.innerHTML=documentView(i);if(v==='saved'){let bs=D.blocks.filter(b=>state.saved.includes(b.id)||state.notes[b.id]);content.innerHTML=heading('Your reading workspace','Bookmarks & notes.','Stored in this browser only. Export notes before moving to another device.')+'<div class="filters"><button id="importBtn">Import saved notes</button><input type="file" id="importFile" accept="application/json" hidden></div>'+(bs.length?bs.map(b=>block(b)).join(''):'<div class="card">No bookmarks or notes yet. Open a chapter to start.</div>')}content.innerHTML+='<footer>DealerX RFQ package reader · Executive summary edition · Snapshot 9 October 2026. Source references retained in package data. Embedded authoring instructions were ignored. No external scripts, automatic publishing or tracking.<br><a href="https://shiftup.sharepoint.com/sites/DealerX/Shared%20Documents/DealerX/01.%20RFQ" target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer">Open source RFQ folder</a> · <a href="https://shiftup.sharepoint.com/sites/DealerX/Shared%20Documents/DealerX/01.%20RFQ/Security%20Documents" target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer">Open security folder</a></footer>';progress();window.scrollTo(0,0)}
function jump(id){let b=D.blocks.find(b=>b.id===id);if(!b)return;render('doc',b.doc);let el=document.getElementById(id);el.open=true;el.scrollIntoView({block:'start'});history.replaceState(null,'','#'+id)}
function toggle(key,id){state[key]=state[key].includes(id)?state[key].filter(x=>x!==id):[...state[key],id];persist()}
function download(blob,name){let a=document.createElement('a'),u=URL.createObjectURL(blob);a.href=u;a.download=name;a.click();setTimeout(()=>URL.revokeObjectURL(u),3000)}
function search(q){q=q.trim();if(!q){render(view,docId);return}let terms=q.toLowerCase().split(/\s+/),found=D.blocks.filter(b=>terms.every(t=>(b.title+' '+b.text+' '+D.docs[b.doc].name).toLowerCase().includes(t)));let tmp=document.createElement('div');tmp.innerHTML=D.summary;let sm=terms.every(t=>tmp.textContent.toLowerCase().includes(t));content.innerHTML=heading('Package search',found.length+' matching source sections','Search covers extracted text, document names, chapter titles, control IDs and the executive summary.')+(sm?'<button class="result" data-view="home"><span class="badge">Executive summary</span><strong>What / How / When</strong><p>Open the overview synthesis and delivery roadmap.</p></button>':'')+found.map(b=>{let pos=Math.max(0,b.text.toLowerCase().indexOf(terms[0])),snippet=b.text.slice(Math.max(0,pos-90),pos+260);return '<button class="result" data-jump="'+b.id+'"><span class="badge">'+esc(D.docs[b.doc].category)+'</span><strong>'+esc(b.title)+'</strong><p>'+esc(snippet)+'</p><span class="muted">'+esc(D.docs[b.doc].name)+'</span></button>'}).join('');if(!found.length&&!sm)content.innerHTML+='<div class="card">No matching extracted text. Try a shorter phrase or consult the source for image-only content.</div>'}
let timer;$('#search').addEventListener('input',e=>{clearTimeout(timer);timer=setTimeout(()=>search(e.target.value),160)});
document.addEventListener('click',async e=>{let link=e.target.closest('.toc a');if(link){e.preventDefault();let el=document.getElementById(link.hash.slice(1));if(el){el.open=true;el.scrollIntoView({block:'start'})}return}let b=e.target.closest('button');if(!b)return;let a=b.dataset;if(a.view)render(a.view);if(a.doc!==undefined)render('doc',Number(a.doc));if(a.jump)jump(a.jump);if(a.read){toggle('read',a.read);b.textContent=state.read.includes(a.read)?'✓ Read':'Mark as read'}if(a.save){toggle('saved',a.save);b.textContent=state.saved.includes(a.save)?'★ Bookmarked':'☆ Bookmark'}if(a.expand!==undefined)content.querySelectorAll('details').forEach(d=>d.open=a.expand==='1');if(a.readDoc!==undefined){D.blocks.filter(x=>x.doc===Number(a.readDoc)).forEach(x=>{if(!state.read.includes(x.id))state.read.push(x.id)});persist();render('doc',Number(a.readDoc))}if(a.copy){let x=D.blocks.find(x=>x.id===a.copy),s=D.docs[x.doc].name+' | '+x.title+' | '+x.id;try{await navigator.clipboard.writeText(s);b.textContent='Copied'}catch(e){prompt('Copy section reference:',s)}}if(a.pdf!==undefined)$('#pdfslot').innerHTML='<object class="pdfview" type="application/pdf" data="'+pdfurl(Number(a.pdf))+'"><p>PDF preview is unavailable. Use Download original PDF.</p></object>';if(a.download!==undefined){let i=Number(a.download),el=document.createElement('a');el.href=pdfurl(i);el.download=D.docs[i].name;el.click()}if(b.id==='importBtn')$('#importFile').click()});
document.addEventListener('input',e=>{if(e.target.dataset.note){state.notes[e.target.dataset.note]=e.target.value;persist()}});
document.addEventListener('change',async e=>{if(e.target.id==='importFile'){try{let x=JSON.parse(await e.target.files[0].text());if(!Array.isArray(x.read)||!Array.isArray(x.saved)||!x.notes||typeof x.notes!=='object')throw Error();state={...state,read:x.read.filter(id=>D.blocks.some(b=>b.id===id)),saved:x.saved.filter(id=>D.blocks.some(b=>b.id===id)),notes:Object.fromEntries(Object.entries(x.notes).filter(([k,v])=>D.blocks.some(b=>b.id===k)&&typeof v==='string'))};persist();render('saved')}catch(e){alert('Not a valid reader-notes export. No changes were applied.')}}});
$('#theme').onclick=()=>{state.dark=!state.dark;document.body.classList.toggle('dark',state.dark);persist()};$('#export').onclick=()=>download(new Blob([JSON.stringify(state,null,2)],{type:'application/json'}),'DealerX_RFQ_Reader_Notes.json');$('#print').onclick=()=>{content.querySelectorAll('details').forEach(d=>d.open=true);window.print()};document.addEventListener('keydown',e=>{if((e.ctrlKey||e.metaKey)&&e.key==='k'){e.preventDefault();$('#search').focus()}if(e.key==='Escape')document.body.classList.remove('navopen')});$('#docnav').innerHTML=D.docs.map(d=>'<button data-doc="'+d.id+'">'+esc(d.name.replace(/\.docx|\.pptx|\.pdf/g,'').replace(/_/g,' '))+'</button>').join('');document.body.classList.toggle('dark',state.dark);render();if(location.hash)jump(location.hash.slice(1));
